2.5. Data Division
2.5.1. WorkingΓÇôStorage Section
         The WorkingΓÇôStorage Section is composed of the section header, followed by data
         description entries for noncontiguous data items and/or record description entries. Each
         WorkingΓÇôStorage Section record name and noncontiguous item name must be unique
         since it cannot be qualified. Subordinate data-names need not be unique if they can be
         made unique by qualification.

2.5.1.1. Noncontiguous WorkingΓÇôStorage
         Items and constants in WorkingΓÇôStorage which bear no hierarchical relationship to one
         another need not be grouped into records, provided they do not need to be further
         subdivided. Instead, they are classified and defined as noncontiguous elementary items.
         Each of these items is defined in a separate data description entry which begins with the
         special level-number, 77.

         The following data clauses are required in each data description entry:
         a.   level-number 77
         b. data-name
         c.   the PICTURE clause or the USAGE IS INDEX, COMPUTATIONALΓÇô1,
              COMPUTATIONALΓÇô2, or LOCK clause.

         Other data description clauses are optional and can be used to complete the description
         of the item if necessary.

2.5.1.2. WorkingΓÇôStorage Records
         Data elements and constants in WorkingΓÇôStorage which bear a definite hierarchic
         relationship to one another must be grouped into records according to the rules for
         formation of record descriptions. All clauses which are used in record descriptions in the
         File Section can be used in record descriptions in the WorkingΓÇôStorage Section.

2.5.1.3. Initial Values
         The initial value of any item in the WorkingΓÇôStorage Section except an index data item is
         specified by using the VALUE clause with the data item. The initial value of any index
         data item is unpredictable.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                 2ΓÇô13
Nucleus




2.5.2. The Data DescriptionΓÇöComplete Entry Skeleton
2.5.2.1. Function
          A data description entry specifies the characteristics of a particular item of data.

2.5.2.2. General Format
          Format 1

          level-number         data-name-1
                               FILLER

          [ ; REDEFINES data-name-2 ]

            ;     PICTURE            IS character-string
                  PIC

                                      COMPUTATIONAL
                                      COMP
                                      DISPLAY
                                      COMPUTATIONAL-1
             [ USAGE IS ]
                                      COMP-2
                                      COMPUTATIONAL-2
                                      COMP-1
                                      DISP


           ; [ SIGN IS ]       LEADING        [ SEPARATE CHARACTER ]
                               TRAILING

            ;    SYNCHRONIZED                 LEFT
                 SYNC                         RIGHT

            ;    JUSTIFIED
                                          RIGHT
                 JUST

          [ ; BLANK WHEN ZERO ]

          [ ; VALUE IS literal ] .

          Format 2


            66 data-name-1; RENAMES data-name-2                        THROUGH   data-name-3      .
                                                                       THRU


          Format 3

           88 condition-name ;         VALUE IS            literal-1      THROUGH     literal-2
                                       VALUES ARE                         THRU


                 , literal-3           THROUGH        literal-4         ... .
                                       THRU




2ΓÇô14                                                                                        7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                         Nucleus




2.5.2.3. Syntax Rules
         1. In Level 1, the level-number in Format 1 may be any number from 01ΓÇô10 or 77.
            In Level 2, the level-number in Format 1 may be any number from 01ΓÇô49 or 77.
         2. The clauses may be written in any order with two exceptions: the dataΓÇônameΓÇô1 or
            FILLER clause must immediately follow the levelΓÇônumber; the REDEFINES clause,
            when used, must immediately follow the dataΓÇônameΓÇô1 clause.
         3. The PICTURE clause must be specified for every elementary item except an index
            data item, lock, or floating point data item, in which case use of this clause is
            prohibited.
         4. The words THRU and THROUGH are equivalent.

2.5.2.4. General Rules
         1. The clauses SYNCHRONIZED, PICTURE, JUSTIFIED, and BLANK WHEN ZERO must
            not be specified except for an elementary data item.
         2. Format 3 is used for each condition-name. Each condition-name requires a separate
            entry with level-number 88. Format 3 contains the name of the condition and the
            value, values, or range of values associated with the condition-name. The condition-
            name entries for a particular conditional variable must follow the entry describing the
            item with which the condition-name is associated. A condition-name can be
            associated with any data description entry which contains a level-number except the
            following:

             a.   Another condition-name.
             b. A level 66 item.
             c.   A group containing items with descriptions including JUSTIFIED,
                  SYNCHRONIZED, or USAGE (other than USAGE IS DISPLAY).
             d. An index data item (see 3.2.2).

2.5.3. The BLANK WHEN ZERO Clause
2.5.3.1. Function
         The BLANK WHEN ZERO clause permits the blanking of an item when its value is zero.

2.5.3.2. General Format
           BLANK WHEN ZERO


2.5.3.3. Syntax Rules
         1. The BLANK WHEN ZERO clause can be used only for an elementary item whose
            PICTURE is specified as numeric or numeric edited. (See 2.5.7.)




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                 2ΓÇô15
Nucleus




2.5.3.4. General Rules
          1. When the BLANK WHEN ZERO clause is used, the item will contain nothing but
             spaces if the value of the item is zero.
          2. When the BLANK WHEN ZERO clause is used for an item whose PICTURE is
             numeric, the category of the item is considered to be numeric edited.

          The following example shows the contents of variable data items following a move of
          zeros to the field:


                   PICTURE       BLANK WHEN ZERO        EDITED ITEM
                                    SPECIFIED?

                    $ZZZ9                No               $      0

                    $ZZZ9                Yes

                     ****                No                   ****

                     9(4)                No                   0000

                     9(4)                Yes



2.5.4. The DataΓÇôName or FILLER Clause
2.5.4.1. Function
          A data-name specifies the name of the data being described. The word FILLER
          specifies an item of the logical record that cannot be referred to explicitly.

2.5.4.2. General Format
             data-name
             FILLER

2.5.4.3. Syntax Rules
          In the File, WorkingΓÇôStorage, Common Storage, Communication, and Linkage Sections,
          a data-name or the key word FILLER must be the first word following the level-number
          in each data description entry.

2.5.4.4. General Rules
          The key word FILLER can name a data item in a record. Under no circumstances can a
          FILLER item be referred to explicitly. However, the key word FILLER may be used as a
          conditional variable because such use does not require explicit reference to the FILLER
          item, but to its value.




2ΓÇô16                                                                               7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                           Nucleus




         FILLER can be used in place of data-name to indicate a portion that is to contain no
         directly addressable data; for example, a space between two data items that are to be
         printed.

         As an example, if the following were written:
            01 EMPLOYEE-HISTORY.
                 02 EMPLOYEE-ID.
                     03 LIFE-NO PICTURE IS 9(6).
                     03 FILLER PICTURE IS X(6) VALUE IS SPACE.
                     03 NAME PICTURE IS A(24).

         A nonaddressable 6-character field would be inserted into the record between LIFEΓÇôNO
         and NAME and preset to contain spaces.

         The contents of that 6-character field can then be modified only by changing the
         contents of the group item EMPLOYEEΓÇôID or the record EMPLOYEEΓÇôHISTORY.

2.5.5. The JUSTIFIED Clause
2.5.5.1. Function
         The JUSTIFIED clause specifies nonstandard positioning of data within a receiving data
         item.

2.5.5.2. General Format
            JUSTIFIED
                             RIGHT
            JUST

2.5.5.3. Syntax Rules
         1. The JUSTIFIED clause can be specified only at the elementary item level.
         2. JUST is an abbreviation for JUSTIFIED.
         3. The JUSTIFIED clause cannot be specified for any data item described as numeric or
            for which editing is specified.

2.5.5.4. General Rules
         1. When a receiving data item is described with the JUSTIFIED clause and the sending
            data item is larger than the receiving data item, the leftmost characters are
            truncated. When the receiving data item is described with the JUSTIFIED clause
            and it is larger than the sending data item, the data is aligned at the rightmost
            character position in the data item with space fill for the leftmost character positions.
             For example, a field described as X(5) JUSTIFIED RIGHT would contain:
                 ΓêåΓêåABC if the literal ΓÇ£ABCΓÇ¥ were moved to it, or
                 BCDEF if the literal ΓÇ£ABCDEFΓÇ¥ were moved to it.
             A normally justified field would contain ABCΓêåΓêå and ABCDE if the same literals were
             moved to it.



7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                   2ΓÇô17
Nucleus




          2. When the JUSTIFIED clause is omitted, the standard rules for aligning data within an
             elementary item apply. (See 1.3.3.3.6.)

2.5.6. LevelΓÇôNumber
2.5.6.1. Function
          The level-number shows the hierarchy of data within a logical record. In addition, it is
          used to identify entries for working storage items, linkage items, condition-names, and
          the RENAMES clause.

2.5.6.2. General Format
            levelΓÇônumber

2.5.6.3. Syntax Rules
          1. A level-number is required as the first element in each data description entry.
          2. Data description entries subordinate to an FD, SD, or CD entry must have level-
             numbers with the values 01 through 10 in Level 1, and 0 ΓÇô 49, 66, or 88 in Level 2.
             (See 4.3.3 for FD, 7.3.2 for SD, and 13.2.2 for CD.)
          3. Data description entries subordinate to an RD entry must have levelΓÇônumbers with
             the value 01 through 10 in Level 1; 01ΓÇô 49 in Level 2. (See 8.2.4 for RD.)
          4. Data description entries in the WorkingΓÇôStorage Section, Common-Storage Section,
             and Linkage Section must have levelΓÇônumbers with the values 01ΓÇô10 or 77 in Level
             1, and 01ΓÇô 49, 66, 77, or 88 in Level 2.

2.5.6.4. General Rules
          1. The level-number 01 identifies the first entry in each record description or a report
             group. (See 8.2.5.)
          2. Special level-numbers have been assigned to certain entries where there is no real
             concept of level:
              a.   Level-number 77 is assigned to identify noncontiguous working storage data
                   items, noncontiguous linkage data items, and can be used only as described by
                   Format 1 of the data description skeleton. (See 2.5.2.)
              b. Level-number 66 is assigned to identify RENAMES entries and can be used only
                 as described in Format 2 of the data description skeleton. (See 2.5.2.)
              c.   Level-number 88 is assigned to entries which define condition-names associated
                   with a conditional variable and can be used only as described in Format 3 of the
                   data description skeleton. (See 2.5.2.)
          3. Multiple level 01 entries subordinate to any given level indicator, other than RD,
             represent implicit redefinitions of the same area.

                                                                                      Nucleus




2.5.7. The PICTURE Clause
2.5.7.1. Function
         The PICTURE clause describes the general characteristics and editing requirements of an
         elementary item.

2.5.7.2. General Format
            PICTURE
                          IS character-string
            PIC

2.5.7.3. Syntax Rules
         1. A PICTURE clause can be specified only at the elementary item level.
         2. A character-string consists of certain allowable combinations of characters in the
            COBOL character set used as symbols. The allowable combinations determine the
            category of the elementary item.
         3. The maximum number of characters allowed in the character-string is 30.
         4. The PICTURE clause must be specified for every elementary item except an index
            data item, lock, or floating-point data item, in which case use of this clause is
            prohibited.
         5. PIC is an abbreviation for PICTURE.
         6. The asterisk when used as the zero suppression symbol and the clause BLANK
            WHEN ZERO may not appear in the same entry.

2.5.7.4. General Rules
         1. There are five categories of data that can be described with a PICTURE clause:
            alphabetic, numeric, alphanumeric, alphanumeric edited, and numeric edited.
         2. To define an item as alphabetic:
            a.   Its PICTURE character-string can only contain the symbols ΓÇ£AΓÇ¥ or ΓÇ£BΓÇ¥; and
            b. Its contents when represented in standard data format must be any combination
               of the 26 letters of the Roman alphabet, 26 lowercase letters of the Roman
               alphabet, and the space from the COBOL character set.
            c.   An alphabetic item may have only DISPLAY usage associated with it.

                 AAA is an example of a valid alphabetic PICTURE string.
         3. To define an item as numeric:
            a.   Its PICTURE character-string can only contain the symbols ΓÇ£9ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£PΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥, and
                 ΓÇ£VΓÇ¥. The number of digit positions that can be described by the PICTURE
                 character-string must range from 1 to 18 inclusive; and




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                2ΓÇô19
Nucleus




               b. If unsigned, its contents when represented in standard data format must be a
                  combination of the Arabic numerals ΓÇ£0ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£1ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£2ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£3ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£4ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£5ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£6ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£7ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£8ΓÇ¥,
                  and ΓÇ£9ΓÇ¥; if signed, the item may also contain a ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥, or other representation
                  of an operational sign. (See 2.5.10.)
                    SPP9(4) and 9V99 are valid numeric PICTURE strings.
          4.   To define an item as exact binary:
               a.   When a PICTURE string contains at least one character ΓÇ£1ΓÇ¥, and no more than
                    one operational sign ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥ and no other symbols, it defines an exact binary data
                    item. Exact binary data items must not have associated USAGE clauses.
               b. The total allocated size of an exact binary field may not exceed 72 bits. If the
                  operational sign is present the first bit will be treated as a sign indicator with the
                  remainder of the field assumed to be the absolute value. If the value is negative,
                  the sign bit is 1 and the remainder of the field is 1ΓÇÖs complement of the
                  magnitude of the value. Thus, a PICTURE string S1(4) will have one sign bit and
                  3 magnitude bits.

                    S1(3) and 1111 are valid exact binary strings.
          5. To define an item as alphanumeric:
               a.   Its PICTURE character-string is restricted to certain combinations of the symbols
                    ΓÇ£AΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£XΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£9ΓÇ¥, and the item is treated as if the character-string contained all XΓÇÖs.
                    A PICTURE character-string which contains all AΓÇÖs or all 9ΓÇÖs does not define an
                    alphanumeric item; and
               b. Its contents when represented in standard data format are allowable characters
                  in the computerΓÇÖs character set.

               9XX9, AAXX, and A9(3) are all valid alphanumeric picture strings. Furthermore all
               three are equivalent and are treated as if X(4) had been written. An alphanumeric
               item has DISPLAY usage.
          6. To define an item as alphanumeric edited:
               a.   Its PICTURE character-string is restricted to certain combinations of the
                    following symbols: ΓÇ£AΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£XΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£9ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£BΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£0ΓÇ¥ , and ΓÇ£/ΓÇ¥ ; and
                    1) The character-string must contain at least one ΓÇ£BΓÇ¥ and at least one ΓÇ£XΓÇ¥ or at
                       least one ΓÇ£0ΓÇ¥ (zero) and at least one ΓÇ£XΓÇ¥ or at least one ΓÇ£/ΓÇ¥ (stroke) and at
                       least one ΓÇ£XΓÇ¥ ; or
                    2) The character-string must contain at least one ΓÇ£0ΓÇ¥ (zero) and at least one
                       ΓÇ£AΓÇ¥ or at least one ΓÇ£/ΓÇ¥ (stroke) and at least one ΓÇ£AΓÇ¥; and

               b. The contents when represented in standard data format are allowable characters
                  in the computerΓÇÖs character set.
                    An alphanumeric-edited PICTURE string must not cause more than 255
                    characters to be allocated.
                    XBBX and XB(15)X0(10) are valid alphanumeric-edited PICTURE strings. An
                    alphanumeric-edited field has DISPLAY usage.




2ΓÇô20                                                                                    7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                          Nucleus




         7. To define an item as numeric edited:
             a.   Its PICTURE characterΓÇôstring is restricted to certain combinations of the symbols
                  ΓÇ£BΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£/ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£PΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£VΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£ZΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£0ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£9ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£,ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£.ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£*ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£CRΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£DBΓÇ¥, and the

                  2) The character-string must contain at least one ΓÇ£0ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£BΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£/ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£ZΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£*ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥,
                     ΓÇ£,ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£.ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£CRΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£DBΓÇ¥, or currency symbol.
             b. The contents of the character positions of these symbols that are allowed to
                represent a digit in standard data format, must be one of the numerals.

             A numeric-edited item must have DISPLAY usage associated with it.

             $$$, $$9.99CR and ΓÇôZZZ are valid numeric-edited picture strings.

         8. The size of an elementary item, where size means the number of character positions
            occupied by the elementary item in standard data format, is determined by the
            number of allowable symbols that represent character positions. An integer which is
            enclosed in parentheses following the symbols ΓÇ£AΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£,ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£XΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£9ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£PΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£ZΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£*ΓÇ¥,
            ΓÇ£BΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£/ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£0ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥, or the currency symbol indicates the number of consecutive
            occurrences of the symbol. Note that the following symbols may appear only once

         The following examples illustrate the use of replication symbols:

                AAAAAA is equivalent to A(6)

                PPPP99999 is equivalent to P(4)9(5)

                S999V9999 is equivalent to S999V9(4)

         9. The functions of the symbols used to describe an elementary item are explained as
            follows:
             A
                  Each ΓÇ£AΓÇ¥ in the character-string represents a character position which can
                  contain only a letter of the alphabet or a space.
             B
                  Each ΓÇ£BΓÇ¥ in the character-string represents a character position into which the
                  space character will be inserted.

Nucleus




              P

                  the location of an assumed decimal point when the point is not within the
                  number that appears in the data item. The scaling position character ΓÇ£PΓÇ¥ is not
                  counted in the size of the data item. Scaling position characters are counted in
                  determining the maximum number of digit positions (18) in numeric-edited items
                  or numeric items. The scaling position character ΓÇ£PΓÇ¥ can appear only to the left
                  or right as a continuous string of PΓÇÖs within a PICTURE description; since the
                  scaling position character ΓÇ£PΓÇ¥ implies an assumed decimal point (to the left of
                  PΓÇÖs if PΓÇÖs are leftmost PICTURE characters and to the right if PΓÇÖs are rightmost
                  PICTURE characters), the assumed decimal point symbol ΓÇ£VΓÇ¥ is redundant as
                  either the leftmost or rightmost character within such a PICTURE description.
                  The character ΓÇ£PΓÇ¥ and the insertion character ΓÇ£.ΓÇ¥ (period) cannot both occur in
                  the same PICTURE character-string. If, in any operation involving conversion of
                  data from one form of internal representation to another, the data item being
                  converted is described with the PICTURE character ΓÇ£PΓÇ¥, each digit position
                  described by a ΓÇ£PΓÇ¥ is considered to contain the value zero, and the size of the
                  data item is considered to include the digit positions so described.
                  The following example:

                    02 FLDΓÇô2 PIC P999.
                    02 FLDΓÇô3 PIC 999PP.

                  would produce the following results:
                    FLDΓÇô1 would contain 23
                    FLDΓÇô2 would contain 012
                    FLDΓÇô3 would contain 123
                    FLDΓÇô4 would contain 12300.00143
                        (.00023 + .0012 + 12300)

          S
              The letter ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥ is used in a character-string to indicate the presence, but neither the
              representation nor, necessarily, the position, of an operational sign. It must be
              written as the leftmost character in the PICTURE. The ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥ is not counted in
              determining the size (in terms of standard data format characters) of the elementary
              item unless the entry is subject to a SIGN clause which specifies the optional
              SEPARATE CHARACTER phrase. (See 2.5.10.)
              The operational sign is used to indicate whether the value of a data item is positive
              or negative. When a data item is described with an operational sign, the contents of
              the data item can be signed positive, signed negative, or unsigned values. Unsigned
              values are treated conceptually as positive.

2.5.7.5. Editing Rules
         1. There are two general methods of performing editing in the PICTURE clause:
            insertion, and suppression and replacement. There are four types of insertion editing
            available:
              a.   Simple insertion
              b. Special insertion
              c.   Fixed insertion
              d. Floating insertion

              There are two types of suppression and replacement editing:
              a.   Zero suppression and replacement with spaces
              b. Zero suppression and replacement with asterisks




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                   2ΓÇô25
Nucleus




          2. The type of editing which may be performed upon an item is dependent upon the
             category to which the item belongs. The table that follows specifies which type of
             editing may be performed upon a given category.


                              Category                    Type of Editing

                      Alphabetic               Simple insertion ΓÇ£BΓÇ¥ only
                      Numeric                  None
                      Alphanumeric             None
                      Alphanumeric Edited      Simple insertion ΓÇ£0ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£BΓÇ¥ and ΓÇ£/ΓÇ¥
                      Numeric Edited           All, subject to rules in rule 3


          3. Floating insertion editing and editing by zero suppression and replacement are
             mutually exclusive in a PICTURE clause. Only one type of replacement may be used
             with zero suppression in a PICTURE clause.
          4. Simple Insertion Editing. The ΓÇ£,ΓÇ¥ (comma), ΓÇ£BΓÇ¥ (space), ΓÇ£0ΓÇ¥ (zero), and ΓÇ£/ΓÇ¥ (stroke)
             are used as the insertion characters. The insertion characters are counted in the size
             of the item and represent the position in the item into which the character will be
             inserted.
              The only circumstance when simple insertion symbols will not appear in a numericΓÇô
              edited field is when simple insertion characters are either embedded in or preceded
              on the left by suppression and replacement of floating insertion symbols. In this
              case the simple insertion characters are suppressed and replaced if the digit position
              to their left is suppressed and replaced.

              For example, a numeric-edited field defined as:
                 $***,***.99

              will contain:
                 $**1,000.00

              if the literal 1000 is moved to it or:
                 $****100.00

              if the literal 100 is moved to it.

          5. Special Insertion Editing. The ΓÇ£.ΓÇ¥ (period) is used as the insertion character. In
             addition to being an insertion character it also represents the decimal point for
             alignment purposes. The insertion character used for the actual decimal point is
             counted in the size of the item. The use of the assumed decimal point, represented
             by the symbol ΓÇ£VΓÇ¥ and the actual decimal point, represented by the insertion
             character, in the same PICTURE character-string is disallowed. The result of special
             insertion editing is the appearance of the insertion character in the item in the same
             position as shown in the character-string.
              The period (or the comma if DECIMALΓÇôPOINT IS COMMA is specified in the
              SPECIALΓÇôNAMES paragraph) is the only special insertion symbol.


2ΓÇô26                                                                                7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                          Nucleus




            The result of special insertion editing is the appearance of the insertion character in
            the item in the same position as shown in the character-string. The only exception is
            if a PICTURE string uses only floating insertion symbols (ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥, or currency sign)
            or the suppression/replacement symbol ΓÇ£ZΓÇ¥ to represent the capacity of an edited
            field and the value being edited to zero, the entire item, including the decimal point,
            will contain spaces.

            For example, moving zero to a field defined by the picture string $$$ , $$$ . $$ will
            result in 10 spaces. The effect of moving zero to a field defined by *** , *** . ** is
            the result *******.**.

         6. Fixed Insertion Editing . The currency symbol and the editing sign control symbols,
            ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£CRΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£DBΓÇ¥, are the insertion characters. Only one currency symbol and
            only one of the editing sign control symbols can be used in a given PICTURE
            character-string. When the symbols ΓÇ£CRΓÇ¥ or ΓÇ£DBΓÇ¥ are used they represent two
            character positions in determining the size of the item and they must represent the
            rightmost character positions that are counted in the size of the item. The symbol
            ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥ or ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥, when used, must be either the leftmost or rightmost character position
            to be counted in the size of the item. The currency symbol must be the leftmost
            character position to be counted in the size of the item except that it can be
            preceded by either a ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥ or a ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥ symbol. Fixed insertion editing results in the
            insertion character occupying the same character position in the edited item as it
            occupied in the PICTURE character-string. Editing sign control symbols produce the
            following results depending upon the value of the data item:

                                                                 Result

                Editing Symbol in Picture   Data Item Positive or Zero    Data Item Negative
                     Character-String

                           +                            +                           -

                            -                         space                         -

                           CR                        2 spaces                      CR

                           DB                        2 spaces                     DB


            The multiple consecutive occurrence of the currency sign, the ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥, or the ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥ implies
            floating insertion editing and must abide by the rules for that type of insertion
            editing. No picture may specify two separate types of sign control editing.

         7. Floating Insertion Editing. The currency symbol and editing sign control symbols ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥
            or ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥ are the floating insertion characters and as such are mutually exclusive in a
            given PICTURE character-string.
            Floating insertion editing is indicated in a PICTURE character-string by using a string
            of at least two of the floating insertion characters. This string of floating insertion
            characters may contain any of the fixed insertion symbols or have fixed insertion
            characters immediately to the right of this string. These simple insertion characters
            are part of the floating string.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                  2ΓÇô27
Nucleus




          The leftmost character of the floating insertion string represents the leftmost limit of
          the floating symbol in the data item. The rightmost character of the floating string
          represents the rightmost limit of the floating symbols in the data item.

          The second floating character from the left represents the leftmost limit of the
          numeric data that can be stored in the data item. Nonzero numeric data may replace
          all the characters at or to the right of this limit.

          In a PICTURE character-string, there are only two ways of representing floating
          insertion editing. One way is to represent any or all of the leading numeric character
          positions on the left of the decimal point by the insertion character. The other way is
          to represent all of the numeric character positions in the PICTURE character-string by
          the insertion character.

          In other words, a numeric edited picture string which represents any digit positions
          to the right of a decimal point indicator with the symbol ΓÇ£9ΓÇ¥ must represent all
          fractional digits with the symbol ΓÇ£9ΓÇ¥.

          If the insertion characters are only to the left of the decimal point in the PICTURE
          character-string, the result is that a single floating insertion character will be placed
          into the character position immediately preceding either the decimal point or the first
          nonzero digit in the data represented by the insertion symbol string, whichever is
          farther to the left in the PICTURE character-string. The character positions preceding
          the insertion character are replaced with spaces.

          For example:
             $$$,$$$.99

          will contain:
             $10,000.00
              $1,000.00
                $100.00
                   $.01

          if 10000, 1000, 100 and .01, respectively, are moved to the edited field.

          If all numeric character positions in the PICTURE character-string are represented by
          the insertion character, the result depends upon the value of the data. If the value is
          zero the entire data item will contain spaces. If the value is not zero, the result is the
          same as when the insertion character is only to the left of the decimal point.




2ΓÇô28                                                                               7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                          Nucleus




             For example, a field defined by the picture string:
                ++,+++.++

             will contain:
                 +1,000.00
                   +100.00
                     +1.00

                        +.01

             if 1000, 100, 1, 0, and .01, respectively, are moved to the edited field.

             To avoid truncation, the minimum size of the PICTURE character-string for the
             receiving data item must be the number of characters in the sending data item, plus
             the number of nonfloating insertion characters being edited into the receiving data
             item, plus one for the floating insertion character.

             In a given PICTURE string, floating insertion and fixed insertion of the same symbol
             are disallowed. Also illegal is the specification of more than one type of floating
             insertion editing, or a mixture of floating insertion and suppression and replacement
             editing. In addition, no PICTURE may contain more than one type of sign control
             editing.

         8. Zero Suppression Editing. The suppression of leading zeroes in numeric character
            positions is indicated by the use of the alphabetic character ΓÇ£ZΓÇ¥ or the asterisk (*) as
            suppression symbols in a PICTURE character-string. These symbols are mutually
            exclusive in a given PICTURE characterΓÇôstring. Each suppression symbol is counted
            in determining the size of the item. If ΓÇ£ZΓÇ¥ is used the replacement character will be
            the space and if the asterisk is used, the replacement character will be ΓÇ£*ΓÇ¥.
             Zero suppression and replacement is indicated in a PICTURE character-string by
             using a string of one or more of the allowable symbols to represent leading numeric
             character positions which are to be replaced when the associated character position
             in the data contains a zero. Any of the simple insertion characters embedded in the
             string of symbols or to the immediate right of this string are part of the string.

             In a PICTURE character-string, there are only two ways of representing zero
             suppression. One way is to represent any or all of the leading numeric character
             positions to the left of the decimal point by suppression symbols. The other way is
             to represent all of the numeric character positions in the PICTURE character-string by
             suppression symbols.

             If the suppression symbols appear only to the left of the decimal point, any leading
             zero in the data which corresponds to a symbol in the string is replaced by the
             replacement character. Suppression terminates at the first nonzero digit in the data
             represented by the suppression symbol string or at the decimal point, whichever is
             encountered first.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                  2ΓÇô29
Nucleus




              If all numeric character positions in the PICTURE character-string are represented by
              suppression symbols and the value of the data is not zero the result is the same as if
              the suppression characters were only to the left of the decimal point. If the value is
              zero and the suppression symbol is ΓÇ£ZΓÇ¥, the entire data item will be spaces. If the
              value is zero and the suppression symbol is ΓÇ£*ΓÇ¥, the data item will be all ΓÇ£*ΓÇ¥ except
              for the actual decimal point.

          9. The symbols ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£*ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£ZΓÇ¥, and the currency symbol, when used as floating
             replacement characters, are mutually exclusive within a given character-string.

2.5.8. The REDEFINES Clause
2.5.8.1. Function
          The REDEFINES clause allows the same computer storage area to be described by
          different data description entries.

2.5.8.2. General Format
            levelΓÇônumber dataΓÇônameΓÇô1; REDEFINES dataΓÇônameΓÇô2

          Note: Level-number, data-name-1 and the semicolon are shown in this format to
          improve clarity. Level-number and data-name-1 are not part of the REDEFINES clause.

2.5.8.3. Syntax Rules
          1. The REDEFINES clause, when specified, must immediately follow data-name-1.
          2. The level-numbers of data-name-1 and data-name-2 must be identical, but must not
             be 66 or 88.
          3. This clause must not be used in level 01 entries in the File Section. (See 4.3.6,
             General Rule 2.)
          4. This clause must not be used in level 01 entries in the Communication Section.
          5. The data description entry for data-name-2 cannot contain a REDEFINES clause. In
             Level 1, data-name-2 cannot be subordinate to an entry which contains a
             REDEFINES clause. In Level 2, data-name-2 may be subordinate to an entry which
             contain a REDEFINES clause. The data description entry for data-name-2 cannot
             contain an OCCURS clause. However, data-name-2 may be subordinate to an item
             whose data description entry contains an OCCURS clause. In this case, the
             reference to data-name-2 in the REDEFINES clause may not be subscripted or
             indexed. Neither the original definition nor the redefinition can include an item
             whose size is variable as defined in the OCCURS clause. (See 3.2.1, The OCCURS
             Clause.)
          6. No entry having a level-number numerically lower than the level-number of data-
             name-2 and data-name-1 may occur between the data description entries of data-
             name-2 and data-name-1.

2.5.8.4. General Rules
          1. Redefinition starts at data-name-2 and ends when a level-number less than or equal
             to that of data-name-2 is encountered.
          2. When the levelΓÇônumber of data-name-1 is other than 01, it must specify the same
             number of character positions that the data item referenced by data-name-2
             contains. It is important to observe that the REDEFINES clause specifies the
             redefinition of a storage area, not of the data items occupying the area.




2ΓÇô34                                                                                 7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                          Nucleus




         3. Multiple redefinitions of the same character positions are permitted. The entries
            giving the new descriptions of the character positions must follow the entries
            defining the area being redefined, without intervening entries that define new
            character positions. Multiple redefinitions of the same character positions must all
            use the data-name of the entry that originally defined the area.
         4. The entries giving the new description of the character positions must not contain
            any VALUE clauses, except in condition-name entries.
         5. Multiple level 01 entries subordinate to any given level indicator represent implicit
            redefinitions of the same area.
         6. If data-name-2 is synchronized, its unused bit positions are included in the storage
            allocation of data-name-1.
         7. REDEFINES clauses may be included in RENAMES areas so long as the start of the
            RENAMES area precedes the terminating field of the RENAMES area both in the
            record description and in the storage allocation.

2.5.9. The RENAMES Clause
2.5.9.1. Function

         The RENAMES clause permits alternative, possibly overlapping, groupings of elementary
         items.

         The RENAMES data item permits an item or items established by a record description
         entry to be assigned a new name. Unlike REDEFINES, this clause does not redefine
         existing data descriptions but merely allows data to be accessed and grouped under
         alternative names while maintaining the previously defined data description.

2.5.9.2. General Format


          66 data-name-1; RENAMES       data-name-2               THROUGH           data-name-3          .
                                                                  THRU



         Note: Level-number 66, data-name-1, and the semicolon are shown in the previous
         format to improve clarity. Level-number and data-name-1 are not part of the RENAMES
         clause.

2.5.9.3. Syntax Rules

         1. ALL RENAMES entries referring to data items within a given logical record must
            immediately follow the last data description entry of the associated record
            description entry.
         2. Data-name-2 and data-name-3 must be names of elementary items or groups of
            elementary items in the same logical record, and cannot be the same data-name. A
            66 level entry cannot rename another 66 level entry nor can it rename a 77, 88, or 01
            level entry.



7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                     2ΓÇô35
Nucleus




          3. Data-name-1 cannot be used as a qualifier, and can only be qualified by the names of
             the associated level 01, FD, CD or SD entries. Neither data-name-2 nor data-name-3
             may have an OCCURS clause in its data description entry nor may be subordinate to
             an item that has an OCCURS clause in its data description entry. (See 3.2.1.)

             The RENAMES entry may, however, span an entire table or array. If it does, the size
             of the RENAMES item will include any unused main storage introduced by
             elementary or group item synchronization.

             For example:
                   02 B
                          03 C OCCURS 3 TIMES
                          03 D OCCURS 3 TIMES
                               04 E
                               04 F
                          03 G
                   02 H
                   66 J RENAMES B THRU H

             is a legal sequence while:

                 66 K RENAMES C THRU F

             alone is not correct.

          4. The beginning of the area described by data-name-3 must not be to the left of the
             beginning of the area described by data-name-2. The end of the area described by
             data-name-3 must be to the right of the end of the area described by data-name-2.
             Data-name-3, therefore, cannot be subordinate to data-name-2.

             For example:

                      02 A.
                           03 D PIC X(2).
                           03 C PIC X(2).
                           03 G
                                04 E PIC X(2).
                                04 F PIC X(2).
                      02 B REDEFINES A.
                           03 H PIC X(3).
                           03 I PIC X(4).
                           03 J PIC X.
                      66 K RENAMES D THRU E.
                      66 L RENAMES C THRU I.

             will result in K being the first six characters in either A or B, and L being the third
             through seventh character in either A or B.

          5. Data-name-2 and data-name-3 may be qualified.
          6. The words THRU and THROUGH are equivalent.



2ΓÇô36                                                                                    7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                       Nucleus




         7. None of the items within the range, including data-name-2 and data-name-3, if
            specified, can be an item whose size is variable as defined in the OCCURS clause
            (see 3.2.1).

2.5.9.4. General Rules
         1. One or more RENAMES entries can be written for a logical record.
         2. When data-name-3 is specified, data-name-1 is a group item which includes all
            elementary items starting with data-name-2 (if data-name-2 is an elementary item) or
            the first elementary item in data-name-2 (if data-name-2 is a group item), and
            concluding with data-name-3 (if data-name-3 is an elementary item) or the last
            elementary item in data-name-3 (if data-name-3 is a group item).
         3. When data-name-3 is not specified, data-name-2 can be either a group or an
            elementary item; when data-name-2 is a group item, data-name-1 is treated as a
            group item, and when data-name-2 is an elementary item, data-name-1 is treated as
            an elementary item.

         4. The usage, and therefore the initial alignment, of a RENAMES entry is determined by
            the usage of the data-name-2 or the first elementary item in data-name-2 (if data-
            name-2 is a group item).

2.5.10. The SIGN Clause
2.5.10.1. Function
         The SIGN clause specifies the position and the mode of representation of the operational
         sign when it is necessary to describe these properties explicitly.

2.5.10.2. General Format

         [ SIGN IS ]   LEADING        [ SEPARATE CHARACTER ]
                       TRAILING

2.5.10.3. Syntax Rules
         1. The SIGN clause may be specified only for a numeric data description entry whose
            PICTURE contains the character ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥, or a group item containing at least one such
            numeric data description entry.
         2. The numeric data description entries to which the SIGN clause applies must be
            described as usage is DISPLAY.
         3. At most one SIGN clause may apply to any given numeric data description entry.
         4. If the CODEΓÇôSET clause is specified, any signed numeric data description entries
            associated with that file description entry must be described with the SIGN IS
            SEPARATE clause.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                               2ΓÇô37
Nucleus




2.5.10.4. General Rules
          1. The optional SIGN clause, if present, specifies the position and the mode of
             representation of the operational sign for the numeric data description entry to which
             it applies, or for each numeric data description entry subordinate to the group to
             which it applies. The SIGN clause applies only to numeric data description entries
             whose PICTURE contains the character ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥; the ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥ indicates the presence of, but
             neither the representation nor, necessarily, the position of the operational sign.
          2. A numeric data description entry whose PICTURE contains the character ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥, but to
             which no optional SIGN clause applies, has an operational sign, but neither the
             representation nor, necessarily, the position of the operational sign is specified by
             the character ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥. In this (default) case, the operational sign is represented as an
             overpunch character (see Table 2-1). General rules 3 through 5 do not apply to such
             signed numeric data items.
          3. If the optional SEPARATE CHARACTER phrase is not present, then:
              a.   The operational sign will be presumed to be associated with the leading (or,
                   respectively, trailing) digit position of the elementary numeric data item.
              b. The letter ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥ in a PICTURE character-string is not counted in determining the
                 size of the item (in terms of standard data format characters).
              c.   The valid signs for data items are listed in Table 2-1.

          4. If the optional SEPARATE CHARACTER phrase is present, then:
              a.   The operational sign will be presumed to be the leading (or, respectively, trailing)
                   character position of the elementary numeric data item. This character position
                   is not a digit position.
              b. The letter ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥ in a PICTURE character-string is counted in determining the size
                 of the item (in terms of standard data format characters).
              c.   The operational signs for positive and negative are the standard data format
                   characters ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥ and ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥, respectively.
          5. Every numeric data description entry whose PICTURE contains the character ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥ is
             a signed numeric data description entry. If a SIGN clause applies to such an entry
             and conversion is necessary for purposes of computation or comparisons,
             conversion takes place automatically.
          6. The SIGN clause specified at the elementary level overrides the SIGN clause
             specified at the group level.

2.5.11. The SYNCHRONIZED Clause
2.5.11.1. Function
          The SYNCHRONIZED clause specifies the alignment of an elementary item on the
          natural boundaries of the computer storage (see 1.3.3.3.7).




2ΓÇô38                                                                                   7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                           Nucleus




2.5.11.2. General Format
            SYNCHRONIZED              LEFT
            SYNC                     RIGHT

2.5.11.3. Syntax Rules
         1. This clause may appear only with an elementary item.
         2. SYNC is an abbreviation for SYNCHRONIZED.

2.5.11.4. General Rules
         1. This clause specifies that the subject data item is to be aligned in the computer such
            that no other data item occupies any of the character positions between the leftmost
            and rightmost natural boundaries delimiting this data item. If the number of
            character positions required to store this data item is less than the number of
            character positions between those natural boundaries, the unused character
            positions (or portions thereof) must not be used for any other data item. Such
            unused character positions, however, are included in:
             a.   The size of any group items to which the elementary item belongs, and
             b. The character positions redefined when this data item is the object of a
                REDEFINES clause.
         2. SYNCHRONIZED not followed by either RIGHT or LEFT specifies that the
            elementary item is to be SYNCHRONIZED LEFT if alphanumeric and
            SYNCHRONIZED RIGHT if numeric.
         3. SYNCHRONIZED LEFT specifies that the elementary item is to be positioned such
            that it will begin at the left boundary of the first word in which the elementary item is
            placed. Unused portions of the word, if any, will be to the right of the lower order
            character or digit position of the data item.
         4. SYNCHRONIZED RIGHT specifies that the elementary item is to be positioned such
            that it will terminate on the right boundary of the last word in which the elementary
            item is placed. Unused portions of the word, if any, will be to the left of the high
            order character or digit position of the data item.
         5. Whenever a SYNCHRONIZED item is referenced in the source program, the original
            size of the item, as shown in the PICTURE clause, is used in determining any action
            that depends on size, such as justification, truncation or overflow.
         6. If the data description of an item contains the SYNCHRONIZED clause and an
            operational sign, the sign of the item appears in the normal operational sign position,
            regardless of whether the item is SYNCHRONIZED LEFT or SYNCHRONIZED
            RIGHT.
         7. When the SYNCHRONIZED clause is specified in a data description entry of a data
            item that also contains an OCCURS clause, or in a data description entry of a data
            item subordinate to a data description entry that contains an OCCURS clause, then:
             a.   Each occurrence of the data item is SYNCHRONIZED.
             b. Any implicit FILLER generated for other data items within that same table are
                generated for each occurrence of those data items. (See general rule 8b.)



7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                   2ΓÇô39
Nucleus




          8. This clause is hardware-dependent and in addition to rules 1 through 7, the
             elementary items associated with this clause are handled as follows:

              a.   The format on the external media of records or groups containing elementary items
                   whose data description contains the SYNCHRONIZED clause is the same as the internal
                   format.

              b. Any necessary generation of implicit FILLER, if the elementary item immediately
                 preceding an item containing the SYNCHRONIZED clause does not terminate at
                 a word boundary, is not included as part of the elementary item. Such
                 automatically generated FILLER positions are included in:

                   1) The size of any group to which the FILLER item belongs; and
                   2) The number of character positions allocated when the group item of which
                      the FILLER item is a part appears as the object of a REDEFINES clause.

          9. In the absence of the SYNCHRONIZED clause, ASCII COBOL will align data items on
             the next available word, quarter word, sixth word, or bit boundary in accord with the
             data itemΓÇÖs USAGE clause (see 2.5.12) or position in a word. A full description of
             data allocation and alignment may be found in D.2.
          10. The specification of SYNCHRONIZED for a data item which is already synchronized
              by virtue of its usage (COMPUTATIONALΓÇô1, COMPUTATIONALΓÇô2, or level 01 data
              item) is redundant although permitted.
          11. Level 77 items are implicitly synchronized left and need a SYNCHRONIZED or
              SYNCHRONIZED RIGHT if synchronization different from the default is desired.

2.5.12. The USAGE Clause
2.5.12.1. Function
          The USAGE clause specifies the format of a data item in storage.

2.5.12.2. General Format
                                 COMPUTATIONAL
                                 COMP-2
                                 COMPUTATIONAL-2
          [ USAGE IS ]           COMP-1
                                 COMPUTATIONAL-1
                                 DISPLAY
                                 COMP
                                 DISP


2.5.12.3. Syntax Rules
          1. The PICTURE character-string of a COMPUTATIONAL item can contain only 9ΓÇÖs, the
             operational sign character ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥, the implied decimal point character ΓÇ£VΓÇ¥, and one or
             more PΓÇÖs. (See 2.5.7, the PICTURE Clause.)
          2. COMP, COMPΓÇô1, COMPΓÇô2, and DISP are abbreviations for COMPUTATIONAL,
             COMPUTATIONALΓÇô1, COMPUTATIONALΓÇô2 and DISPLAY respectively.




2ΓÇô40                                                                                   7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                             Nucleus




         3. COMPUTATIONALΓÇô1, and COMPUTATIONALΓÇô2 usage specifications may not
            appear in a data description which has a PICTURE clause, because the computer
            storage format of these items is fixed.
         4. The USAGE clause cannot be used to describe elementary items with a PICTURE
            character-string containing 1ΓÇÖs.

2.5.12.4. General Rules
         1. The USAGE clause can be written at any level. If the USAGE clause is written at a
            group level, it applies to each elementary item in the group. The USAGE clause of
            an elementary item cannot contradict the USAGE clause of a group to which the
            item belongs. The USAGE clause has the following meanings for group items:
            a.   Any explicit usage for a group item applies to all the contained group or
                 elementary items.
            b. If the group usage is defined as DISPLAY or COMPUTATIONAL, the group is
               considered to be an alphanumeric string of ASCII characters. If the group usage
               is not explicitly defined, the group is considered to be an alphanumeric string of
               ASCII characters.
         2. This clause specifies the manner in which a data item is represented in the storage
            of a computer. It does not affect the use of the data item, although the
            specifications for some statements in the Procedure Division may restrict the
            USAGE clause of the operands referred to. The USAGE clause may affect the radix
            or type of character representation of the item. Table 2-5 describes the meaning

2.5.13. The VALUE Clause
2.5.13.1. Function
         The VALUE clause defines the value of constants, the value of Report Section printable
         items, the initial value of working storage and Common-Storage Section items, the initial
         value of data items in the Communication Section, and the values associated with a
         condition-name.

2.5.13.2. General Format
         Format 1
         VALUE IS literal

         Format 2

            VALUE IS                           THROUGH
                                  literal-1                    literal-2
            VALUES ARE                         THRU

                                        THROUGH
                    , literal-3                    literal-4          ...
                                        THRU


2.5.13.3. Syntax Rules

         1. The words THRU and THROUGH are equivalent.
         2. The VALUE clause cannot be stated for any items whose size is variable. (See
            3.2.1.)
         3. A signed numeric literal must have associated with it a signed numeric PICTURE
            character-string.
         4. All numeric literals in a VALUE clause of an item must have a value which is within
            the range of values indicated by the PICTURE clause, and not have a value which
            would require truncation of nonzero digits. Nonnumeric literals in a VALUE clause of
            an item must not exceed the size indicated by the PICTURE clause.

2.5.13.4. General Rules
         1. The VALUE clause must not conflict with other clauses in the data description of the
            item or in the data description within the hierarchy of the item. The following rules
            apply:
             a.   If the category of the item is numeric, all literals in the VALUE clause must be
                  numeric. If the literal defines the value of a working storage item, the literal is
                  aligned in the data item according to the standard alignment rules. (See
                  1.3.3.3.6.)




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                      2ΓÇô43
Nucleus




              b. If the category of the item is alphabetic, alphanumeric, alphanumeric edited or
                 numeric edited, all literals in the VALUE clause must be nonnumeric literals. The
                 literal is aligned in the data item as if the data item had been described as
                 alphanumeric. (See 1.3.3.3.6.) Editing characters in the PICTURE clause are
                 included in determining the size of the data item but have no effect on
                 initialization of the data item. Therefore, the VALUE for an edited item is
                 presented in an edited form.
              c.   Initialization takes place independent of any BLANK WHEN ZERO or JUSTIFIED
                   clause that may be specified.
          2. A figurative constant may be substituted in both Format 1 and Format 2 wherever a
             literal is specified.

2.5.13.5. ConditionΓÇôName Rules

          1. In a condition-name entry, the VALUE clause is required. The VALUE clause and the
             condition-name itself are the only two clauses permitted in the entry. The
             characteristics of a condition-name are implicitly those of its conditional variable.
          2. Format 2 can be used only in connection with condition-names. (See 1.3.3.3.8.5.)
             Wherever the THRU phrase is used, literal-1 must be less than literal-2, literal-3 less
             than literal-4, etc.

2.5.13.6. Data Description Entries Other Than ConditionΓÇôNames
          1. Rules governing the use of the VALUE clause differ with the respective sections of
             the Data Division:
              a.   In Level 1, the VALUE clause cannot be used in the File Section. In the File
                   Section, the VALUE clause may be used only in condition-name entries.
              b. In the WorkingΓÇôStorage Section, Common-Storage Section, and the
                 Communication Section, the VALUE clause must be used in condition-name
                 entries. The VALUE clause may also be used to specify the initial value of any
                 other data item, in which case the clause causes the item to assume the
                 specified value at the start of the object program. If the VALUE clause is not
                 used in an itemΓÇÖs description, the initial value is undefined.
              c.   In Level 1, the VALUE clause cannot be used in the Linkage Section. In the
                   Linkage Section, the VALUE clause may be used only in condition-name entries.
              d. In the Report Section, if the elementary report entry containing the VALUE
                 clause does not contain a GROUP INDICATE clause, then the printable item will
                 assume the specified value each time its report group is printed. However,
                 when the GROUP INDICATE clause is also present, the specified value will be
                 presented only when certain object time conditions exist. (See 8.2.12.)
          2. The VALUE clause must not be stated in a data description entry that contains an
             OCCURS clause, or in an entry that is subordinate to an entry containing an OCCURS
             clause. This rule does not apply to condition-name entries. (See 3.2.1.)




2ΓÇô44                                                                                 7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                           Nucleus




         3. The VALUE clause must not be stated in a data description entry that contains a
            REDEFINES clause, or in an entry that is subordinate to an entry containing a
            REDEFINES clause. This rule does not apply to condition-name entries.
         4. If the VALUE clause is used in an entry at the group level, the literal must be a
            figurative constant or a nonnumeric literal, and the group area is initialized without
            consideration for the individual elementary or group items contained within this
            group. The VALUE clause cannot be stated at the subordinate levels within this
            group.
         5. The VALUE clause must not be written for a group containing items with
            descriptions including JUSTIFIED, SYNCHRONIZED, or USAGE (other than USAGE
            IS DISPLAY).

2.6. Procedure Division
2.6.1. Arithmetic Expressions
2.6.1.1. Definition of an Arithmetic Expression

          An arithmetic expression can be an identifier of a numeric elementary item, a numeric
          literal, such identifiers and literals separated by arithmetic operators, two arithmetic
          expressions separated by an arithmetic operator, or an arithmetic expression enclosed in
          parentheses. Any arithmetic expression may be preceded by a unary operator. The
          permissible combinations of variables, numeric literals, arithmetic operators, and
          parentheses are given in Table 2-7.

          Those identifiers and literals appearing in an arithmetic expression must represent either
          numeric elementary items or numeric literals on which arithmetic may be performed.

2.6.1.2. Arithmetic Operators

          There are five binary arithmetic operators and two unary arithmetic operators that may
          be used in arithmetic expressions. These operators are represented by specific
          characters that must be preceded by a space and followed by a space.

                Binary Arithmetic Operators                   Meaning

                               +                         Addition

                               -                         Subtraction

                               *                         Multiplication

                               /                         Division

                              **                         Exponentiation

                  Unary Arithmetic Operators                   Meaning

                               +                     The effect of multiplication by
                                                     numeric literal +1

                               -                     The effect of multiplication by
                                                     numeric literal -1

2.6.1.3. Formation And Evaluation Rules

         1. Parentheses may be used in arithmetic expressions to specify the order in which
            elements are to be evaluated. Expressions within parentheses are evaluated first,
            and within nested parentheses, evaluation proceeds from the least inclusive set to
            the most inclusive set. When parentheses are not used, or parenthesized
            expressions are at the same level of inclusiveness, the following hierarchical order of
            execution is implied:
             1st        Unary plus and minus
             2nd        Exponentiation
             3rd        Multiplication and division
             4th        Addition and subtraction
         2. Parentheses are used either to eliminate ambiguities in logic where consecutive
            operations of the same hierarchical level appear or to modify the normal hierarchical
            sequence of execution in expressions where it is necessary to have some deviation
            from the normal precedence. When the sequence of execution is not specified by
            parentheses, the order of execution of consecutive operations of the same
            hierarchical level is from left to right.
         3. The ways in which operators, variables, and parentheses may be combined in an
            arithmetic expression are summarized in Table 2-7, where:

             a.    The letter ΓÇ£PΓÇ¥ indicates a permissible pair of symbols.
             b. The character ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥ indicates an invalid pair.
             c.    ΓÇ£VariableΓÇ¥ indicates an identifier or literal.


                  Table 2-7. Combination of Symbols in Arithmetic Expressions

                                                              Second Symbol

                   First Symbol     Variable          * / ** ΓÇô +    Unary + or ΓÇô   (   )

                      Variable           -                P              -         -   P

                     * / ** + -          P                -              P         P   -

                    Unary + or -         P                -              -         P   -

                         (               P                -              P         P   -

                         )               -                P              -         -   P



         4. An arithmetic expression may only begin with the symbol ΓÇ£(ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£+ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£-ΓÇ¥, or a variable
            and may only end with a ΓÇ£)ΓÇ¥ or a variable. There must be a oneΓÇôtoΓÇôone
            correspondence between left and right parentheses of an arithmetic expression such
            that each left parenthesis is to the left of its corresponding right parenthesis.

          See 2.6.3.7 for a description of techniques used in handling arithmetic expressions.

          The following examples illustrate natural and parentheses enforced ordering of COBOL

               Example              Evaluation

               A+B C
                  * **D             52

               (A+B C)
                   * **D            4096

          A+B

         Parentheses have higher precedence than any operator. Operations within parentheses,
         therefore, have precedence over any other in a calculation. In the following example, let
         A = 4, B = 3, and C = 6:

         A+B
                  *AΓÇôC/2
         This produces 13 as a result, whereas:

         ((A + B)
                    * A ΓÇô C) / 2
         produces 11, with the sequence of evaluation proceeding from the innermost
         parenthesized operation to the outermost as follows:

             1.      A+B=7

             2.      7 * A = 28

             3.      28 - C = 22

             4.      22/2 = 11 (Result)


         Double exponentiation is sometimes used in an algebraic expression. For example:


              c
           Ab


         may not be written as:
            A
                ** B ** C
         Parentheses must be used to indicate which exponentiation is to be done first. The
         correct expression is:
            A
                ** (B ** C)
         As an example, let A = 2, B = 2, and C = 3. The resulting evaluations are:

            A                      3 = 64
                ** B ** C = 4

            A                        8 = 256
                ** (B ** C) = 2

2.6.2. Conditional Expressions
          Conditional expressions identify conditions that are tested to enable the object program
          to select between alternate paths of control depending upon the truth value of the
          condition. Conditional expressions are specified in the IF, PERFORM and SEARCH
          statements. There are two categories of condition associated with conditional
          expressions: simple conditions and complex conditions. Each may be enclosed within
          any number of paired parentheses, in which case its category is not changed.

2.6.2.1. Simple Conditions
          The simple conditions are the relation, class condition-name, switch-status, and sign
          conditions. A simple condition has a truth value of ΓÇ£trueΓÇ¥ or ΓÇ£falseΓÇ¥. The inclusion in
          parentheses of simple conditions does not change the simple truth value.
2.6.2.1.1. Relation Condition

          A relation condition causes a comparison of two operands, each of which may be the
          data item referenced by an identifier, a literal, or the value resulting from an arithmetic
          expression. A relation condition has a truth value of ΓÇ£trueΓÇ¥ if the relation exists between
          the operands. Comparison of two numeric operands is permitted regardless of the
          formats specified in their respective USAGE clauses. However, for all other
          comparisons the operands must have the same usage. If either of the operands is a
          group item, the nonnumeric comparison rules apply.

          The general format of a relation condition is:

                                             IS [ NOT] GREATER THAN
                                             IS [ NOT] LESS THAN
            identifier-1                                                          identifier-2
            literal-1                        IS [ NOT] EQUAL TO                   literal-2
            arithmetic-expression-1          IS [ NOT] >                          arithmetic-expression-2
                                             IS [ NOT] <
                                             IS [ NOT] =


          Note: The required relational characters ΓÇ£ > ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£ < ΓÇ¥, and ΓÇ£ = ΓÇ¥ are not underlined, to
          avoid confusion with other symbols such as ΓÇ£ΓëÑΓÇ¥ (greater than or equal to).

          The first operand (identifier-1, literal-1, or arithmetic-expression-1 ) is called the subject of
          the condition; the second operand (identifier-2, literal-2, or arithmetic-expression-2 ) is
          called the object of the condition. The relation condition must contain at least one
          reference to a variable.

          The relational operator specifies the type of comparison to be made in a relation
          condition. A space must precede and follow each reserved word comprising the
          relational operator. When used, ΓÇ£NOTΓÇ¥ and the next key word or relation character are
          one relational operator that defines the comparison to be executed for truth value; for
          example, ΓÇ£NOT EQUALΓÇ¥ is a truth test for an ΓÇ£unequalΓÇ¥ comparison; ΓÇ£NOT GREATERΓÇ¥
          is a truth test for an ΓÇ£equalΓÇ¥ or ΓÇ£lessΓÇ¥ comparison. The meaning of the relational
          operators is as follows.

                     Meaning                       Relational Operator

         Greater than or not greater than    IS [ NOT ] GREATER THAN
                                             IS [ NOT ] >
         Less than or not less than          IS [ NOT ] LESS THAN
                                             IS [ NOT ] <
         Equal to or not equal to            IS [ NOT ] EQUAL TO
                                             IS [ NOT ] =


         Note: The required relational characters ΓÇ£ > ΓÇ¥, ΓÇ£ < ΓÇ¥, and ΓÇ£ = ΓÇ¥ are not underlined, to
         avoid confusion with other symbols such as ΓÇ£ΓëÑΓÇ¥ (greater than or equal to).

2.6.2.1.1.1. Comparison of Numeric Operands

         For operands whose class is numeric (see 1.3.3.3.3), a comparison is made with respect
         to the algebraic value of the operands. The length of the literal or arithmetic expression
         operands, in terms of number of digits represented, is not significant. Zero is considered
         a unique value regardless of the sign.

         For example, a comparison of a data-item which has a value of +000003 with a data-item
         which has a value of +03 will result in an ΓÇ£equalΓÇ¥ condition. Similarly, the value of
         000000 is equal to the value +0000. Following the rules of algebra, +01 is greater than ΓÇô
         155.

         Comparison of these operands is permitted regardless of the manner in which their
         usage is described. Unsigned numeric operands are considered positive for purposes of
         comparison.

         For example, A is equal to B if they are described as:
            02 A PIC 99V99 VALUE 0.01.
            02 B COMP-1 VALUE 10.E-3.

2.6.2.1.1.2. Comparison of Nonnumeric Operands

         For nonnumeric DISPLAY operands, or one numeric DISPLAY and one nonnumeric
         DISPLAY operand, a comparison is made with respect to a specified collating sequence
         of characters (see 2.4.1.2). If one of the operands is specified as numeric, it must be an
         integer data item or an integer literal and:
         1. If the nonnumeric operand is an elementary data item or nonnumeric literal, the
            numeric operand is treated as though it were moved to an elementary alphanumeric
            data item of the same size as the numeric data item (in terms of standard data
            format characters), and the contents of this alphanumeric data item were then
            compared to the nonnumeric operand. (See 2.6.14 and 2.5.7.)
         2. If the nonnumeric operand is a group item, the numeric operand is treated as though
            it were moved to a group item of the same size as the numeric data item (in terms
            of standard data format characters), and the contents of this group item were then
            compared to the nonnumeric operand. (See 2.6.14, the MOVE Statement, and 2.5.7,
            the PICTURE character ΓÇ£PΓÇ¥.)


7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                  2ΓÇô51
Nucleus




          3. A noninteger numeric operand cannot be compared to a nonnumeric operand.
             The size of an operand is the total number of standard data format characters in the
             operand. Numeric and nonnumeric operands may be compared only when their
             usage is the same.

          There are two cases to consider: operands of equal size and operands of unequal size.
          1. Operands of equal size. If the operands are of equal size, comparison effectively
             proceeds by comparing characters in corresponding character positions starting from
             the high order end and continuing until either a pair of unequal characters is
             encountered or the low order end of the operand is reached, whichever comes first.
             The operands are determined to be equal if all pairs of characters compare equally
             through the last pair, when the low order end is reached.
             The first encountered pair of unequal characters is compared to determine their
             relative position in the collating sequence. The operand that contains the character
             that is positioned higher in the collating sequence is considered to be the greater
             operand.
          2. Operands of unequal size. If the operands are of unequal size, comparison proceeds
             as though the shorter operand were extended on the right by sufficient spaces to
             make the operands of equal size.
