Section 9
Segmentation


9.1. General
9.1.1. Function
         The Segmentation module provides a capability to specify object program overlay
         requirements.

9.1.2. Level Characteristics
         Segmentation Level 1 provides a facility for specifying permanent and independent
         segments (see 9.2.2.1). All sections with the same segment-number must be
         contiguous in the source program. All segments specified as permanent segments must
         be contiguous in the source program.

         Segmentation Level 2 provides the facility for intermixing sections with different
         segment-numbers and allows the fixed portion of the source program to contain
         segments that may be overlaid (see 9.2.2.2).




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                 9ΓÇô1
Segmentation




9.2. General Description
       COBOL segmentation is a facility by which the user may communicate with the compiler
       to specify object program overlay requirements.

9.2.1. Scope
       COBOL segmentation deals only with segmentation of procedures. As such, only the
       Procedure Division and the Environment Division are considered in determining
       segmentation requirements for an object program.

9.2.2. Organization
9.2.2.1. Program Segments
       Although it is not mandatory, the Procedure Division for a source program is usually
       written as a consecutive group of sections, each of which is composed of a series of
       closely related operations that are designed to collectively perform a particular function.
       However, when segmentation is used, the entire Procedure Division must be in
       sections. Each section must be classified as belonging either to the fixed portion or to
       one of the independent segments of the object program. Segmentation in no way
       affects the need for qualification of procedure-names to ensure uniqueness.

9.2.2.2. Fixed Portion
       The fixed portion is defined as that part of the object program which is logically treated
       as if it were always in memory. This portion of the program is composed of two types
       of segments: fixed permanent segments and fixed overlayable segments.

       A fixed permanent segment is a segment in the fixed portion which cannot be overlaid
       by any other part of the program.

       A fixed overlayable segment is a segment in the fixed portion which, although logically
       treated as if it were always in memory, can be overlaid by another segment to optimize
       memory utilization. Variation of the number of fixed permanent segments in the fixed
       portion can be accomplished by using a special facility called the SEGMENTΓÇôLIMIT
       clause (see 9.3.2). Such a segment, if called for by the program, is always made
       available in its last used state.




9ΓÇô2                                                                                7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                      Segmentation




9.2.2.3. Independent Segments
         An independent segment is defined as part of the object program which can overlay, and
         can be overlaid by, either a fixed overlayable segment or another independent segment.
         An independent segment is in its initial state whenever control is transferred (either
         implicitly or explicitly) to that segment for the first time during the execution of a
         program. On subsequent transfers of control to the segment, an independent segment
         is also in its initial state when:
         1. Control is transferred to that segment as a result of the implicit transfer of control
            between consecutive statements from a segment with a different segment-number.
         2. Control is transferred to that segment as the result of the implicit transfer of control
            between a SORT or MERGE statement, in a segment with a different segment-
            number, and an associated input or output procedure in that independent segment.
         3. Control is transferred explicitly to that segment from a segment with a different
            segment-number (with the exception noted in paragraph 2 that follows).

         On subsequent transfer of control to the segment, an independent segment is in
         its last-used state when:
         1. Control is transferred implicitly to that segment from a segment with a different
            segment-number (except as noted in preceding paragraphs 1 and 2).
         2. Control is transferred explicitly to that segment as the result of the execution of an
            EXIT PROGRAM statement.

         See 1.3.3.4.2 for an explanation of explicit and implicit transfers of control.

9.2.3. Segmentation Classification
         Sections which are to be segmented are classified, using a system of segmentΓÇônumbers
         (see 9.3.1) and the following criteria:
         1. Logic RequirementsΓÇöSections which must be available for reference at all times, or
            which are referred to very frequently, are normally classified as belonging to one of
            the permanent segments; sections which are used less frequently are normally
            classified as belonging either to one of the overlayable fixed segments or to one of
            the independent segments, depending on logic requirements.
         2. Frequency of UseΓÇöGenerally, the more frequently a section is referred to, the
            lower its segment-number, the less frequently it is referred to, the higher its
            segment-number.
         3. Relationship to Other SectionsΓÇöSections that frequently communicate with one
            another should be given the same segment-numbers.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                    9ΓÇô3
Segmentation




9.2.4. Segmentation Control
       The logical sequence of the program is the same as the physical sequence, except for
       specific transfers of control. The compiler provides all necessary transfers of control
       from segment to segment, and provides control necessary for a segment to operate
       when that segment is called upon to be used. The segment under reference will be
       brought in before program continuation unless it is already in main storage. Control may
       be transferred within a source program to any paragraph in the section; that is, it is not
       mandatory to transfer control to the beginning of a section.




9ΓÇô4                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                 Segmentation




9.3. Structure of Program Segments
9.3.1. SegmentΓÇôNumbers
         Section classification is accomplished by means of a system of segment-numbers. The
         segment-number is included in the section header.

9.3.1.1. General Format
           section-name   SECTION [   segment-number ]   .


9.3.1.2. Syntax Rules
         1. The segment-number must be an integer ranging in value from 0 through 99.
         2. If the segment-number is omitted from the section header, the segment-number is
            assumed to be 0.
         3. Sections in the declaratives must contain segment-numbers less than 50.

9.3.1.3. General Rules
         1. All sections which have the same segment-number constitute a program segment.
            In Level 1, all sections which have the same segment-number must be together in
            the source program. In Level 2, sections with the same segment-numbers need
            not be physically contiguous in the source program.
         2. Segments with segment-number 0 through 49 belong to the fixed portion of the
            object program. In Level 1 all sections with segment-number 0 through 49 must be
            together in the source program.
         3. Segments with segment-number 50 through 99 are independent segments.

9.3.2. SEGMENTΓÇôLIMIT Clause
         Ideally, all program segments having segment-numbers ranging from 0 through 49
         should be specified as permanent segments. However, when insufficient memory
         is available to contain all permanent segments plus the largest overlayable segment,
         it becomes necessary to decrease the number of permanent segments. The
         SEGMENTΓÇôLIMIT feature provides the user with a means by which he can reduce
         the number of permanent segments in his program, while still retaining the logical
         properties of fixed portion segments (segment-numbers 0 through 49).

9.3.2.1. General Format

         The SEGMENTΓÇôLIMIT clause appears in the OBJECTΓÇôCOMPUTER paragraph and has
         the following format:

            [ , SEGMENT-LIMIT IS segment-number ]




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                   9ΓÇô5
Segmentation




9.3.2.2. Syntax Rules

       1. Segment-number must be an integer ranging in value from 1 through 49.

9.3.2.3. General Rules

       1. When the SEGMENTΓÇôLIMIT clause is specified, only those segments having
          segment-numbers from 0 up to, but not including, the segment-number designated
          as the segment-limit, are considered as permanent segments of the object program.
       2. Those segments having segment-numbers from the segmentΓÇôlimit through 49 are
          considered as overlayable fixed segments.
       3. When the SEGMENTΓÇôLIMIT clause is omitted, all segments having segment-
          numbers from 0 through 49 are considered as permanent segments of the object
          program.




9ΓÇô6                                                                         7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                 Segmentation




9.4. Restriction on Program Flow
         When segmentation is used, the following restrictions are placed on the ALTER,
         PERFORM, MERGE, and SORT statements.

9.4.1. The ALTER Statement
         A GO TO statement in a section whose segment-number is greater than or equal to 50
         must not be referred to by an ALTER statement in a section with a different segment-
         number.

         All other uses of the ALTER statement are valid and are performed even if the GO TO to
         which the ALTER refers is in a fixed overlayable segment.

9.4.2. The PERFORM Statement
         A PERFORM statement that appears in a section that is not in an independent segment
         can have within its range, in addition to any declarative sections whose execution is
         caused within that range, only one of the following:
         1. Sections and/or paragraphs wholly contained in one or more nonindependent
            segments.
         2. Sections and/or paragraphs wholly contained in a single independent segment.

         A PERFORM statement that appears in an independent segment can have within its
         range, in addition to any declarative sections whose execution is caused within that
         range, only one of the following:
         1. Sections and/or paragraphs wholly contained in one or more nonindependent
            segments.
         2. Sections and/or paragraphs wholly contained in the same independent segment as
            that PERFORM statement

9.4.3. The MERGE Statement
         If the MERGE statement appears in a section that is not in an independent segment,
         then any output procedure referenced by that MERGE statement must appear:
         ΓÇó   Totally within nonindependent segments, or
         ΓÇó   Wholly contained in a single independent segment.
             If a MERGE statement appears in an independent segment, then any output
             procedure referenced by that MERGE statement must be contained:
         ΓÇó   Totally within nonindependent segments, or
         ΓÇó   Wholly within the same independent segment as that MERGE statement.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                   9ΓÇô7
Segmentation




9.4.4. The SORT Statement
       If a SORT statement appears in a section that is not an independent segment, then any
       input procedures or output procedures referenced by that SORT statement must appear:
       1. Totally within nonindependent segments, or
       2. Wholly contained in a single independent segment.

       If a SORT statement appears in an independent segment, then any input procedures or
       output procedures referenced by that SORT statement must be contained:
       1. Totally within nonindependent segments, or
       2. Wholly within the same independent segment as that SORT statement.

Section 10
Library


10.1. General
10.1.1. Function
         The Library module provides a capability for specifying text that is to be copied from a
         library.

         COBOL libraries contain library texts that are available to the compiler for copying at
         compile time. The effect of the interpretation of the COPY statement is to insert text
         into the source program, where it will be treated by the compiler as part of the source
         program.

         COBOL library text is placed in the COBOL library as a function independent of the
         COBOL program. (See 18.6.)

10.1.2. Level Characteristics
         Library Level 1 provides the facility for copying text from a single library into the source
         program. Text is copied from the library without change.

         Library Level 2 provides the additional capability of replacing all occurrences of a given
         literal, identifier, word or group of words in the library text, with alternate text, during the
         copying process. Level 2 also provides for the availability of more than one COBOL
         library at compile time. (See 18.5.)




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                       10ΓÇô1
Library




10.2. The COPY Statement
10.2.1. Function
          The COPY statement incorporates text into a COBOL source program.

10.2.2. General Format

                                   OF
          COPY text-name                   library-name
                                   IN


                                     = = pseudo-text-1 = =          = = pseudo-text-2 = =
                                     identifier-1                   identifier-2
                REPLACING      ,                             BY                               ...
                                     literal-1                      literal-2
                                     word-1                         word-2




10.2.3. Syntax Rules
          1. If more than one COBOL library is available during compilation, textΓÇôname must be
             qualified by the library-name identifying the COBOL library in which the text
             associated with text-name resides. (See 2.1.3.2 for constraints that apply when
             Library is associated with Nucleus, Level 1.)
              Within one COBOL library, each text-name must be unique.
          2. The COPY statement must be preceded by a space and terminated by the separator
             period.
          3. Pseudo-text-1 must not be null, nor may it consist solely of the character space, nor
             may it consist solely of comment lines.
          4. Pseudo-text-2 may be null.
          5. Character-strings within pseudo-text-1 and pseudo-text-2 may be continued.
             However, both characters of a pseudo-text delimiter must be on the same line. (See
             1.3.9.2.2.) Pseudo-text-1 and pseudo-text-2 consist of COBOL text-words.
          6. Word-1 or word-2 may be any single COBOL word.
          7. A COPY statement may occur in the source program anywhere a character-string or
             a separator may occur, except that a COPY statement must not occur within a COPY
             statement.
          8. If the word COPY appears in a comment-entry or in the place where a
             comment-entry can appear, it is considered part of the comment-entry.




10ΓÇô2                                                                                 7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                                  Library




10.2.4. General Rules
         1. The compilation of a source program containing COPY statements is logically
            equivalent to processing all COPY statements prior to the processing of the resulting
            source program.
         2. The effect of processing a COPY statement is that the library text associated with
            text-name is copied into the source program, logically replacing the entire COPY
            statement, beginning with the reserved word COPY and ending with the punctuation
            character period, inclusive. (See 18.5.)
         3.   If the REPLACING phrase is not specified, the library text is copied unchanged.
              If the REPLACING phrase is specified, the library text is copied or each properly
              matched occurrence of pseudo-text-1, identifier-1, word-1, or literal-1 in the library
              text is replaced by the corresponding pseudo-text-2, identifier-2, word-2, or literal-2.

         4. For purposes of matching, identifier-1, word-1, and literal-1 are treated as
            pseudo-text containing only identifier-1, word-1, and literal-1, respectively.
         5. The comparison operation to determine text replacement occurs in the following
            manner:

              Any separator comma, semicolon, and/or spaces preceding the leftmost library
              text-word are copied into the source program. Starting with the leftmost library
              text-word and the first pseudo-text-1, identifier-1, word-1, or literal-1 that was
              specified in the REPLACING phrase, the entire REPLACING phrase operand that
              precedes the reserved word BY is compared to an equivalent number of contiguous
              library text-words.
              Pseudo-text-1, identifier-1, word-1, or literal-1 match the library text if, and only if, the
              ordered sequence of text-words that forms pseudo-text-1, identifier-1, word-1, or
              literal-1 is equal, character for character, to the ordered sequence of library
              text-words. For purposes of matching, each occurrence of a separator comma or
              semicolon in pseudo-text-1 or in the library text is considered to be a single space
              except when pseudo-text-1 consists solely of either a separator comma or
              semicolon, in which case it participates in the match as a text-word. Each sequence
              of one or more space separators is considered to be a single space.
              If no match occurs, the comparison is repeated with each next successive
              pseudo-text-1, identifier-1, word-1, or literal-1, if any, in the REPLACING phrase until
              either a match is found or there is no next successive REPLACING operand.
              When all the REPLACING phrase operands have been compared and no match has
              occurred, the leftmost library textΓÇôword is copied into the source program. The next
              successive library textΓÇôword is then considered as the leftmost library text-word, and
              the comparison cycle starts again with the first pseudo-text-1, identifier-1,
              word-1, or literal-1 specified in the REPLACING phrase.
              Whenever a match occurs between pseudo-textΓÇô1, identifier-1, word-1, or literal-1
              and the library text, the corresponding pseudo-text-2, identifier-2, word-2, or literal-2
              is placed into the source program. The library text-word immediately following the
              rightmost textΓÇôword that participated in the match is then considered as the leftmost
              library text-word. The comparison cycle starts again with the first pseudo-text-1,
              identifier-1, word-1, or literal-1 specified in the REPLACING phrase.



7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                        10ΓÇô3
Library




               The comparison operation continues until the rightmost text-word in the library text
               has either participated in a match or been considered as a leftmost library text-word
               and participated in a complete comparison cycle.
          6.   A comment line occurring in the library text and pseudo-text-1 is interpreted, for
               purposes of matching, as a single space. Comment lines appearing in
               pseudo-text-2 and library text are copied into the source program unchanged.
          7. Debugging lines are permitted within library text and pseudo-text-2. Debugging lines
             are not permitted within pseudo-text-1; text-words within a debugging line
             participate in the matching rules as if the ΓÇ£DΓÇ¥ did not appear in the indicator area. If
             a COPY statement is specified on a debugging line, the text that is the result of the
             processing of the COPY statement will appear as though it were specified on
             debugging lines with the following exception: comment lines in library text will
             appear as comment lines in the resultant source program.
          8. The text produced as a result of the complete processing of a COPY statement must
             not contain a COPY statement.
          9. The syntactic correctness of the library text cannot be independently determined.
             The syntactic correctness of the entire COBOL source program cannot be
             determined until all COPY statements have been completely processed.
          10. Each word in pseudo-text-2 that is to be placed in the resultant program is placed in
              the same area as it appears in pseudo-text-2. Library text must conform to the rules
              for COBOL reference format.
          11. For purposes of compilation, text-words after replacement are placed in the source
              program according to the rules for reference format. (See 1.3.9.) On the source
              listing, all copied material will be realigned to allow for replacement of greater
              length.

Section 11
Debug


11.1. General
11.1.1. Function
         The Debug module provides a means by which the user can describe his debugging
         algorithm including the conditions under which data items or procedures are to be
         monitored during the execution of the object program.

         The decision of what to monitor and what information to display on the output device are
         explicitly in the domain of the user. The ASCII COBOL debug facility simply provides a
         convenient access to pertinent information.

11.1.2. Level Characteristics
         Debug Level 1 provides a basic debugging capability, including the ability to specify
         selective or full procedure monitoring, and optionally compiled debugging statements.

         Debug Level 2 provides the full ASCII COBOL debugging facility.

11.1.3. Language Concepts
         The features of the COBOL language that support the Debug module are:
         1. A compile time switchΓÇöWITH DEBUGGING MODE.
         2. An object time switch.
         3. A USE FOR DEBUGGING statement.
         4. A special registerΓÇöDEBUGΓÇôITEM.
         5. Debugging lines.

11.1.3.1. DEBUGΓÇôITEM
         The reserved word DEBUGΓÇôITEM is the name for a special register generated
         automatically by the compiler. Only one DEBUGΓÇôITEM is allocated per program. The
         names of the subordinate data items in DEBUGΓÇôITEM are also reserved words.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                11ΓÇô1
Debug




11.1.3.2. Compile Time Switch
        The WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause is written as part of the SOURCEΓÇôCOMPUTER
        paragraph. It serves as a compile time switch over the debugging statements written in
        the program.

        When the WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause is specified in a program, all debugging
        sections and all debugging lines are compiled as specified in this section. When the
        WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause is not specified, all debugging lines and all debugging
        sections are compiled as if they were comment lines.

        The specification of the U extra option on the ACOB processor call statement will cause
        the compiler to ignore the WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause if specified. This option
        provides a means to turn off the compiler time switch without editting the source
        program.

11.1.3.3. Object Time Switch
        An object time switch dynamically activates the debugging code inserted by the
        compiler. This switch cannot be addressed in the program. It is controlled outside the
        COBOL environment. If the switch is ΓÇ£onΓÇ¥, all the effects of the debugging language
        written in the source program are permitted. If the switch is ΓÇ£offΓÇ¥, all the effects
        described in 11.3.1 are inhibited. Recompilation of the source program is not required to
        provide or take away this facility.

        The object time switch is the D option on the @XQT statement. If the switch is ΓÇ£onΓÇ¥
        (the D option is not present), all the effects of the debugging language written in the
        source program are executed. If the switch is ΓÇ£offΓÇ¥ (the D option is present), the effects
        of USE FOR DEBUGGING are inhibited. It should be noted that the run-time libraries and
        inline code are still present. What is inhibited is the updating of the DEBUGΓÇôITEM and
        the execution of the associated debugging section.

        The object time switch has no effect on the execution of the object program if the WITH
        DEBUGGING MODE clause was not specified in the source program at compile time.




11ΓÇô2                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                             Debug




11.2. Environment Division
11.2.1. The WITH DEBUGGING MODE Clause
11.2.1.1. Function
         The WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause indicates that all debugging sections and all
         debugging lines are to be compiled. If this clause is not specified, all debugging lines
         and sections are compiled as if they were comment lines.

11.2.1.2. General Format
           SOURCE-COMPUTER.   computer-name   [ WITH DEBUGGING MODE     ]   .


11.2.1.3. General Rules
         1. If the WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause is specified in the SOURCEΓÇôCOMPUTER
            paragraph of the Configuration Section of a program, all USE FOR DEBUGGING
            statements and all debugging lines are compiled.
         2. If the WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause is not specified in the
            SOURCEΓÇôCOMPUTER paragraph of the Configuration Section of a program, any
            USE FOR DEBUGGING statements and all associated debugging sections, and
            any debugging lines are compiled as if they were comment lines.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                   11ΓÇô3
Debug




11.3. Procedure Division
11.3.1. The USE FOR DEBUGGING Statement
11.3.1.1. Function
        The USE FOR DEBUGGING statement identifies the user items that are to be monitored
        by the associated debugging section.

11.3.1.2. General Format

        section-name SECTION [ segment-number ] .


                                            cd-name-1
                                            [ ALL REFERENCES OF ] identifier-1
        USE FOR DEBUGGING ON                file-name-1
                                            procedure-name-1
                                            ALL PROCEDURES



                         cd-name-2
                         [ ALL REFERENCES OF ] identifier-2
                     ,   file-name-2                                 ... .
                         procedure-name-2
                         ALL PROCEDURES

11.3.1.3. Syntax Rules
        1. Debugging sections, if specified, must appear together immediately after the
           DECLARATIVES header.
        2. Except in the USE FOR DEBUGGING statement itself, there must be no reference to
           any nondeclarative procedure within the debugging section.
        3. Statements appearing outside of the set of debugging sections must not reference
           procedure-names defined within the set of debugging sections.
        4. Except for the USE FOR DEBUGGING statement itself, statements appearing within
           a given debugging section may reference procedure-names defined within a
           different USE procedure only with a PERFORM statement.
        5. Procedure-names defined within debugging sections must not appear within USE
           FOR DEBUGGING statements.
        6. Any given identifier, cd-name, file-name, or procedure-name may appear in only one
           USE FOR DEBUGGING statement and may appear only once in that statement.
        7. The ALL PROCEDURES phrase can appear only once in a program.
        8. When the ALL PROCEDURES phrase is specified, procedure-name-1,
           procedure-name-2, ... must not be specified in any USE FOR DEBUGGING
           statement.




11ΓÇô4                                                                             7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                               Debug




         9. Identifier-1, identifier-2, ..., must not reference any data item defined in the Report
            Section except sum counters.
         10. If the data description entry of the data item referenced by identifier-1, identifier-2,
             ..., contains an OCCURS clause or is subordinate to a data description entry that
             contains an OCCURS clause, identifier-1, identifier-2, ..., must be specified without
             the subscripting or indexing normally required.
         11. References to the special register DEBUGΓÇôITEM are restricted to references from
             within a debugging section or a table error section .

11.3.1.4. General Rules
         1. In the following general rules, all references to cd-name-1, identifier-1,
            procedure-name-1, and file-name-1 apply equally to cd-name-2, identifier-2,
            procedure-name-2, and file-name-2, respectively.
         2. Automatic execution of a debugging section is not caused by a statement appearing
            in a debugging section.
         3. When file-name-1 is specified in a USE FOR DEBUGGING statement, that debugging
            section is executed:

             a.   After the execution of any OPEN or CLOSE statement that references
                  file-name-1, and
             b. After the execution of any READ statement (after any other specified USE
                procedure) not resulting in the execution of an associated AT END or INVALID
                KEY imperative statement, and
             c.   After the execution of any DELETE or START statement that references
                  file-name-1.
         4. When procedure-name-1 is specified in a USE FOR DEBUGGING statement that
            debugging section is executed:
             a.   Immediately before each execution of the named procedure;
             b. Immediately after the execution of an ALTER statement which references
                procedure-name-1.
         5. The ALL PROCEDURES phrase causes the effects described in general rule 4 to
            occur for every procedure-name in the program, except those appearing within a
            debugging section.
         6. When the ALL REFERENCES OF identifier-1 phrase is specified, that debugging
            section is executed for every statement that explicitly references identifier-1 at each
            of the following times:

             a.   In the case of a WRITE or REWRITE statement immediately before the
                  execution of that WRITE or REWRITE statement and after the execution of any
                  implicit move resulting from the presence of the FROM phrase.
             b. In the case of a GO TO statement with a DEPENDING ON phrase, immediately
                before control is transferred and prior to the execution of any debugging section
                associated with the procedure-name to which control is to be transferred.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                     11ΓÇô5
Debug




            c.   In the case of a PERFORM statement in which a VARYING, AFTER, or UNTIL
                 phrase references identifier-1, immediately after each initialization, modification,
                 or evaluation of the contents of the data item referenced by identifier-1.
            d. In the case of any other COBOL statement, immediately after execution of that
               statement.

                 If identifier-1 is specified in a phrase that is not executed or evaluated, the
                 associated debugging section is not executed.

        7. When identifier-1 is specified without the ALL REFERENCES OF phrase, that
           debugging section is executed at each of the following times:

            a.   In the case of a WRITE or REWRITE statement that explicitly references
                 identifier-1, immediately before the execution of that WRITE or REWRITE
                 statement and after the execution of any implicit move resulting from the
                 presence of the FROM phrase.
            b. In the case of a PERFORM statement in which a VARYING, AFTER or UNTIL
               phrase references identifier-1, immediately after each initialization, modification,
               or evaluation of the contents of the data item referenced by identifier-1.
            c.   Immediately after the execution of any other COBOL statement that explicitly
                 references and causes the contents of the data item referenced by identifier-1 to
                 be changed.
            If identifier-1 is specified in a phrase that is not executed or evaluated, the
            associated debugging section is not executed.
        8. The associated debugging section is not executed for a specific operand more than
           once as a result of the execution of a single statement, regardless of the number of
           times that operand is explicitly specified. In the case of a PERFORM statement
           which causes iterative execution of a referenced procedure, the associated
           debugging section is executed once for each iteration.
            Within an imperative statement, each individual occurrence of an imperative verb
            identifies a separate statement for the purpose of debugging.
        9. When cd-name-1 is specified in a USE FOR DEBUGGING statement, that debugging
           section is executed:

            a.   After the execution of any ENABLE, DISABLE, and SEND statement that
                 references cd-name-1,
            b. After the execution of a RECEIVE statement referencing cd-name-1 that does
               not result in the execution of the NO DATA imperative-statement, and
            c.   After the execution of an ACCEPT MESSAGE COUNT statement that references
                 cd-name-1.
        10. A reference to file-name-1, identifier-1, procedure-name-1, or cd-name-1 as a
            qualifier does not constitute reference to that item for the debugging described in
            the general rules above.




11ΓÇô6                                                                                   7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                            Debug




         11. Associated with each execution of a debugging section is the special register
             DEBUGΓÇôITEM, which provides information about the conditions that caused the
             execution of a debugging section. DEBUGΓÇôITEM has the following implicit
             description:
             01   DEBUG-ITEM.
                  02 DEBUG-LINE     PICTURE IS X(6).
                  02 FILLER         PICTURE IS X VALUE SPACE.
                  02 DEBUG-NAME     PICTURE IS X(30).
                  02 FILLER         PICTURE IS X VALUE SPACE.
                  02 DEBUG-SUB-1    PICTURE IS S9999 SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE CHARACTER.
                  02 FILLER         PICTURE IS X VALUE SPACE.
                  02 DEBUG-SUB-2    PICTURE IS S9999 SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE CHARACTER.
                  02 FILLER         PICTURE IS X VALUE SPACE.
                  02 DEBUG-SUB-3    PICTURE IS S9999 SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE CHARACTER.
                  02 FILLER         PICTURE IS X VALUE SPACE.
                  02 DEBUG-CONTENTS PICTURE IS X(n).

         12. Prior to each execution of a debugging section, the contents of the data item
             referenced by DEBUGΓÇôITEM are space filled. The contents of data items
             subordinate to DEBUGΓÇôITEM are then updated, according to the following general
             rules, immediately before control is passed to that debugging section. The contents
             of any data item not specified in the following general rules remains spaces.
             Updating is accomplished in accordance with the rules for the MOVE statement.
             The sole exception is the move to DEBUGΓÇôCONTENTS, when the move is treated
             exactly as if it were an alphanumeric to alphanumeric elementary move with no
             conversion of data from one form of internal representation to another.
         13. The content of DEBUGΓÇôLINE is the number of the source line which causes the
             execution of a debugging section.
         14. DEBUGΓÇôNAME contains the first 30 characters of the name that caused the
             debugging section to be executed.
             All qualifiers of the name are separated in DEBUGΓÇôNAME by the word ΓÇ£INΓÇ¥ or ΓÇ£OFΓÇ¥.
             Subscripts or indices, if any, are not entered into DEBUGΓÇôNAME.

11.3.2. Debugging Lines
         A debugging line is any line with a ΓÇ£DΓÇ¥ in the indicator area of the line. Any debugging
         line that consists solely of spaces from margin A to margin R is the same as a blank line.

         The contents of a debugging line must be such that a syntactically correct program is
         formed with or without the debugging lines being considered as comment lines.

         A debugging line will be considered to have all the characteristics of a comment line, if
         the WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause is not specified in the SOURCEΓÇôCOMPUTER
         paragraph.

         Successive debugging lines are allowed. Continuation of debugging lines is permitted,
         except that each continuation line must contain a ΓÇ£DΓÇ¥ in the indicator area, and
         character-strings may not be broken across two lines.

         A debugging line is permitted in the program only after the OBJECTΓÇôCOMPUTER
         paragraph.

11.4. Table Error Facility
11.4.1. General
        The Table Error facility allows the user to check for validity of table elements referenced
        in a program by specifying syntax, a compiler option, or both. A table error or subscript
        out of range occurs any time the subscript value exceeds the maximum number of
        occurrences of an item as specified in the OCCURS clause.

11.4.2. Compiler Option
11.4.2.1. Function

        When the compiler extra option X is specified, a subscript range check will be performed
        for every table reference in the program.

11.4.2.2. General Rule

        When the X extra option is specified, if the data item is not the object of a USE FOR
        TABLE ERROR procedure and the subscript of the data item is out of range, the name of
        the data item and its source line number will be displayed, and execution terminated.

11.4.3. Procedure Division
11.4.3.1. The DECLARATIVE Paragraph
11.4.3.1.1. Function

        The USE FOR TABLE ERROR statement in the DECLARATIVE paragraph identifies the
        user table data items that are to be monitored by the associated table error section.

11.4.3.1.2. General Format


                                                              ALL
            USE FOR TABLE ERROR REFERENCES ON                 { identifier-1 } . . .


11.4.3.1.3. Syntax Rules

        1. There must be no reference to any nondeclarative procedure within the table error
           section.
        2. Statements appearing outside of the set of table error sections must not reference
           procedure-names defined within the set of table error sections.
        3. Statements appearing within a given table error section may reference procedure-
           names defined within a different USE procedure only with a PERFORM statement.
        4. Identifier-1 may appear in only one USE FOR TABLE ERROR statement and may
           appear only once in that statement.



11ΓÇô10                                                                                  7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                           Debug




         5. The ALL phrase can appear only once in a program, and when it is specified,
            identifier-1 must not be specified in any USE FOR TABLE ERROR statement.
         6. Identifier-1 must not reference any data item in the Report Section.
         7. The data description entry of the data item referenced by identifierΓÇô1 must contain
            an OCCURS clause or be subordinate to a data description entry that contains an
            OCCURS clause. Identifier-1 must be specified without the subscripting or indexing
            normally required.
         8. The special register DEBUGΓÇôITEM (see subsections 11.1.3.1 and 11.3.1.4, rule 11)
            may be referenced from within a table error section.

11.4.3.1.4. General Rules

         1. Automatic execution of a table error section is not caused by a statement appearing
            in table error section.
         2. If the data item is the object of a USE FOR TABLE ERROR procedure and the
            subscript is out of range, DEBUGΓÇôITEM is filled, and then the USE FOR TABLE
            ERROR procedure is executed.
         3. The ALL phrase causes the effects described in general rule 2 to occur for every
            table reference in the program except those appearing within a table error section.
         4. Special register DEBUGΓÇôITEM is filled as follows:

             a.   DEBUGΓÇôLINE contains the number of the source line which caused the
                  execution of the table error section.
             b. DEBUGΓÇôNAME contains the first 30 characters of the name that caused the
                table error section to be executed. All qualifiers of the name are separated in
                DEBUGΓÇôNAME by the word IN or OF.
             c.   DEBUGΓÇôSUBΓÇôn contains the occurrence number of each level.
             d. DEBUGΓÇôCONTENTS contains ΓÇ£TABLE ERRORΓÇ¥.

11.5. Programmers Advanced Debugging System
      (PADS 2200)
11.5.1. General
        The Programmers Advanced Debugging System (PADS 2200) is a debugging tool which
        allows users to display and alter the contents of variables defined in their programs
        during the execution of the programs. It also allows users to set ΓÇ£trapsΓÇ¥ at section
        names, paragraph names, and at source lines containing executable statements. The
        ΓÇ£trapΓÇ¥ causes program execution to be suspended when the section name, paragraph
        name, or line number is reached.

        PADS 2200 contains a number of features in addition to these. A complete description
        of the PADS 2200 command language can be found in OS 2200 Programmers Advanced
        Debugging System (PADS) Programming Guide (7831 0562).

        Users may invoke PADS by specifying syntax in the COBOL source language program or
        by entering a processor call statement immediately before the user program is executed.
        In either case, it is necessary to compile the source language program with a special
        option in order to use all the functions of PADS during program execution.

11.5.2. Compiler Option
11.5.2.1. Function

        When the compiler extra option K is specified, the compiler generates symbolic
        debugging tables that enable PADS to locate and reference user-defined program
        entities during execution of the user program.

        These tables include information describing the variables defined in the user program
        which PADS needs in order to display or alter the contents of the variables. The
        contents of variables are displayed or altered only upon user command.

11.5.2.2. General Rules

        The K extra option should not be used with the J extra option. Should both these
        options be specified, the J extra option overrides the K extra option, and the compiler
        does not generate the symbolic debugging tables.

        Limited PADS functionality is available within programs not compiled with the K extra
        option. In these cases, any PADS commands which reference section or paragraph
        names, variables, or source program line numbers generate PADS 2200 diagnostic
        messages.




11ΓÇô12                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                         Debug




11.5.3. Procedure Division
11.5.3.1. The CALL Statement
11.5.3.1.1. Function

         The CALL statement in the procedure division may be used to force PADS to gain
         control of the user program at the point at which the CALL statement is executed.

11.5.3.1.2. General Format

           CALL   ΓÇÿPADS$ΓÇÖ


11.5.3.1.3. Syntax Rules

         1. No arguments may be specified with this use of the CALL statement.
         2. The ON OVERFLOW clause may not be specified with this use of the CALL
            statement.

11.5.3.1.4. General Rules

         1. When the CALL statement is executed, execution of the user program is suspended,
            and PADS is given control. PADS prints a message identifying itself and then solicits
            the user for commands.
         2. This form of the CALL statement should not be used in source programs that use
            the COBOL language segmentation module or that use any features of the
            Asynchronous Control System.
         3. PADS must not be invoked from COBOL subprograms that are called from a main
            program written in ASCII FORTRAN, PL/I, Fieldata FORTRAN, Fieldata COBOL, or
            ASM.
         4. PADS may be invoked from COBOL subprograms that are called from a main
            program written in MASM. The MASM main program must preserve the contents
            of registers R1 through R3, R11 through R15, and A4 and A5, that were set by the
            Executive when the user program was loaded into storage.
         5. PADS may not be used with programs which run in the TIP or HVTIP environment
            (see OS 1100 ASCII COBOL, Installation Reference Manual, UPΓÇô8585).
         6. PADS can be given control during execution of the user program without the need
            for any changes to the source language program. See OS 2200 Programmers
            Advanced Debugging System (PADS) Programming Guide (7831 0562) for a
            description of the manner in which this can be done.

Section 12
Interprogram Communication


12.1. General
12.1.1. Function
         The Interprogram Communication module provides a facility by which a program can
         communicate with one or more programs. This communication is provided by the ability
         to transfer control from one program to another within a run unit and the ability for both
         programs to have access to the same data items.

12.1.2. Level Characteristics
         Interprogram Communication Level 1 provides a capability to transfer control to one or
         more programs whose names are known at compile time and for the sharing of data
         among such programs.

         Additionally, Interprogram Communication Level 2 provides the capability to transfer
         control to one or more programs whose names are not known at compile time as well as
         the ability to determine the availability of object time memory for the program to which
         control is being passed.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                 12ΓÇô1
Interprogram Communication




12.2. Environment Division
12.2.1. The IΓÇôOΓÇôCONTROL Paragraph
12.2.1.1. The APPLY Clause
12.2.1.1.1. Function

        The APPLY clause in the IΓÇôOΓÇôCONTROL paragraph specifies which compiler-generated
        tables and data areas are to be shared during execution among two or more separately
        compiled programs.

12.2.1.1.2. General Format

                           EXREF
                APPLY      EXDEF        ON    { identifier-1 } . . .   ...


12.2.1.1.3. Syntax Rules

        1. Identifier-1 ..., must specify a cd-name, file-name, sa-name, or Working-Storage level
           01 data-name, and must be unique in the first 12 characters.
        2. An identifier may be the object of only one APPLY EXDEF clause in a run unit.
        3. An identifier may occur only once in an APPLY clause of a program.
        4. An identifier may be the object of more than one APPLY EXREF clause in a run unit.
        5. An identifier in an APPLY EXREF clause must specify the same type of item as was
           specified in its associated APPLY EXDEF clause.

12.2.1.1.4. General Rules

        1. The tables and data areas associated with the identifier in the APPLY EXDEF clause
           are accessible by programs that specify the same identifier in an APPLY EXREF
           clause.
        2. The descriptions associated with each identifier in the APPLY EXREF clause must be
           equivalent to the descriptions associated with that same identifier when specified in
           an APPLY EXDEF clause.
        3. All declarative procedures and Report Descriptions associated with a file must be
           specified in the same program that has the APPLY EXDEF for that file.
        4. The APPLY EXDEF clause must be specified in the main program for any file that
           potentially invokes a declarative procedure or has a Report attached to it.
        5. The identifier specified in the APPLY EXREF clause must not have a REDEFINES
           clause at the record level. It can, however, be the object of a REDEFINES clause
           and can contain subordinate items that are redefined.




12ΓÇô2                                                                             7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                             Interprogram Communication




         6. The identifier specified in the APPLY EXREF clause must define the same number of
            character positions as the same identifier when specified in the APPLY EXDEF
            clause. It is important to note that the APPLY EXREF clause specifies the
            redefinition of a storage area, not of the data items occupying the area.
         7. When APPLY EXREF is specified, the VALUE clause must not be present in that
            entry.
         8. The APPLY EXDEF clause must be specified in the main program for any IBM
            compatible tape file which contains an OCCURS DEPENDING ON data item.

            a.   Define the FILE STATUS data item in the COMMONΓÇôSTORAGE SECTION of all

               WORKINGΓÇôSTORAGE SECTION. In the subprograms that reference it, define it
               in the LINKAGE SECTION.
            c.   EXDEF the FILE STATUS item in the program where the file is EXDEFΓÇÖed, and

12.3. Data Division
12.3.1. Linkage Section
       The Linkage Section in a program is meaningful if, and only if, the object program is to
       function under the control of a CALL statement, and the CALL statement in the calling
       program contains a USING phrase.

       The Linkage Section is used for describing data that is available through the calling
       program but is to be referred to in both the calling and the called program. No space is
       allocated in the program for data items referenced by data-names in the Linkage Section
       of that program. Procedure Division references to these data items are resolved at
       object time by equating the reference in the called program to the location used in the
       calling program. In the case of index-names, no such correspondence is established.
       Index-names in the called and calling program always refer to separate indices.

       Data items defined in the Linkage Section of the called program may be referenced
       within the Procedure Division of the called program only if they are specified as operands
       of the USING phrase of the Procedure Division header or are subordinate to such
       operands, and the object program is under the control of a CALL statement that
       specifies a USING phrase.

       The structure of the Linkage Section is the same as that previously described for the
       Working-Storage Section, beginning with a section header, followed by data description
       entries for noncontiguous data items and record description entries.

       Each Linkage Section record-name and noncontiguous item name must be unique within
       the called program since it cannot be qualified. Data items defined in the Linkage
       Section of the called program must not be associated with data items defined in the
       Report Section of the calling program.

       Of those items defined in the Linkage Section only data-name-1, data-name-2, ..., in the
       USING phrase of the Procedure Division header, data items subordinate to these
       data-names, and condition-names and/or index-names associated with such
       data-names and/or subordinate data items, may be referenced in the Procedure Division.

12.3.1.1. Noncontiguous Linkage Storage
       Items in the Linkage Section that bear no hierarchic relationship to one another need not
       be grouped into records and are classified and defined as noncontiguous elementary
       items. Each of these data items is defined in a separate data description entry which
       begins with the special level-number 77.

       The following data clauses are required in each data description entry:
       1. Level-number 77
       2. data-name
       3. the PICTURE clause or the USAGE IS INDEX, COMPUTATIONALΓÇô1,
          COMPUTATIONALΓÇô2, or LOCK clause.
       Other data description clauses are optional and can be used to complete the description
       of the item if necessary.


12ΓÇô4                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                               Interprogram Communication




12.3.1.2. Linkage Records
         Data elements in the Linkage Section which bear a definite hierarchic relationship to one
         another must be grouped into records according to the rules for formation of record
         descriptions. Any clause which is used in an input or output record description can be
         used in a Linkage Section.

12.3.1.3. Initial Values
         The VALUE clause must not be specified in the Linkage Section except in conditionΓÇô
         name entries (level 88).

12.3.2. Common-Storage Section
         The Common-Storage Section is a block of main storage which is shared by all collected
         COBOL programs which define a Common-Storage Section.

         The structure and permissible data definition statements for Common-Storage are
         identical to those for the Working-Storage Section.

         If Common-Storage Sections are different sizes, the total area allocated for an execution
         is sufficient for the largest Common-Storage Section.

         The main storage area shared by two or more COBOL Common-Storage Sections may
         also be shared by assembly language blank common which is specified by the INFO
         directive.

         The common areas may be used to conserve main storage by providing a ΓÇ£scratch padΓÇ¥
         area which each main program and subprogram may use for itself. Or it may be used to
         allow one program to directly address data that belongs to another program. If
         Common-Storage is used for this purpose, the user must take the necessary actions to
         ensure that data field allocation and alignment is consistent among all programs that
         share the area. The use of the COPY statement for this function is recommended.

         When using Common-Storage in nonsegmented programs it is advisable to have all
         Common-Storage areas defined identically, including initial values. This is because the
         last one collected is the one whose Common-Storage values will be loaded.

         When compiling with a V option on the processor call statement and a 1 option in the
         Extra Options field, no initial values will be generated for the subprogramΓÇÖs
         Common-Storage area. If a ΓÇ£1ΓÇ¥ is not specified in the Extra Options field of the
         processor call statement with a V option, the subprogramΓÇÖs Common-Storage area will
         have its initial values generated. If these values are contained in a secondary segment
         they will overlay the main programΓÇÖs Common-Storage values when the subprogram is
         called and subsequently loaded.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                 12ΓÇô5
Interprogram Communication




12.4. Procedure Division
12.4.1. The Procedure Division Header
       The Procedure Division is identified by and must begin with the following header:

         PROCEDURE DIVISION

                     [ USING data-name-1 [ , data-name-2 ] . . . ]

                     [ WITH ENTRY POINTS { procedure-name-1 } . . . ] .


       The USING phrase is present if and only if the object program is to function under the
       control of a CALL statement, and the CALL statement in the calling program contains a
       USING phrase.

       Each of the operands in the USING phrase of the Procedure Division header must be
       defined as a data item in the Linkage Section of the program in which this header occurs,
       and it must have a 01 or 77 level-number.

       Within a called program, Linkage Section data items are processed according to their
       data descriptions given in the called program.

       When the USING phrase is present, the object program operates as if data-name-1 of
       the Procedure Division header in the called program and data-name-1 in the USING
       phrase of the CALL statement in the calling program refer to a single set of data that is
       equally available to both the called and calling programs. Their descriptions must define
       an equal number of character positions; however, they need not be the same name. In
       like manner, there is an equivalent relationship between data-name-2, ..., in the USING
       phrase of the called program and data-name-2, ..., in the USING phrase of the CALL
       statement in the calling program. A dataΓÇôname must not appear more than once in the
       USING phrase in the Procedure Division header of the called program; however, a given
       data-name may appear more than once in the same USING phrase of a CALL statement.

       If the USING phrase is specified, the INITIAL clause must not be present in any CD
       entry. (See syntax rule 2 of 13.2.2.3.)

       A COBOL program which may be called by another program within the same run unit is
       normally executed starting with the first nondeclarative paragraph in the program. To
       have execution begin at other than the first nondeclarative statement, the ENTRY
       POINTS phrase is required.




12ΓÇô6                                                                             7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                               Interprogram Communication




         A maximum of 31 data-names may be specified. The combined number of procedure-
         names and items referenced in the APPLY EXDEF clause must not exceed 100. The
         procedure-names may be any section-name or paragraph-name that is not contained in
         the declaratives portion of a program, so long as the procedure-names are not qualified
         and are unique in the first three characters and the last six characters. The specified
         procedure-names must not conflict with the program-name or with entries in the APPLY
         clause. In addition, procedure-names on the ENTRY POINTS phrase must not conflict
         with the procedure-names on the ENTRY POINTS phrase, program-names, or entries in
         the APPLY clause for other programs within the run unit.

         The execution of a CALL or ENTER statement which references procedure-name on the
         ENTRY POINTS phrase or program-name of another program transfers control to the first
         executable statement following the specified name (or the first nondeclarative statement
         in the program).

         The use of entry-point-names does not permit recursive calling of a subprogram.

12.4.2. The CALL Statement
12.4.2.1. Function
         The CALL statement causes control to be transferred from one object program to
         another, within the run unit.

12.4.2.2. General Format
                   identifier-1      USING     data-name-1           data-name-2
         CALL                                                    ,                   ...
                   literal-1                   literal-2             literal-3

                [ ; ON OVERFLOW imperative-statement ]

12.4.2.3. Syntax Rules
         1. Literal-1 must be a nonnumeric literal. This literal must be equal to a program-name
            or a procedure-name specified on the ENTRY POINTS phrase.
         2.   Identifier-1 must be defined as an alphanumeric data item such that its value can be
              a program-name or a procedure-name specified on the ENTRY POINTS phrase.
         3. The USING phrase is included in the CALL statement only if there is a USING phrase
            in the Procedure Division header of the called program and the number of operands
            in each USING phrase must be identical.
         4. Each of the operands in the USING phrase must have been defined as a data item in
            the File Section, Working-Storage Section, Communication Section, or Linkage
            Section, and must have a level-number of 01 or 77. Data-name-1, data-name-2, ...,
            may be qualified when they reference data items defined in the File Section or the
            Communication Section. A maximum of 31 arguments may be specified.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                 12ΓÇô7
Interprogram Communication




12.4.2.4. General Rules
       1. The program whose name is specified by the value of literal-1 or identifier-1 is the
          called program. The program in which the CALL statement appears is the calling
          program.
       2. The execution of a CALL statement causes control to pass to the called program.
       3. A called program is in its initial state the first time it is called within a run unit and the
          first time it is called after a CANCEL to the called program.
           On all other entries into the called program, the state of the program remains
           unchanged from its state when last exited. This includes all data fields, the status
           and positioning of all files, and all alterable switch settings.
       4. If, during the execution of a CALL statement, the available portion of object time
          storage is incapable of accommodating the program specified in the CALL statement
          and the ON OVERFLOW phrase is specified, no action is taken and the
          imperative-statement is executed.

           If this condition exists and the ON OVERFLOW phrase is not specified, a run-time
           diagnostic will be issued.
       5. Called programs may contain CALL statements. However, a called program must
          not contain a CALL statement that directly or indirectly calls the calling program.
       6. The data-names, specified by the USING phrase of the CALL statement, indicate
          those data items available to a calling program that may be referred to in the called
          program. The order of appearance of the data-names in the USING phrase of the
          CALL statement and the USING phrase in the Procedure Division header is critical.
          Corresponding data-names refer to a single set of data which is available to the
          called and calling program. The correspondence is positional, not by name. In the
          case of index-names, no such correspondence is established. Index-names in the
          called and calling program always refer to separate indices.
       7. The CALL statement may appear anywhere within a segmented program. When a
          CALL statement appears in a section with a segmentΓÇônumber greater than or equal
          to 50, that segment is in its last used state when the EXIT PROGRAM statement
          returns control to the calling program.
       8. When identifier-1 is used, an element named C$S333 must be collected with the
          object module. This element must be furnished by the user and contains a list of all
          valid routines to be called. See 18.7.1.

12.4.3. The CANCEL Statement
12.4.3.1. Function

         The CANCEL statement releases the memory areas occupied by the referred to
         program.

12.4.3.2. General Format


          CANCEL         identifier-1       , identifier-2
                                                             ...
                         literal-1          , literal-2


12.4.3.3. Syntax Rules

         1. Literal-1, literal-2, ..., must each be a nonnumeric literal. This literal must be equal to
            a program-name. This literal must not equal a procedure-name specified on the
            ENTRY POINTS phrase.
         2. Identifier-1, identifierΓÇô2, ..., must each be defined as an alphanumeric data item such
            that its value can be a program-name. Identifier-1, identifier-2, ..., must not contain a
            value that equals a procedureΓÇôname specified on the ENTRY POINTS phrase.

12.4.3.4. General Rules

         1. After the execution of a CANCEL statement, the program cancelled no longer has
            any logical relationship to the run unit in which the CANCEL statement appears. A
            subsequently executed CALL statement naming the same program will result in that
            program being initiated in its initial state. The storage areas associated with the
            named programs are released so as to be made available for disposition by the
            operating system. Files referenced in the APPLY EXREF clause are not affected.
         2. A program named in the CANCEL statement must not refer to any program that has
            been called and has not yet executed an EXIT PROGRAM statement.
         3. A logical relationship to a cancelled subprogram can be established only by execution
            of a subsequent CALL statement.
         4. A called program is cancelled either by being referred to as the operand of a
            CANCEL statement or by the termination of the run unit of which the program is a
            member.
         5. No action is taken when a CANCEL statement is executed naming a program that
            has not been called in this run unit or has been called and is at present cancelled.
            Control passes to the next statement.

         6. The CANCEL statement has no effect on Common-Storage data-items.
         7. All files defined in the program named in the CANCEL statement must be closed
            prior to execution of the CANCEL statement.
         8. Any subprogram being cancelled must reside in core prior to the execution of the
            CANCEL statement.

Interprogram Communication




12.4.4. The ENTER Statement
12.4.4.1. Function

        The ENTER statement transfers control to a non-ASCII COBOL program within the same
        run unit.

12.4.4.2. General Format

        Format 1

                         MASM
                         ASM
          ENTER          PL1         literal [ USING { argument-1 } . . . ]
                         FTN


        Format 2

          ENTER   MASM    ΓÇ¥C$INFOΓÇ¥   USING    file-name,    data-name.

12.4.4.3. Syntax Rules
        Format 1
        1. Literal must conform to the requirements for entry-points for the languages
           specified.
        2. A maximum of 31 arguments may be specified. However, if ENTER ASM is used,
           only 11 of these arguments can be from the Linkage Section, and if the program is
           over 65K, only 10 of the arguments can be from the Linkage Section.
        3. Arguments for MASM or ASM may be literals, identifiers, and procedure-names.

           a.   Numeric literals are assumed to be fixed-point binary, right justified in single or
                double precision as necessary. Floating-point literals are assumed to be double
                precision floating-point, and nonnumeric literals are assumed to be ASCII.
           b. Identifiers may be any data items which are referred to in the calling program.
              Level 88 items may not be used as arguments. Subscripts and indexes must be
              integer values.
           c.   Procedure-names should contain at least one nonnumeric character to avoid
                conflict with numeric literal arguments.

        4. Arguments for PL1 may be elementary or group items with DISPLAY,
           COMPUTATIONAL (start on a word boundary and be four or eight bytes in length),
           COMPUTATIONAL-1, COMPUTATIONAL-2, or Exact Binary Usage.
        5. Arguments for FTN may be elementary or group items with DISPLAY,
           COMPUTATIONAL (start on a word boundary and be four bytes in length),
           COMPUTATIONAL-1, or COMPUTATIONAL-2 Usage. The arguments can also be
           COBOL paragraph-names.




12ΓÇô10                                                                               7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                 Interprogram Communication




12.4.4.4. General Rules

         Format 1
         1. The program whose entry-point is specified by the value of the literal is the called
            program; the program in which the ENTER statement appears is the calling program.
         2. Execution of an ENTER statement causes control to pass to the called program.
         3. A called program must not contain a statement that directly or indirectly calls the
            calling program.
         4. See Section 18 for a description of preserving the COBOL environment, calling
            sequences, and the parameter format.
         Format 2
         Refer to 6.1.4 for additional information on this format.

12.4.5. The EXIT PROGRAM Statement
12.4.5.1. Function
         The EXIT PROGRAM statement marks the logical end of a called program.

12.4.5.2. General Format
           EXIT PROGRAM.


12.4.5.3. Syntax Rules
         1. The EXIT PROGRAM statement must appear in a sentence by itself.
         2. The EXIT PROGRAM sentence must be the only sentence in the paragraph.

12.4.5.4. General Rules
         An execution of an EXIT PROGRAM statement in a called program causes control to be
         passed to the calling program. Execution of an EXIT PROGRAM statement in a program
         which is not called behaves as if the statement were an EXIT statement. (See 2.6.10.)
