14.2. Environment Division
14.2.1. InputΓÇôOutput Section
14.2.1.1. The FILEΓÇôCONTROL Paragraph
14.2.1.1.1. Function

        The FILEΓÇôCONTROL paragraph in the INPUT-OUTPUT section specifies file-related
        information.

14.2.1.1.2. General Format

          FILE-CONTROL. [ , file-control-entry ] . . .


14.2.1.2. The File Control Entry
14.2.1.2.1. Function

        The file control entry may specify the order in which logical records are processed by the
        COBOL program.

14.2.1.2.2. General Format

          [ PROCESSING MODE IS RANDOM   [ FOR integer RECORDS ] ]

14.2.1.2.3. General Rules

        1. When PROCESSING MODE IS RANDOM is specified, the logical records are
           processed asynchronously. The integer in the FOR integer RECORDS phrase
           specifies the number of areas allocated to contain logical records. In the random
           processing mode, the COBOL program normally contains one or more USE FOR
           RANDOM PROCESSING declarative sections which access the file. The maximum
           number of asynchronous processing cycles which can be accessing the file
           concurrently is limited to the value of integer in the FOR integer RECORDS phrase. If
           the maximum number of asynchronous processing cycles are executing, and another
           cycle is started, ACS waits until a logical record area becomes available.
        2. When files are asynchronously processed the OPEN and CLOSE statements should
           be executed as part of the main cycle. An exception to this is when they are
           contained in RANDOM PROCESSING declaratives which contain proper logic to
           control the sequence of operations.
        3. The integer in the FOR integer RECORDS phrase represents the maximum number
           of records required for asynchronous cycle processing. An additional record will
           always be assigned for the main cycle.




14ΓÇô4                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                    Asynchronous Processing




         4. The area allocated to contain the logical records is not compiled as part of the object
            program. Rather, the object program is dynamically extended prior to the execution
            of a RANDOM PROCESSING declarative. A logical record area is assigned at this
            time for each file accessed in the declarative section. When the last statement in
            the declarative section has been executed, these logical record areas are released.
            Therefore, an executing COBOL program will only use as much storage area as the
            execution of asynchronous cycles dictates.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                  14ΓÇô5
Asynchronous Processing




14.3. Data Division
14.3.1. The USAGE Clause
14.3.1.1. Function
        The USAGE clause specifies the use and the format of a data item in storage.

14.3.1.2. General Format
          [ USAGE IS ] LOCK


14.3.1.3. Syntax Rules
        1. A lock data item can be referenced explicitly only in a LOCK or UNLOCK statement,
           or in a conditional statement. When appearing in a conditional statement, it is
           meaningful only to test their state, locked or unlocked, which is equivalent to
           nonzero or zero, respectively.
        2. The SYNCHRONIZED, JUSTIFIED, PICTURE, VALUE, and BLANK WHEN ZERO
           clause cannot be used to describe group or elementary items described with the
           USAGE IS LOCK clause.

14.3.1.4. General Rules
        1. The USAGE clause can be written at any level. If the USAGE clause is written at a
           group level, it applies to each elementary item in the group. The USAGE clause of
           an elementary item cannot contradict the USAGE clause of a group to which the
           item belongs.
        2. An elementary item described with the USAGE IS LOCK clause is called a lock data
           item and contains a value of nonzero or zero. The elementary item cannot be a
           conditional variable. If a group item is described with the USAGE IS LOCK clause
           the elementary items in the group are all lock data items. The group itself is not a
           lock data item and cannot be used in the LOCK or UNLOCK statement or in a relation
           condition.
        3. A lock data item can be part of a group which is referred to in a MOVE or input-
           output statement, in which case no conversion will take place.
        4. The external and internal format of an index format of an index data item is one word
           with implicit synchronization and implicit COMPUTATIONAL usage.

14.3.2. File Section
14.3.2.1. The SavedΓÇôArea DescriptionΓÇöComplete Entry Skeleton
14.3.2.1.1. Function

        The SavedΓÇôArea description furnishes information concerning the physical structure and
        attributes of a local storage area required for random processing. Associated with each
        cycle is a copy of a SavedΓÇôArea dedicated to the exclusive use of this cycle. The storage
        occupied by the copy is returned to the dynamic storage pool for reuse upon termination
        of the cycle.


14ΓÇô6                                                                             7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                   Asynchronous Processing




14.3.2.1.2. General Format
           SA   area-name

                      ; AREA CONTAINS    integer-1 RECORDS

                  [   ; WITH RANK OF     integer-2 ]    .

14.3.2.1.3. Syntax Rules

         1. An SA entry is required when random processing is specified.
         2. A level indicator SA is used to identify the beginning of a Saved-Area description
            entry and must precede the unique area-name.
         3. An SA descriptor names the Saved-Area, establishes an upper bound the number of
            copies that can be allocated concurrently, and may specify the saved priority
            component.
         4. The order in which the clauses appear is immaterial.
         5. Saved-Area record descriptions, if any, must immediately follow the Saved-Area
            description for which they apply.
         6. Data records within a Saved-Area represent overlays of the same record area. This
            is in no way altered by the presence of more than one type of data record within the
            Saved-Area.

14.3.2.2. The AREA CONTAINS Clause
14.3.2.2.1. Function

         The AREA CONTAINS clause establishes an upperΓÇôbound to the number of copies that
         can be allocated concurrently.

14.3.2.2.2. General Format

           AREA CONTAINS integer-1 RECORDS

14.3.2.2.3. Syntax Rules

         1. This clause is required in every Saved-Area description entry.
         2. The value of integer-1 must be greater than zero and less than 512.
14.3.2.2.4. General Rules

         Integer-1 specifies the maximum number of copies of the Saved-Area record that can be
         allocated concurrently. If the ACS is requested to allocate one beyond the maximum,
         the current cycle is suspended until another allocated copy is freed by the completion of
         its cycle.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                    14ΓÇô7
Asynchronous Processing




14.3.2.3. The WITH RANK Clause
14.3.2.3.1. Function

        The WITH RANK clause specifies the rank of the associated Saved-Area.

14.3.2.3.2. General Format

          WITH RANK OF integer

14.3.2.3.3. Syntax Rules

        1. The WITH RANK clause is optional.
        2. The value of integer must be less than 512.
14.3.2.3.4. General Rules

        1. If the WITH RANK clause is omitted, a value of zero is assumed for integer.
        2. Cycle priority is computed as the sum of the rank of the Random Processing Section
           being executed and the rank of the associated Saved-Area. The greater the sum of
           the two numbers the higher the priority.

14.3.3. Communication Section
        The PROCESSING MODE IS RANDOM clause may be specified in addition to the other
        clauses that may be specified in a communication description entry. (See 13.2.2.)

14.3.3.1. The PROCESSING MODE Clause
14.3.3.1.1. Function

        The PROCESSING MODE clause is used to allow messages to be randomly processed.
        It specifies the maximum number of CD areas that may be allocated.

14.3.3.1.2. General Format

          [ , PROCESSING MODE IS RANDOM [ FOR integer RECORDS ] ]

14.3.3.1.3. General Rules

        1. PROCESSING MODE IS RANDOM specifies that messages are to be processed
           asynchronously. In this case, the compiler ensures that each PROCESS statement
           specifying a RANDOM PROCESSING declarative referencing the CD will allocate a
           separate CD area to be used for the execution of the declarative.
        2. Integer RECORDS specifies to the compiler the maximum number of CD areas for
           this CD that can be concurrently active. During execution, when all CD areas are
           active, the execution of a process statement referencing this CD causes a wait
           status until a CD area becomes available.




14ΓÇô8                                                                            7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                   Asynchronous Processing




14.4. Procedure Division
14.4.1. The ALL Conditional
14.4.1.1. Function
         The ALL conditional provides a means for testing the current status of asynchronous
         activity with respect to the entire run unit.

14.4.1.2. General Format

         ALL    INACTIVE      FOR     area-name-1
                ACTIVE                section-name-1    ...

14.4.1.3. Syntax Rules
         1. The parameter section-name-1 used as an operand of the ALL statement must be a
            name of a section defined in a USE FOR RANDOM PROCESSING section in a USE
            declarative.
         2. The parameter area-name-1 used as an operand of the ALL statement must be a
            name of Saved-Areas defined by an SA level descriptor in the Data Division of the
            program.

14.4.1.4. General Rules
         1. The ALL conditional uses the named SavedΓÇôAreas and section-name-1 to test for the
            existence of the stated mode (ALL ACTIVE or ALL INACTIVE) with respect to the run
            unit. For the condition to be ΓÇ£trueΓÇ¥ when the ACTIVE option is used, each
            Saved-Area specified must have its maximum number of copies currently allocated
            and each section-name-1 specified must have the maximum number of cycles
            currently being processed; otherwise, the condition is ΓÇ£falseΓÇ¥.
         2. When the INACTIVE option is used, the condition is ΓÇ£falseΓÇ¥ if at least one copy of a
            specified Saved-Area is currently allocated or at least one cycle of a specified
            section-name is currently being processed; otherwise, the condition is ΓÇ£trueΓÇ¥.

14.4.2. The ANY Conditional
14.4.2.1. Function
         The ANY conditional tests the current status of asynchronous activity with respect to the
         entire run unit.

14.4.2.2. General Format

         ANY    INACTIVE      FOR     area-name-1
                ACTIVE                section-name-1    ...




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                14ΓÇô9
Asynchronous Processing




14.4.2.3. Syntax Rules
        1. The parameter section-name-1 used as an operand of the ANY statement must be a
           name of a section defined in a USE FOR RANDOM PROCESSING section in a USE
           declarative.
        2. The parameter area-name-1 used as an operand of the ANY statement must be the
           name of Saved-Areas defined by an SA level descriptor in the Data Division of the
           program.

14.4.2.4. General Rules
        1. The ANY conditional uses the named SavedΓÇôAreas and section-name-1 to test for
           the existence of the stated mode (ANY ACTIVE or ANY INACTIVE) with respect to
           the run unit. For the condition to be ΓÇ£trueΓÇ¥ when the ACTIVE option is used there
           must be at least one copy of a specified Saved-Area currently allocated or at least
           one cycle of the specified section-name-1 currently being processed; otherwise, the
           condition is ΓÇ£falseΓÇ¥.
        2. When the INACTIVE option is used, the condition is ΓÇ£falseΓÇ¥ if the maximum number
           of copies of each specified SavedΓÇôArea is currently allocated and if the maximum
           number of cycles is currently being processed for section-name-1; otherwise, the
           condition is ΓÇ£trueΓÇ¥.

14.4.3. The HOLD Statement
14.4.3.1. Function
        The HOLD statement suspends execution of a cycle until a specified subset of
        progeny-cycles are inactive. (Inactive implies normally terminated, abnormally
        terminated, or never initiated.)

14.4.3.2. General Format
                   ALL
        HOLD         area-name-1      ...
                    section-name-1

14.4.3.3. Syntax Rules
        1. The section-names used as operands of the HOLD statement must be names of
           sections defined in a USE FOR RANDOM PROCESSING section in a USE
           declarative. (See 14.4.7.)
        2. The area-names used as operands of the HOLD statement must be names of
           Saved-Areas defined by an SA level descriptor entry in the Data Division of the
           program. (See 14.3.2.1.)




14ΓÇô10                                                                            7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                    Asynchronous Processing




14.4.3.4. General Rules
         1. The ALL specifies that all cycles initiated from the cycle executing the HOLD
            statement (all progeny cycles) have been completed before any statements
            following the HOLD ALL statement are executed.
         2. When a section-name or area-name is specified all cycles pertaining to the named
            sections or associated with the named savedΓÇôareas and initiated from the cycle
            executing the HOLD statement (and all progeny cycles) have been completed before
            any statements following the HOLD statement are executed.

14.4.4. The LOCK Statement
14.4.4.1. Function
         The LOCK statement provides a means for obtaining exclusive use of a shared resource,
         such as, a shared data item, or procedure overlay area.

14.4.4.2. General Format
           LOCK {identifier-1} . . .


14.4.4.3. Syntax Rule
         Identifier-1 must be defined with a USAGE IS LOCK clause.

14.4.4.4. General Rules
         1. The association of a lock data-item with a shared resource is conceptual in nature,
            and hence, a lock data-item can be considered simply as a 2-position status indicator:
            ON, when locked, and OFF, when unlocked.
         2. When the LOCK statement is executed, all the identifiers are tested in order until a
            previously locked identifier is encountered or all identifiers are found to be unlocked.
            When a previously locked identifier is encountered, the cycle is effectively
            suspended. When the cycle is reactivated, all identifiers are again tested in order.
            After all have been tested and found to be unlocked, each identifier is locked and
            control transfers to the next executable statement following the LOCK statement.

14.4.5. The PROCESS Statement
14.4.5.1. Function
         The PROCESS statement initiates a set of USE procedures under the control of an
         Asynchronous Control System (ACS).

14.4.5.2. General Format
           PROCESS section-name [ [ FROM identifier ] USING area-name ]




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                 14ΓÇô11
Asynchronous Processing




14.4.5.3. Syntax Rules
        1. Section-name specified in the PROCESS statement must be the name of a USE
           procedure defined in the Declarative Section with a USE FOR RANDOM
           PROCESSING clause in its header section. It identifies the Random Processing
           Section to be executed.
        2. The USING phrase is required for programs containing more than one SavedΓÇôArea
           Description.
        3. The area-name must be the name of a Saved-Area description entry (SA) defined in
           the File Section. (See 14.3.2.1.)

14.4.5.4. General Rules
        1. The PROCESS statement causes the named Random Processing Section to be
           executed as an asynchronous USE cycle. Actual commencement of execution for
           the initiated cycle is a function of the Asynchronous Control System. Control for the
           initiating cycle is returned to the next statement following the PROCESS statement.
        2. The cycle which contains the PROCESS statement will be suspended until another
           execution of the named Random Processing Section is completed, if activation of
           this cycle would exceed the maximum number of cycles stated in the FOR integer-2
           CYCLES clause of the named Random Processing Section.
        3. When the optional phrase FROM is used, moving an identifier to the copy of the
           Saved-Area allocated for the cycle initiated by the PROCESS statement takes place
           in accordance with the rules specified for the MOVE statement without the
           CORRESPONDING option.
        4. The PROCESS statement causes the allocation of one copy of the named SavedΓÇô
           Area and one copy of each PROCESSING MODE IS RANDOM or PROCESSING
           MODE IS RANDOM CD stated in the USING clause of the USE FOR RANDOM
           PROCESSING clause for the named Random Processing Section, to be dedicated to
           the exclusive use of the cycle initiated at execution of the PROCESS statement.
           Saved-Area copies are released for reassignment upon completion of the cycle to
           which they were dedicated. If no copies of the SA or of a record area of a
           PROCESSING MODE IS RANDOM file are available, the cycle which has the
           PROCESS statement is suspended until a copy of the record-area or SA is made
           available by completion of another cycle. (See 14.3.2.2.)
        5. Exclusive use of shared data items can be assured only through explicit embedding
           of appropriate LOCK and UNLOCK statements throughout the source language
           programs. Data items which occupy portions of a word in conjunction with a shared
           data item must also be treated as an extension of the shared data item. Therefore,
           shared data items should be either implicitly or explicitly word synchronized.




14ΓÇô12                                                                            7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                   Asynchronous Processing




14.4.6. The UNLOCK Statement
14.4.6.1. Function
         The UNLOCK statement releases exclusive use of a shared resource, such as a shared
         data item or procedure overlay area.

14.4.6.2. General Format
           UNLOCK {identifier-1} . . .


14.4.6.3. Syntax Rules
         Identifier-1 must be defined with a USAGE IS LOCK clause.

14.4.6.4. General Rules
         1. The association of a lock data item with a shared resource is conceptual in nature.
            Therefore, a lock data item can be considered simply as a two position status
            indicator: ON, when locked; and OFF, when unlocked.
         2. When the UNLOCK statement is executed, all locked fields specified are unlocked.
            Control transfers to the next executable statement following the UNLOCK
            statement.

14.4.7. The USE Statement
14.4.7.1. Function
         The USE FOR RANDOM PROCESSING statement identifies a set of procedural
         statements as a Random Processing Section to be processed asynchronously.

14.4.7.2. General Format
         USE FOR RANDOM PROCESSING


                                file-name-1    ...
                      USING
                                cd-name-1


                   [ WITH RANK OF integer-1 ] [ FOR integer-2 CYCLES ] .

14.4.7.3. Syntax Rules
         1. A USE statement, when present, must immediately follow a section header in the
            declaratives section and must be followed by a period followed by a space. The
            remainder of the section must consist of zero, one or more procedural paragraphs
            that define the procedures to be used.
         2. The USE statement itself is never executed. It merely defines the conditions calling
            for the execution of the USE procedures.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                               14ΓÇô13
Asynchronous Processing




        3. The files implicitly or explicitly referenced in a USE statement need not all have the
           same organization or access.
        4. File-name-1 may not be a sort or merge file.
        5. All file-names and cd-names referenced within a Random Processing Section must
           be named in the USING clause whether or not they specify PROCESSING MODE IS
           RANDOM in their descriptions.
        6. The value of integer-1 or integer-2 must be less than 512.

14.4.7.4. General Rules
        1. The WITH RANK phrase specifies the rank of its associated USE procedure.
        2. If the WITH RANK phrase is omitted, a value of zero is assumed for integer-1.
        3. Cycle priority is computed as the sum of the rank of the Random Processing Section
           being executed and the rank of the associated Saved-Area. The greater the sum of
           the two numbers the higher the priority.
        4. The FOR integer-2 CYCLES phrase establishes an upper-bound to the number of
           cycles of the associated USE procedure that can be concurrently active.
        5. If the FOR integer-2 CYCLES phrase is omitted, a value of one is assumed for
           integer-2.
        6. If ACS is requested to activate one more cycle than is stated in the FOR integer-2
           CYCLES phrase, it will suspend that cycle containing the PROCESS statement until
           another cycle of the Random Processing Section is completed.
        7. If the file-name or cd-name contains a PROCESSING MODE IS RANDOM FOR
           integer RECORDS clause, a copy of the record area for this file-name or cd-name is
           allocated for exclusive use of this cycle. This record area will be released for
           reassignment upon completion of the cycle. If ACS is requested to allocate one more
           record area than is stated in the FOR integer RECORDS phrase, the cycle which
           contains the PROCESS statement for this Random Processing Section will be
           suspended.
        8. In the statements of the USE procedure, the execution of an ALTER or PERFORM
           statement affects that particular cycle only; that is, any other cycle of this USE
           procedure is not affected by another concurrent cycle in which an ALTER or
           PERFORM statement is executed.




14ΓÇô14                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
Section 15
IBM Tape Processing


15.1. General
15.1.1. Function
         The IBM Tape Processing module can access records of an IBM formatted tape file in an
         established sequence. The sequence is established as a result of writing the records to
         the file. It also provides for the specification of rerun points and the sharing of storage
         areas among files.

15.1.2. Language Concepts
15.1.2.1. Organization
         Each record of a sequential file except the first has a unique predecessor record,
         and each record except the last has a unique successor record. These
         predecessor-successor relationships are established by the order of WRITE
         statements when the file is created. Once established, the predecessor-successor
         relationships do not change.

15.1.2.2. Access Mode
         In the sequential access mode, the sequence in which records are accessed is the order
         in which the records were originally written.

15.1.2.3. Current Record Pointer
         The current record pointer is a conceptual entity used to specify the next record to be
         accessed within a given file. The concept of the current record pointer has no meaning
         for a file opened in the output mode. The setting of the current record pointer is
         affected only by the OPEN and READ statements.

15.1.2.4. The AT END Condition
         The AT END condition can occur as a result of the execution of a READ statement. For
         details of the causes of the condition, see 15.4.3.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                  15ΓÇô1
IBM Tape Processing




15.2. Environment Division
15.2.1. InputΓÇôOutput Section
15.2.1.1. The FILEΓÇôCONTROL Paragraph
15.2.1.1.1. Function

        The FILEΓÇôCONTROL paragraph in the INPUT-OUTPUT section names each file and
        allows specification of other file-related information.

15.2.1.1.2. General Format

          FILE-CONTROL. {    file-control-entry }      . . .


15.2.1.2. The File Control Entry
15.2.1.2.1. Function

        The file control entry names a file and may specify other file-related information.

15.2.1.2.2. General Format

        SELECT [ OPTIONAL ] file-name

            ASSIGN TO implementor-name-1 [ , implementor-name-2 ] . . .

                            integer-1                   AREA
             ; RESERVE                  ALTERNATE
                            NO                          AREAS

            [ ; ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL ]

            [ ; ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL ]

15.2.1.2.3. Syntax Rules

        1. The SELECT clause must be specified first in the file control entry. The clauses that
           follow the SELECT clause may appear in any order.
        2. Each file described in the Data Division must be named once and only once as
           file-name in the FILEΓÇôCONTROL paragraph. Each file specified in the file control
           entry must have a file description entry in the Data Division.
        3. The implementor-name-1 is UNISERVO∩ú¬.
        4. If the implementor-name-2 is specified, it is a 1 to 12- character name used to link
           the ASCII COBOL file to OS 2200 Executive File Control and should appear on an
           @ASG or @USE statement in the run stream for executing the object program. (See
           15.5).
        5. When implementor-name-2 is not specified, the first 12 characters of the file-name
           are used to link the ASCII COBOL file to the OS 2200 Executive File Control. (See
           15.5).




15ΓÇô2                                                                                7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                          IBM Tape Processing




         6. All recursions of implementor-name-1 and implementor-name-2 are for
            documentation only.
         7. If the ACCESS MODE clause is not specified, the ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL
            clause is implied.
         8. When the ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL clause is not specified, the
            ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL clause is implied.
         9. The OPTIONAL phrase may only be specified for input files. Its specification is
            required for input files that are not necessarily present each time the object program
            is executed.
15.2.1.2.4. General Rules

         1. The ASSIGN clause specifies the association of the file referenced by file-name to a
            storage medium.
         2. The RESERVE clause allows the user to affect the number of input-output areas
            allocated. If the RESERVE clause is not specified or if integer-1 is specified, two
            input-output areas are allocated. If NO is specified, one input-output area is
            allocated.
         3. The ORGANIZATION clause specifies the logical structure of a file. The file
            organization is established at the time a file is created and cannot subsequently be
            changed.
         4. Records in the file are accessed in the sequence dictated by the file organization.
            This sequence is specified by predecessor-successor record relationships
            established by the execution of WRITE statements when the file is created.

15.2.1.3. The IΓÇôOΓÇôCONTROL Paragraph
15.2.1.3.1. Function

         The IΓÇôOΓÇôCONTROL paragraph specifies the points at which rerun is to be established,
         and the storage area which is to be shared by different files.

15.2.1.3.2. General Format

         I-O-CONTROL .


                                                          [ END OF ] REEL
             ; RERUN ON implementor-name       EVERY
                                                          integer-1 RECORDS


                      OF file-name-1   ...


           [ ; SAME [ RECORD ] AREA FOR { file-name-2 } . . . ] . . . .

15.2.1.3.3. Syntax Rules

         1. The IΓÇôOΓÇôCONTROL paragraph is optional.
         2. File-name-1 may be either an input or output file.
         3. The allowable implementorΓÇônames are MASSΓÇôSTORAGE and UNISERVO.


7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                 15ΓÇô3
IBM Tape Processing




        4. More than one RERUN clause may be specified for a given file-name-1, subject to
           the following restrictions:
            a.   When multiple integer-1 RECORDS clauses are specified, no two of them may
                 specify the same file-name-1.
            b. When multiple END OF REEL clauses are specified, no two of them may specify
               the same file-name-1.
        5. The two forms of the SAME clause (SAME AREA, SAME RECORD AREA) are
           considered separately in the following:
            More than one SAME clause may be included in a program. However:
            a.   A file-name must not appear in more than one SAME AREA clause.
            b. A file-name must not appear in more than one SAME RECORD AREA clause.
            c.   If one or more file-names of a SAME AREA clause appear in a SAME RECORD
                 AREA clause, all of the file-names in that SAME AREA clause must appear in
                 that SAME RECORD AREA clause. However, additional file-names not
                 appearing in that SAME AREA clause may also appear in that SAME RECORD
                 AREA clause. The rule that only one of the files mentioned in a SAME AREA
                 clause can be open at any given time takes precedence over the rule that all files
                 mentioned in a SAME RECORD AREA clause can be open at any given time.
        6. The files referenced in the SAME AREA or SAME RECORD AREA clause need not all
           have the same organization or access.
15.2.1.3.4. General Rules

        1. The RERUN clause specifies when and where the rerun information is recorded.
        2. Rerun information is written in a separate file whose file-name is RERUN$. The two
           forms of the RERUN clause are based on the following conditions under which rerun
           points can be established:
            a.   When the END OF REEL clause is used. In this case, the rerun information is
                 written whenever the END OF REEL condition occurs on file-name-1.
            b. When the integer-1 RECORDS is used. In this case, the rerun information is
               written whenever integer-1 records of file-name-1 have been processed.
        3. The SAME AREA clause specifies that two or more files that do not represent sort or
           merge files are to use the same main storage area during processing. The area
           being shared includes all storage area assigned to the files specified; therefore, it is
           not valid to have more than one of the files open at the same time. (See syntax rule
           5c in 15.2.1.3.3.)
        4. The SAME RECORD AREA clause specifies that two or more files are to use the
           same storage area for processing of the current logical record. All of the files may
           be open at the same time. A logical record in the SAME RECORD AREA is
           considered as a logical record of each opened output file whose file-name appears in
           this SAME RECORD AREA clause and of the most recently read input file whose file-
           name appears in this SAME RECORD AREA clause. This is equivalent to an implicit
           redefinition of the area; in other words, records are aligned on the leftmost character
           position.




15ΓÇô4                                                                               7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                             IBM Tape Processing




15.3. Data Division
15.3.1. File Section
         In a COBOL program the file description entry (FD) represents the highest level of
         organization in the File Section. The File Section header is followed by a file description
         entry consisting of a level indicator (FD), a file-name and a series of independent clauses.
         The FD clauses specify the size of the logical and physical records, the presence or
         absence of label records, the value of Unisys defined label items, and the names of the
         data records which comprise the file. The entry itself is terminated by a period.

15.3.2. The File DescriptionΓÇöComplete Entry Skeleton
15.3.2.1. Function
         The file description furnishes information concerning the physical structure,
         identification, and record names pertaining to a given file.

15.3.2.2. General Format
         FD file-name

                                                                          RECORDS
            ; BLOCK CONTAINS       [ integer-1 TO ]     integer-2
                                                                          CHARACTERS

          [ ; RECORD CONTAINS [ integer-3 TO ] integer-4              CHARACTERS ]

                        RECORD IS             STANDARD
            ; LABEL     RECORDS ARE           OMITTED

                                                            data-name-1
            ; VALUE OF      implementor-name-1     IS                        ...
                                                            literal-1


                        RECORD IS
            ; DATA                           data-name-2            ...
                        RECORDS ARE

                                         F
            ; RECORDING MODE IS          U       [ AN ] .
                                         V

15.3.2.3. Syntax Rules
         1. The level indicator FD identifies the beginning of a file description and must precede
            file-name.
         2. The clauses that follow the name of the file are optional in many cases, and their
            order of appearance is immaterial.
         3. One or more record description entries must follow the file description entry.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                   15ΓÇô5
IBM Tape Processing




15.3.3. The BLOCK CONTAINS Clause
15.3.3.1. Function
        The BLOCK CONTAINS clause specifies the size of a physical record.

15.3.3.2. General Format

        BLOCK CONTAINS        [ integer-1 TO ]   integer-2      RECORDS
                                                                CHARACTERS

15.3.3.3. General Rules
        1. This clause is required except when:
            a.   A physical record contains one and only one complete logical record.
            b. RECORDING MODE U is specified.
        2. The size of the physical record may be stated in terms of RECORDS, unless one of
           the following situations exists, in which case the RECORDS phrase must not be
           used.
            a.   The physical record contains padding (area not contained in a logical record).
            b. Logical records are grouped in such a manner that an inaccurate physical record
               size would be implied.
        3. When the word CHARACTERS is specified, the physical record size is specified in
           terms of the number of ASCII character positions required to store the physical
           record, regardless of the types of characters used to represent the items within the
           physical record.
        4. If only integer-2 is shown, it represents the exact size of the physical record.
            If integer-1 and integer-2 are both shown, they refer to the minimum and maximum
            size of the physical record, respectively.

15.3.4. The DATA RECORDS Clause
15.3.4.1. Function
        The DATA RECORDS clause serves only as documentation for the names of data
        records with their associated file.

15.3.4.2. General Format
                   RECORD IS
        DATA                         { data-name-1 } . . .
                   RECORDS ARE

15.3.4.3. Syntax Rules
        Data-name-1 represents the names of the data records and must have 01 level-number
        record descriptions, with the same names, associated with them.




15ΓÇô6                                                                                7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                            IBM Tape Processing




15.3.4.4. General Rules
         The presence of more than one data-name indicates that the file contains more than one
         type of data record. These records may be of different sizes, different formats, etc. The
         order in which they are listed is not significant.

         Conceptually, all data records within a file share the same area. This is in no way altered
         by the presence of more than one type of data record within the file.

15.3.5. The LABEL RECORDS Clause
15.3.5.1. Function
         The LABEL RECORDS clause specifies whether labels are present.

15.3.5.2. General Format

         LABEL      RECORD IS             STANDARD
                    RECORDS ARE           OMITTED

15.3.5.3. Syntax Rules
         This clause is required in every file description entry.

15.3.5.4. General Rules
         1. OMITTED specifies that no explicit labels exist for the file or the device to which the
            file is assigned.
         2. STANDARD specifies that EBCDIC labels exist for the file or the device to which the
            file is assigned.

15.3.6. The RECORD CONTAINS Clause
15.3.6.1. Function
         The RECORD CONTAINS clause specifies the size of data records.

15.3.6.2. General Format
           RECORD CONTAINS [ integer-1 TO ] integer-2 CHARACTERS


15.3.6.3. General Rules
         1. The size of each data record is completely defined within the record description
            entry, therefore this clause is never required. When present, however, the following
            notes apply:
             a.   Integer-2 may not be used by itself unless all the data records in the file have the
                  same size. In this case, integer-2 represents the exact number of characters in
                  the data record. If integer-1 and integer-2 are both shown, they refer to the
                  minimum number of characters in the smallest size data record and the
                  maximum number of characters in the largest size data record, respectively.


7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                    15ΓÇô7
IBM Tape Processing




            b. The size is specified in terms of the number of character positions required to
               store the logical record, regardless of the types of characters used to represent
               the items within the logical record. The size of a record is determined by the
               sum of the number of characters in all fixed length elementary items plus the
               sum of the maximum number of characters in any variable length item
               subordinate to the record. This sum may be different from the actual size of the
               record. See 1.3.3.3.4, 15.3.11, and 15.3.12.

15.3.7. The RECORDING MODE Clause
15.3.7.1. Function
        The RECORDING MODE clause is used to specify IBM OS/360 tape compatibility.

15.3.7.2. General Format
                                    F
        RECORDING MODE IS           U       [ AN ]
                                    V

15.3.7.3. General Rules
        1. The structure of the physical data blocks may be defined by one of the following
           forms:
            a.   The F phrase specifies fixed blocked records.
            b. The U phrase specifies variable length unblocked records.
            c.   The V phrase specifies variable length blocked records.
        2. When the AN option is specified the records are assumed to consist entirely of
           ASCII characters internally and of EBCDIC characters on magnetic tape. The
           character translation is performed when records are transferred to or from storage.
        3. When the AN option is not specified, the following data conversions are performed:
            a.   On input all DISPLAY data items are converted from EBCDIC to ASCII.
            b. On output all DISPLAY data items are converted from ASCII to EBCDIC.
            c.   When a record is read from tape, in every numeric DISPLAY field leading blanks
                 are converted to leading zeros.
            d. Signed numeric DISPLAY fields are written to tape with an overpunched sign on
               the low order digit.
            e. On input all COMPUTATIONAL, COMPUTATIONALΓÇô1, COMPUTATIONALΓÇô2,
               and COMPUTATIONALΓÇô3 data items are converted from IBM OS/360 format to
               OS 2200 ASCII COBOL internal format.
            f.   On output all COMPUTATIONAL, COMPUTATIONALΓÇô1, COMPUTATIONALΓÇô2
                 and COMPUTATIONALΓÇô3 data items are converted from OS 2200 ASCII COBOL
                 internal format to IBM OS/360 format.
            g. Records written to tape are adjusted such that slack bytes are inserted where
               necessary to ensure proper IBM OS/360 alignment.




15ΓÇô8                                                                             7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                              IBM Tape Processing




             h. For RECORDING MODES U and V files, Format 2 of the OCCURS clause is
                allowed in the record description and the following processing is performed:
                   ΓÇó   A data item whose size is variable is expanded on input using the value of
                       the data item referenced by data-name-1 of the OCCURS clause (see 3.2.1).
                   ΓÇó   A data item whose size is variable is compressed on output using the value
                       of the data item referenced by data-name-1 of the OCCURS clause (see
                       3.2.1).
             i.    If a REDEFINES clause is used within a record description, then the original
                   definition is used rather than the redefinition for the purposes of record
                   conversion.
         4. If AN is not specified and the file contains multiple record descriptions, then a record
            selector field within each record description is required. (See 15.3.14.)

15.3.8. The VALUE OF Clause
15.3.8.1. Function
         The VALUE OF clause particularizes the description of an item in the label records
         associated with a file.

15.3.8.2. General Format
                                                     data-name-1
         VALUE OF        implementor-name-1 IS       literal-1          ...


15.3.8.3. Syntax Rules
         1. The allowable implementor-names are FILEΓÇôACCESS, FILEΓÇôID, and PURGEΓÇôDATE.
            These implementor-names have the implied definition of:
                  FILE-ACCESS    PIC    X.
                  FILE-ID        PIC    X(17).
                  PURGE-DATE     PIC    9(6).

         2. Data-name-1 should be qualified when necessary, but cannot be subscripted or
            indexed, nor can they be items described with the USAGE IS INDEX clause.
         3. Data-name-1 must be in the Working-Storage Section.
         4. Data-name-1 must be described as USAGE DISPLAY.

15.3.8.4. General Rules
         1. For an input file, the appropriate label routine checks to see if the value of
            implementor-name-1 is equal to the value of literal-1 or of data-name-1,
            whichever has been specified. (See 15.4.2 and Appendix E.)
             For an output file, at the appropriate time the value of implementor-name-1 is made
             equal to the value of literal-1 or of a data-name-1, whichever has been specified.
             (See 15.4.2 and Appendix E.)
         2. A figurative constant may be substituted in the format wherever a literal is specified.

15.3.9. The Record DescriptionΓÇöComplete Entry Skeleton
        A record description consists of a set of data description entries that describe the
        characteristics of a particular record. Each data description entry consists of a
        level-number followed by a data-name, if required, followed by a series of
        independent clauses as required. A record description has a hierarchical structure
        and therefore the clauses used with an entry may vary considerably, depending
        upon whether or not it is followed by subordinate entries. The structure of a
        record description is defined in 1.3.3.3.2.

15.3.9.1. Function
        A data description entry specifies the characteristics of a particular item of data.

15.3.9.2. General Format
        Format 1
                        data-name-1
        level-number                        [ ; REDEFINES data-name-2 ]
                        FILLER

                PICTURE
           ;                  IS character-string
                PIC


                                  COMPUTATIONAL
                                  COMP
                                  COMPUTATIONAL-1
                                  COMP-1
           ; [ USAGE IS ]         COMPUTATIONAL-2
                                  COMP-2
                                  COMPUTATIONAL-3
                                  COMP-3
                                  DISPLAY
                                  DISP


                SYNCHRONIZED               LEFT
           ;    SYNC                       RIGHT

                JUSTIFIED
           ;    JUST                  RIGHT


        [ ; BLANK WHEN ZERO ]


                VALUE IS                            THROUGH
           ;                        literal-1                      literal-2      ...
                VALUES ARE                          THRU


        [ ; RANK IS integer-1 ] .

        Format 2

        66 data-name-1 ; RENAMES data-name-2             THROUGH        data-name-3       .
                                                         THRU



15ΓÇô10                                                                                   7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                          IBM Tape Processing




         Format 3
         88 condition-name ;   VALUE IS       literal-1     THROUGH         literal-2
                               VALUES ARE                   THRU


                , literal-3    THROUGH      literal-4     ... .
                               THRU

15.3.9.3. Syntax Rules
         1. The clauses may be written in any order with two exceptions. The data-name-1 or
            FILLER clause must immediately follow the level-number. The REDEFINES clause,
            when used, must immediately follow the data-name-1 clause.
         2. The PICTURE clause must be specified for every elementary item except floatingΓÇô
            point data items, in which case use of this clause is prohibited.
         3. The words THRU and THROUGH are equivalent.

15.3.9.4. General Rules
         Format 1
         1. A PICTURE character-string containing one or more 1ΓÇÖs is not allowed.
         2. The RANK, SYNCHRONIZED, USAGE, and VALUE (in the File Section) clauses are
            described in this section. (See 15.3.10 for the RANK clause, 15.3.11 for the
            SYNCHRONIZED clause, 15.3.12 for the USAGE clause, and 15.3.13 for the VALUE
            clause.)
         3. Excluding the restrictions listed in the previous General Rules, the elements shown
            in the General Format are documented in 2.5.2.
         Format 2 and Format 3
         4. See 2.5.2.

15.3.10. The RANK Clause
15.3.10.1. Function
         The purpose of the RANK clause is to increase the efficiency of the process of record
         selection.

15.3.10.2. General Format
           RANK IS [ integer-1 ]


15.3.10.3. Syntax Rules
         1. The RANK clause is optional.
         2. The RANK clause can only be used in the description of a record selector. Record
            selectors are described in 15.3.14.
         3. Integer-1 is an unsigned integer in the range 1 through 63.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                              15ΓÇô11
IBM Tape Processing




15.3.10.4. General Rules
        1. When the RANK clause is omitted, a value of 63 is assumed for the record selector.
        2. When two or more record selectors in the same record description have the same
           RANK, the textual order determines the order in which the selectors are tested.
        3. When a record description contains multiple record selectors, the value of the RANK
           assigned to each record selector need not be consecutive.
        4. When a record description contains more than one record selector, the order in
           which the record selectors are tested is determined by the RANK of each selector.
           Record selectors of rank n are tested before any record selector of rank n + 1; for
           example, RANK 1 has a higher precedence than a record selector of RANK 2.
        5. When a record description contains only one record selector, the RANK clause is
           permitted but it has no meaning.

15.3.11. The SYNCHRONIZED Clause
15.3.11.1. Function
        The SYNCHRONIZED clause specifies the alignment of an elementary item on the
        natural boundaries of the computer main storage when IBM OS/360 allocation and
        alignment rules apply.

15.3.11.2. General Format
          SYNCHRONIZED            LEFT
           SYNC                   RIGHT

15.3.11.3. Syntax Rules
        1. This clause may only appear with an elementary item.
        2. SYNC is an abbreviation for SYNCHRONIZED.

15.3.11.4. General Rules
        1. A full description of data allocation and alignment may be found in 15.3.15.
        2. This clause specifies that the subject data item is to be aligned in memory such that
           no other data item occupies any of the character positions between the leftmost and
           rightmost natural boundaries delimiting this data item. If the number of character
           positions required to store this data item is less than the number of character
           positions between those natural boundaries, the unused character positions (or
           portions thereof) must not be used for any other data item. Such unused character
           positions, however, are included in:
            a.   The size of any group items to which the elementary item belongs; and
            b. The character positions redefined when this data item is the object of a
               REDEFINES clause.
        3. The LEFT and RIGHT phrases serve only for documentation.




15ΓÇô12                                                                             7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                          IBM Tape Processing




         4. The effect of the SYNCHRONIZED phrase and the USAGE clause on the alignment
            of elementary data items is summarized in the following table:


                              Usage                     Alignment

                  COMPUTATIONAL (1ΓÇô 4 digits)    Half Word boundary
                  COMPUTATIONAL (5 ΓÇô18 digits)   Word boundary
                  COMPUTATIONALΓÇô1                Word boundary
                  COMPUTATIONALΓÇô2                Double-Word boundary
                  COMPUTATIONALΓÇô3                Quarter-Word boundary
                  DISPLAY                        Quarter-Word boundary


         5. Whenever a SYNCHRONIZED item is referenced in the source program, the original
            size of the item, as shown in the PICTURE clause, is used in determining any action
            that depends on size, such as justification, truncation, or overflow.
         6. If the data description of an item contains the SYNCHRONIZED clause and an
            operational sign, the sign of the item appears in the normal operational sign position,
            regardless of whether the item is SYNCHRONIZED LEFT or SYNCHRONIZED
            RIGHT.
         7. When the SYNCHRONIZED clause is specified in a data description entry of a data
            item that also contains an OCCURS clause, or in a data description entry of a data
            item subordinate to a data description entry that contains an OCCURS clause, then:
             a.    Each occurrence of the data item is SYNCHRONIZED.
             b. Any implicit FILLER generated for other data items within that same table are
                generated for each occurrence of those data items.
         8. The elementary items associated with this clause are handled as follows:
             a.    Any necessary generation of implicit FILLER, if the elementary item immediately
                   preceding an item containing the SYNCHRONIZED clause does not terminate at
                   a word boundary, is not included as part of the elementary item. Such
                   automatically generated FILLER positions are included in:
                   ΓÇó   The size of any group to which the FILLER item belongs; and
                   ΓÇó   The number of character positions allocated when the group item of which
                       the FILLER item is a part appears as the object of a REDEFINES clause.
         9. In the absence of the SYNCHRONIZED clause, the ASCII COBOL compiler will align
            data items on the next available quarter-word boundary.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                15ΓÇô13
IBM Tape Processing




15.3.12. The USAGE Clause
15.3.12.1. Function
        The USAGE clause specifies the format of a data item in the computer storage.

15.3.12.2. General Format
                              COMPUTATIONAL
                              COMP
                              COMPUTATIONAL-1
                              COMP-1
        [ USAGE IS ]          COMPUTATIONAL-2
                              COMP-2
                              COMPUTATIONAL-3
                              COMP-3
                              DISPLAY
                              DISP

15.3.12.3. Syntax Rules
        1. The PICTURE character-string of a COMPUTATIONAL, and COMPUTATIONAL-3
           item can contain only 9ΓÇÖs, the operational sign character ΓÇ£SΓÇ¥, the implied decimal
           point character ΓÇ£VΓÇ¥, and one or more PΓÇÖs. (See 2.5.7.)
        2. COMP, COMPΓÇôn, and DISP are abbreviations for COMPUTATIONAL,
           COMPUTATIONALΓÇôn, and DISPLAY, respectively.
        3. COMPUTATIONALΓÇô1, and COMPUTATIONALΓÇô2 usage specifications may not
           appear in a data description which has a PICTURE clause, because the computer
           storage format of these items is fixed.

15.3.12.4. General Rules
        1. A full description of data allocation and alignment may be found in 15.3.15.
        2. The USAGE clause can be written at any level. If the USAGE clause is written at a
           group level, it applies to each group or elementary item in the group. The USAGE
           clause of an elementary item cannot contradict the USAGE clause of a group to
           which the item belongs.
        3. If the group usage is DISPLAY or COMPUTATIONAL, the group is considered to be
           an alphanumeric string of ASCII characters.
        4. If the USAGE clause is not specified on a group item, the group is considered to be
           an alphanumeric string of ASCII characters.
            If the USAGE clause is not specified for an elementary item, or for any group to
            which the item belongs, the usage is implicitly DISPLAY.
        5. This clause specifies the manner in which a data item is represented in the storage
           of a computer. It does not affect the use of the data item, although the
           specifications for some statements in the Procedure Division may restrict the
           USAGE clause of the operands referred to. The USAGE clause may affect the radix
           or type of character representation of the item.




15ΓÇô14                                                                             7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                           IBM Tape Processing




         6. A COMPUTATIONAL or COMPUTATIONALΓÇôn item is capable of representing a
            value to be used in computations and must be numeric. If a group item is described
            as COMPUTATIONAL or COMPUTATIONALΓÇôn, the elementary items in the group
            are COMPUTATIONAL or COMPUTATIONALΓÇôn. The group item itself is not
            COMPUTATIONAL or COMPUTATIONALΓÇôn (cannot be used in computations).
         7. The USAGE IS DISPLAY clause indicates that the format of the data is a standard
            data format.

15.3.13. The VALUE Clause
15.3.13.1. Function
         The VALUE clause is used to specify a record selector. (See 15.3.14.)

15.3.13.2. General Format
            VALUE IS                          THROUGH
                                literal-1                     literal-2      ...
            VALUES ARE                        THRU

15.3.13.3. Syntax Rules
         1. The words THRU and THROUGH are equivalent.
         2. The VALUE clause cannot be stated for any items whose size is variable (see 3.2.1).
         3. A signed numeric literal must have associated with it a signed numeric PICTURE
            character-string.
         4. All numeric literals in a VALUE clause of an item must have a value that is within the
            range of values indicated by the PICTURE clause, and not have a value that would
            require truncation of nonzero digits. Nonnumeric literals in a VALUE clause of an
            item must not exceed the size indicated by the PICTURE clause.

15.3.13.4. General Rules
         1. The VALUE clause must not conflict with other clauses in the data description of the
            item or in the data description within the hierarchy of the item. The following rules
            apply:
             a.   If the category of the item is numeric, all literals in the VALUE clause must
                  be numeric. The literal is aligned according to the standard alignment rules.
                  (See 1.3.3.3.6.)
             b. If the category of the item is alphabetic, alphanumeric, alphanumeric
                edited, or numeric edited, all literals in the VALUE clause must be
                nonnumeric literals. The literal is aligned as if the data item had been
                described as alphanumeric. (See 1.3.3.3.6.)
         2. A figurative constant may be substituted wherever a literal is specified.
         3. Wherever the THRU phrase is used, literal-1 must be less than literal-2.
         4. The VALUE clause must not be stated in a data description entry that contains an
            OCCURS clause, or in an entry that is subordinate to an entry containing an OCCURS
            clause.



7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                 15ΓÇô15
IBM Tape Processing




        5. The VALUE clause must not be stated in a data description entry that contains a
           REDEFINES clause, or in an entry that is subordinate to an entry containing a
           REDEFINES clause.
        6. If the VALUE clause is used in an entry at the group level, the literal must be a
           figurative constant or a nonnumeric literal. The VALUE clause cannot be stated at
           the subordinate levels within this group.
        7. The VALUE clause must not be written for a group containing items with
           descriptions including JUSTIFIED, SYNCHRONIZED, or USAGE (other than USAGE
           IS DISPLAY).

15.3.14. Record Selector Fields
        A record selector field is identified to the compiler by the appearance of a VALUE clause
        in the record description. (See 15.3.13.)

        When the file is read, the record selectors are tested to determine which record
        conversion must be performed. The record selectors in the first record are tested; if any
        of the selectors fail the next record is considered. If all the record selectors match, the
        first record description is chosen. This process is repeated for all the data descriptions,
        until a record description is encountered, all of whose selectors match. If no record
        description can be chosen, a diagnostic is issued.

        In any given record description, the record selectors are listed in their textual order. This
        ordering can be changed by using the RANK clause. (See 15.3.10.)

        The RANK clause does not affect the record description chosen; its purpose is to
        increase the efficiency of the record selection process.

        The number of record selectors in any single record description must not exceed 63.
        Each record description in a given file description need not contain the same number of
        selectors. In addition, the selectors need not be in the same position (internal or
        external) in each record description, and they need not have the same USAGE or
        PICTURE. However, it is the userΓÇÖs responsibility to ensure that this does not lead to
        inadvertent record selection.




15ΓÇô16                                                                                7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                                                    IBM Tape Processing




15.3.15. Data Allocation
                Data allocations for items of various usages differ between OS 2200 ASCII COBOL and
                IBM OS/360 COBOL internal allocation. To provide greater compatibility with the IBM
                OS/360 allocation scheme, OS 2200 ASCII COBOL provides several compiler options
                which allow for the handling and allocation of data items according to IBM OS/360
                COBOL or OS 2200 ASCII COBOL allocation rules without a change in the source
                program. These options may be specified in the Extra Options field of the @ACOB
                processor call statement. Following are the Extra Options and their descriptions:

                      Extra                                                     Description
                     Option
                           A             Use standard OS 2200 allocation rules for RECORDING MODE F, U, and V
                                         (EBCDIC) records.
                           B             Allocate COMPUTATIONALΓÇô3 fields internally as DISPLAY fields outside
                                         RECORDING MODE F, U, and V records.
                           C             Use EBCDIC allocation and alignment rules outside the File Section for
                                         DISPLAY, COMPUTATIONAL, COMPUTATIONALΓÇô1 and
                                         COMPUTATIONALΓÇô2 fields.

                Table 15-1 summarizes conditions under which IBM OS/360 COBOL or OS 2200 ASCII
                COBOL allocation and alignment rules apply. Table 15-2 describes the meaning and
                internal allocation of USAGE clauses. Table 15-3 gives the alignment of these clauses.


                                  Table 15-1. Allocation and Alignment Rules

                                              File Section                                          Non-File Section
  Options
  specified
  in Extra                Recording Mode F, U,                     Non-Recording Mode
  Options
                             and V Records                         F, U, and V Records
  field of
  @ ACOB        USAGE DISPLAY    USAGE                   USAGE DISPLAY    USAGE           USAGE DISPLAY    USAGE
  processor     COMPUTATIONAL,   COMPUTATIONAL-3         COMPUTATIONAL,   COMPUTATIONAL-3 COMPUTATIONAL,   COMPUTATIONAL-3
  call          COMPUTATIONAL-1,                         COMPUTATIONAL-1,                 COMPUTATIONAL-1,
  statement     COMPUTATIONAL-2                          COMPUTATIONAL-2                  COMPUTATIONAL-2
