18.7.2.7. Procedure Name Arguments
         If procedure-name arguments are being passed to a non-COBOL called program, the
         called program has to be modified in the area referencing the procedure-name
         parameters. An X-register is loaded with the program BDI and the base I-bank address.
         The parameter contains a pointer to the X-register in S3 and the procedure-name offset
         in H2. When referencing the procedure-name, H2 of the X-register pointed to by S3 of
         the parameter is added to H2 of the parameter to form the address of the procedure-
         name. The BDI for the procedure-name is found in H1 of the X-register referenced by S3
         of the parameter. An example of a CALL follows:

           CALL "sub" USING DΓÇôN P1.

         where "sub" is the non-COBOL subprogram, D-N is a data-name argument, and P1 is a
         procedure-name argument. The code generated for this CALL is:

                   L,U     Xa,$LCB(1)          . address 0 control counter 1
           $(1).                               . this address gets reloaded to the
                                               . first I-bank address
                   LXI,U   Xa,BDI$
                   L,U     A0,PARAMS
                   LXI,U   X11,BDICALL$+sub
                   IBJ$    X11,sub
           $(8).
           PARAMS.
                  +        C$Bsub,2
                  +        0,address           . address of DΓÇôN
                  +        Xa, offset          . offset of P1
           $(1).

         where Xa is the X-register (usually X10) used for basing the procedure-name, address is
         the address of the data-name argument, and offset is the relative offset from the I-bank
         base address where the procedure-name argument is found.

18.7.3. Non-COBOL Programs Calling ASCII COBOL Programs
18.7.3.1. Considerations for Entering ASCII COBOL Programs
         An ASCII COBOL program, when entered, must have the COBOL environment
         established either by being called from an ASCII COBOL program or via the mechanism
         described in 18.7.3.2. Upon entry to the program, a storage area called the Compiler
         Temporary Area (CTA) will be allocated by the run-time library. If the called program
         contains IΓÇôO statements, a File Directory and storage area called the Operations Control
         Block (OCB) will also be allocated by the run-time library. This allocation takes place
         upon the first entry to the called program per cycle and the area remains for the duration
         of the cycle. Hence, the first call on a called program has much more overhead than
         subsequent calls.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                18ΓÇô27
System Interface




        When the 4 Extra Option is present, the CTA, File Directory, and OCB areas are allocated
        upon entering a called program and deallocated upon exit. Hence, the storage area
        needed for these tables is in existence only for the time spent in the program. This
        option is useful for low-use called programs. Use of this option has the following
        restrictions: ALTER in a called program is in its initial state upon each entry to the called
        program. If the called program contains PROCESS or EXDEF file statements, it cannot
        be collected in an overlay segment. The called program cannot be the entry point to an
        HVTIP bank.

        Files defined in the called program must be closed upon exit if the called program is in an
        overlay, and the segment is overlaid before the next call to the called program.

18.7.3.2. Establishing the ASCII COBOL Environment
        Before and after execution of a run that contains ASCII COBOL programs, certain ASCII
        COBOL/System interface programs must be executed. The purpose of this code, in
        addition to providing a system interface, is to initialize the ASCII COBOL execution
        environment.

        The appropriate code is generated for all ASCII COBOL programs which are not
        identifiable as ASCII COBOL called programs. (The presence of the V option on an
        @ACOB processor call statement or a USING or ENTRY clause on the PROCEDURE
        DIVISION header suppresses generation of this code.) The interface code is
        automatically executed for ASCII COBOL main programs specified as such to the
        Collector.

        When ASCII COBOL is called by an ASM main program, registers A4, A5, R11, and R12
        must be saved at the beginning of execution of the main program and restored before
        the interface prologue routine is called.

        Once the interface prologue has been executed, the ASCII COBOL environment is
        established and it is the userΓÇÖs responsibility to preserve it. Preservation includes the
        saving and restoring of all registers, maintaining the processor state word, and the
        contents of system interrupt trap locations, etc.

        Thus, when an ASCII COBOL called program is invoked and the main program is not an
        ASCII COBOL program, the user must ensure that this necessary initialization has been
        performed. The simplest solution is to always have an ASCII COBOL main program, or
        to insert the appropriate calls in an assembly language main program. Whichever way is
        selected, the initialization must be performed once and only once for a run unit which
        contains one or more collected ASCII COBOL programs.




18ΓÇô28                                                                                7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                             System Interface




         If the assembly language main program method is used, the following sequence:

           PP$   FORM      10,4,4,18
           P     PROC
           IBJ$* NAME.
                 PP$       IBJ$,P(1,1),0,P(1,2)
                 END
           $(1).
                 L,U       A3,TAG
                 LXI,U     X11,BDICALL$+C$S31A
                 IBJ$      X11,C$S31A
           $(8).
           TAG.
                 +         0,C$S300
           $(1).
                 LXI,U     X11,BDICALL$+C$S410
                 IBJ$      X11,C$S410        . not necessary for FTN or PL/I main program

         must be executed as a run unit interface prologue and:

                   LXI,U   X11,BDICALL$+C$S320
                   IBJ$    X11,C$S320          . only necessary at program termination

         must be executed as a run unit interface epilogue.

         If users intend to invoke PADS during execution of their programs, they must preserve
         the values that were set in registers A4, A5, R1-R3, and R11-R15 when the programs
         were loaded by the operating system (see 11.5).

18.7.3.3. Calling Sequence
         Assuming that the ASCII COBOL environment is created and maintained, ASCII COBOL
         programs may be called with the following calling sequence:

           $(1).
                      L,U   A0,address of parameters
                      LXI,U X11,BDICALL$+program-id or entry-point-name
                      IBJ$  X11,program-id or entryu-point-name
           $(8).
           parameters.
                     +      C$Bprogid, number of parameters
                     +      address of parameter1
                     +      address of parameter2
                     .
                     .
                     .
                     +      address of parametern
           $(1).

         C$Bprogid is a reference to an entry-point in the called programΓÇÖs D-bank and is the
         name derived from the I-bank entry-point (program-id or entry-point-name). For ASCII
         COBOL called programs, the compiler will define this entry-point in the called programΓÇÖs
         D-bank. This allows called programs to utilize based D-bank references and is the
         technique used to pass the called programΓÇÖs D-bank from the calling bank to the called
         program common bank.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                               18ΓÇô29
System Interface




        C$Bprogid is derived from the entry-point (program-id or entry-point-name). If the entry-
        point is nine or less characters in length, the entire entryΓÇôpoint is appended to C$B. If
        the entry-point is greater than nine characters, the first three and last six characters are
        appended to C$B.

        The symbol n represents the number of parameters being passed. It must be greater
        than or equal to zero and less than 32.

18.7.3.4. Parameter Format
        The parameter addresses are constructed in the following form:

                 0                      index        0                        u

  0                          11 12              17 18 19 20                                       35

        where:
        u
            is either a relocatable address of the argument item or actual offset from a base
            index.

        index
            is a number from 0 through 26. If index is 0, u is the address of the argument.
            Otherwise, index indicates the register (1 = X1, 2 = X2, 3 = X3, 4 = X4, 5 = X5,
            ...,18 = A6, 19 = A7, 20 = A8, 21 = A9, 22 = A10, 23 = A11, 24 = A12, 25 = A13,
            26 = A14) that contains the base address needed to compute the actual location
            of the argument as follows:
                 Actual location of argument = u + contents of the register indicated by index

        Other bits in the word are zero.

18.8. Executive Request Call Statements
18.8.1. Call ER ACSF$
         This feature provides a means of issuing an Executive Request (ER) to ACSF$ directly
         from a COBOL program. This is done via a CALL statement to the entry point ERACSF$.
         The ER packet is established and initialized within the COBOL program and passed by
         the USING clause in a CALL statement. Use of this feature assumes a knowledge of the
         ER being used as well as what is expected in the packet. The CALL has the form:

           CALL "ERACSF$" USING data-name-1,data-name-2[,data-name-3]

         where:
         data-name-1
            contains the ACSF$ image defined as PIC X up to 80 characters.

         data-name-2
            contains the returned status word defined as PIC S1(36).

         data-name-3
            contains the size in words of the ACSF$ image defined as PIC 9(10) COMP.

         Data-name-3 must be specified if the ACSF$ image defined as data-name-1, is less than
         80 characters, unless the ACSF$ image contained in data-name-1 is terminated by the
                              .
         character sequence ' ' .

         For an explanation of the CSF$ Executive Request Status Codes, see the OS 2200 Exec
         System Software Executive Requests Programming Reference Manual.

18.8.2. Call ER SYMB$
         This implementation allows for the initial language interface with the 777-printer. The
         interface is performed by issuing an ER to SYMB$ directly from a COBOL program. This
         is done via a CALL statement to the entry point ERSYMB$. The SYMB$ packet must be
         established and initialized within the COBOL program and passed by the USING clause
         in a CALL statement. Use of this feature requires a knowledge of the ER being used as
         well as what is expected in the packet. The CALL has the form:

           CALL ΓÇÿERSYMB$ΓÇÖ USING data-name-1,data-name-2[,data-name-3]

         where:

         data-name-1
            is the SYMB$ packet as required by the ΓÇÿSYMB$ΓÇÖ ER. See the OS 2200 Exec
            System Software Executive Requests Programming Reference Manual for packet
            description.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                             18ΓÇô31
System Interface




        data-name-2
           is the area to be used as the image-address. This address will be placed in H2 of
           word 4 of SYMB$ packet.

        data-name-3
           is the area to be used as the image-address. This address will be placed in H2 or
           word 010 of the SYMB$ packet. For W$R$ function only.

18.8.3. Call ER ΓÇÿERERR$ΓÇÖ
        This feature provides a means of issuing an ER to ERR$ directly from a COBOL program.
        If PADS was collected with the absolute, PADS is invoked instead of issuing an ER to
        ERR$. The CALL has the form:
          CALL ΓÇÿERERR$ΓÇÖ.


18.8.4. Call ER ΓÇÿEREABT$ΓÇÖ
        This feature provides a means of issuing an ER to EABT$ directly from a COBOL
        program. If PADS was collected with the absolute, PADS is invoked instead of issuing
        an ER to EABT$. The CALL has the format:
          CALL ΓÇÿEREABT$ΓÇÖ.

18.9. Current Date Service Routine (C$CURDATE)
         The ASCII COBOL current date service routine (C$CURDATE) provides a method to
         obtain the current date with a 4-digit year in the format YYYYMMDD. A 4-digit year can
         also be obtained from the ACCEPT statement (see 2.6.4). The interface to this
         C$CURDATE service routine is:
           CALL   ΓÇÖC$CURDATEΓÇÖ USING   data-name-1

         where data-name-1 is described as a PIC 9(8) USAGE DISPLAY or PIC X(8) USAGE
         DISPLAY data item.

18.10. Messages to the Operator Console
18.10.1. ACCEPT . . . FROM CONSOLE
        While running in the batch mode, an ACCEPT command causes a console message:
          "ENTER DATA"-----

        for every 50 characters required (see 2.6.4). Each message requires the addition of 50
        characters for input.

18.10.2. Blank Tape
        A blank tape, assigned without a specified reel number, which is required to be labelled,
        causes a console message ANSWER WITH REEL NO. ON device. Any 6-character reply is
        accepted.

18.10.3. DISPLAY . . . UPON CONSOLE
        While running in the batch mode, a DISPLAY command causes a console message for
        every 50 characters displayed (see 2.6.8.)

18.10.4. Unlabeled Tape
        An ER TLBL$ request on an output tape reel that is not 8ΓÇôbit labeled causes the
        following operatorΓÇÖs console message to be issued:

          LOAD PROPERLY LABELLED REEL ////// file-name AE

        The parameter ////// specifies the logical device name on which the prelabeled reel is to
        be mounted. The file-name is the external file name specified in the ASSIGN clause for
        the file.

        The operator is given an opportunity to mount a properly labeled tape. The operator may
        then respond with an ΓÇ£AΓÇ¥ or and ΓÇ£EΓÇ¥. A response of ΓÇ£AΓÇ¥ causes the ER TLBL$ request
        to be issued again. A response of ΓÇ£EΓÇ¥ causes a diagnostic message 1161A to be issued
        and the cycle to abort.

18.10.5. VALUE OF CARTRIDGEΓÇôID
        If a file has specified a VALUE OF CARTRIDGEΓÇôID clause, execution of either the OPEN
        statement for a nonreport file or the INITIATE statement for a report file may cause the
        following console messages:
          sname xx IN,yy REQUESTED USE IN? YN

          sname MOUNT CARTRIDGE yy A

        A complete description of these messages may be found in OS 2200 Exec System
        Software Operations Reference Manual (7831 0281).




18ΓÇô34                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                             System Interface




18.10.6. VALUE OF FORMSΓÇôREQUEST
         If a file has specified a VALUE OF FORMSΓÇôREQUEST clause, execution of either the
         OPEN statement for a nonreport file or the INITIATE statement for a report file causes
         the following operators console message:

           X ΓÇô SPECIAL FORMS REQ

         where x is the 24-character alphanumeric field specified in the VALUE OF
         FORMSΓÇôREQUEST clause. The field may not contain any periods.

Section 19
Collection of Programs


19.1. General
         This section discusses the ASCII COBOL compiler element naming conventions and
         ASCII COBOL program collection methods and restrictions. For a discussion on TIP
         collection considerations, see Section 21.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                               19ΓÇô1
Collection of Programs




19.2. Element Naming Conventions
        The ASCII COBOL compiler produces one relocatable element for nonsegmented main
        programs, two relocatable elements for subprograms, and several relocatable elements
        and a symbolic MAP element for segmented main programs. In all cases the compiler
        produces external symbols that are unique. They are constructed using the relocatable
        output (RO) field of the processor call statement.

        The external symbols and the element names of segmented programs are constructed
        as follows. Truncate RO using the leftmost six characters, or if RO is less than six
        characters, ΓÇ£$ΓÇ¥ fill to the right for a total of six characters. The resulting six-character
        symbol [SYMB] is concatenated with six characters supplied by the compiler. [SYMB]
        must be unique to avoid duplicate name problems.

19.2.1. Main Programs
        For main programs, one relocatable binary element is created with the name RO. In
        addition, four external symbols are defined. They are: [SYMB]C$MCBL, [SYMB]C$CTAL,
        [SYMB]C$MENT, and [SYMB]C$EPLG.

19.2.2. Segmented Programs
        For segmented programs, the RO field is used as the name of the MAP symbolic. If the
        MAP symbolic name is the same as the source input (SI) or source output (SO), it is
        given the version name ΓÇÿMAPΓÇÖ.

        A relocatable element is produced for the main segment, for the data, and for each
        segment. (There may not be a one-for-one correspondence between the number of
        elements and the number of segments. The actual number depends on how the source
        program is arranged.) The relocatables are placed in the same file as the RO field and
        are named as follows:
          [SYMB] MAIN
          [SYMB] SYSDTA
          [SYMB] xxxxxx

        where one [SYMB] xxxxxx is created for each segment. The value of xxxxxx is unique
        and is determined by the compiler by numbering the procedure and section names in a
        program from 0 to n (where n is the last procedure in a program). The parameter xxxxxx
        is the n associated with the section name that defines the section.

        The four external symbols defined for nonsegmented programs are defined for
        segmented programs as well. In addition, sets of the following are defined:
         Entry-Point
            [SYMB]Pxxxxx      in each element

         Segment fall through
            [SYMB]Sxxxxx      in prologue




19ΓÇô2                                                                                  7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                        Collection of Programs




          Location counter
             [SYMB]Lxxxxx

         where xxxxx is unique and determined by the compiler by numbering the procedure and
         section names in a program from 0 to n (where n is the last procedure in a program).
         The parameter xxxxx is the n associated with the section name that defines the section.

         Segment names for the MAP are created as follows:
           BASOOO       for base segment
           OVRyyy       for fixed overlayable segment
           INDzzz       for independent segment
         where yyy and zzz are the priority number.

19.2.3. Subprograms
         For subprograms, two relocatable elements are created. One element contains
         exclusively I-bank and is given the name in the RO field. The other element
         contains exclusively D-bank and is given the name [SYMB] SYSDTA.

         The I-bank element contains an entryΓÇôpoint for the PROGRAMΓÇôID name plus one
         for each name on the WITH ENTRY POINTS clause. Also, the epilog entry-point is
         defined as [SYMB]C$EPLG.

         The D-bank element contains an entryΓÇôpoint which is defined at relative address 0
         of control counter 8, C$B[ENTRYΓÇôPOINT]. [ENTRYΓÇôPOINT] is derived from each
         PROCEDURE DIVISION entry-point in the called program. If the entry-point is less
         than or equal to nine characters, [ENTRYΓÇôPOINT] will be the entry-point. If the
         entry-point is greater than nine characters, [ENTRYΓÇôPOINT] is derived by
         concatenating the first three and last six characters of the entry-point. Also defined
         as entry-points are [SYMB]C$CTAL and [SYMB]Lnnnnn. There is a [SYMB]Lnnnnn
         for each location counter in the element where nnnnn is the value of the location
         counter.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                     19ΓÇô3
Collection of Programs




19.3. Collection of ASCII COBOL Programs
        This subsection discusses programming and collection restrictions, installation
        configuration considerations that affect program collection, and ASCII COBOL collection
        methods.

        ASCII COBOL programs may be collected using the following methods:
        ΓÇó   Bank-implied collection
        ΓÇó   Bank-named collection
        ΓÇó   Segmented collection

        All discussions and examples in this subsection assume that ASCII COBOL was installed
        using COMUS or SOLAR. The mode in which ASCII COBOL was installed may impact
        the collection methods to be used. Further information on collection restrictions relating
        to the configuration of ASCII COBOL can be found in 19.3.1.2.

19.3.1. Restrictions
19.3.1.1. General Restrictions
        The following are general restrictions which must be observed regardless of the method
        used to collect an ASCII COBOL program or the configuration of ASCII COBOL on the
        system.
        ΓÇó   I-banks must not exceed 65K (in other words, the address octal 177777).
        ΓÇó   Only one D-bank is allowed for all ASCII COBOL programs and subprograms.
        ΓÇó   When the D-bank exceeds 65K (in other words, the address octal 177777), the
            MEMORY 3 MODULES clause must be specified in the OBJECTΓÇôCOMPUTER
            paragraph on ASCII COBOL programs.

19.3.1.2. Installation Configuration Considerations
        The ASCII COBOL run-time library can be installed and used in the following methods:
        ΓÇó   Relocatable
        ΓÇó   Partial Common Banked (in other words, excluding C$DML)
        ΓÇó   Full Common Banked (in other words, including C$DML)




19ΓÇô4                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                          Collection of Programs




         The form of the library that is used in the collection of a particular program depends on
         which version of the element CBEP$$ACOB is included. The following table relates the
         element CBEP$$ACOB to the form of the library.


                   CBEP$$ACOB Element                     Library

                CBEP$$ACOB/NOΓÇôLIBΓÇôCB           Relocatable
                CBEP$$ACOB/PARTΓÇôLIBΓÇôCB         Partial Common Banked
                CBEP$$ACOB/FULLΓÇôLIBΓÇôCB         Full Common Banked


         No special collection considerations are required to use the relocatable or partial
         common banked libraries. To use the full common banked library (including the C$DML
         common bank), a collection method using C$DML must be followed (see 19.3.3 through
         19.3.5).

19.3.2. Bank-Implied Collections
         The bank-implied collection method is the simplest collection method and should be
         used unless the size of the program prohibits its use or the full common banked library is
         used. The following is an example of the Collector directives necessary for a banked
         implied collection of a main program and one subprogram:
           IN MAIN
           IN SUB
           IN SUB$$$SYSDTA


19.3.3. Collections Using C$DML
         The collection method described in this subsection must be followed if the full common
         banked library is used. This method should not be followed if the relocatable or partial
         common banked library is used. The Collector directives required for this collection
         method are basically the same whether the element CBEP$$ACOB/FULLΓÇôLIBΓÇôCB is
         implicitly included from the ASCII COBOL library (SYS$LIB$*ACOB) or explicitly included
         from the ASCII COBOL C$DML CBEP file (SYS$LIB$*ACOBΓÇôDML). The collection
         method varies depending on whether an ASCII or Fieldata version of the C$DML
         common bank is installed.

         Generally, the ASCII version of the C$DML common bank is installed, but it is important
         to verify this fact. To determine which version of the C$DML common bank is installed
         enter:
           @PRT,TR SYS$LIB$*ACOB.C$D202

         where SYS$LIB$*ACOB is the ASCII COBOL product file.

         If the relocatable is found, an ASCII version is installed; otherwise, a Fieldata version is
         installed.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                     19ΓÇô5
Collection of Programs




        The following example shows the Collector directives for a collection of a main program
        and one subprogram using C$DML:

          IBANK,UX   C$DML
          IBANK,M    I1,022000                      . See Note 1
            IN      MAIN
            IN      SUB
          DBANK,MUC D1
            IN      MAIN
            IN      SUB$$$SYSDTA
            IN      SYS$LIB$*ACOB-DML.CBEP$$ACOB/FULL-LIB-CB
          END

        Note: The collection illustrated assumes that an ASCII C$DML is installed. If a Fieldata
        version is installed, 022000 must be changed to 037000 on the IBANK directive.

19.3.4. Bank-Named Collection
        This subsection describes the method required to collect an ASCII COBOL program that
        requires two or more user I-banks. If only one user I-bank is required, the collection
        method described in 19.3.2 or 19.3.3 should be used.

        Collection of ASCII COBOL programs using multiple I-banks can be extremely
        complicated because the compiler generates LMJs and direct references to many run-
        time library I-bank elements. Since the compiler generates code in this manner, all run-
        time library elements that are referenced by an LMJ or a direct reference must be visible
        when the reference occurs. To ensure this visibility, the library elements must be
        collected in one of the following ways:
        1. In the D-bank
        2. In a separate bank that is always based
        3. In each bank that references the library element

        The third technique listed is the most complex and should only be used when the other
        techniques fail. The following are sample multibanked collections of a main program and
        three subprograms.




19ΓÇô6                                                                             7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                              Collection of Programs




         Not Using C$DML ΓÇö Version 1:
           LIB (D1/$ALL)
           LIB SYS$LIB$*ACOB()
           IBANK,M I1,01000
               IN      MAIN
               IN      SUB2
           IBANK    I2,01000
               IN      SUB1
           IBANK    I3,01000
               IN      SUB3
           DBANK,MC D1,(040000,I1,I2,I3)
               IN      MAIN
               IN      SUB1$$SYSDTA
               IN      SUB2$$SYSDTA
               IN      SUB3$$SYSDTA
           END

         Not Using C$DML ΓÇö Version 2:
           LIB (IL/$ODD, D1/$EVEN)
           LIB SYS$LIB$*ACOB()
           IBANK,UL IL,01000
               IN()    SYS$LIB$*ACOB.C$RET0
           IBANK,M I1,(IL)
               IN      MAIN
               IN      SUB2
               IN()    SYS$LIB$*ACOB.C$RET0
           IBANK    I2,(IL)
               IN      SUB1
               IN()    SYS$LIB$*ACOB.C$RET0
           IBANK    I3,(IL)
               IN      SUB3
               IN()    SYS$LIB$*ACOB.C$RET0
           DBANK,MC D1,(040000,I1,I2,I3)
               IN      MAIN
               IN      SUB1$$SYSDTA
               IN      SUB2$$SYSDTA
               IN      SUB3$$SYSDTA
           END




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                   19ΓÇô7
Collection of Programs




        Using C$DML:
          LIB (D1/$ALL)
          LIB SYS$LIB$*ACOB()
          IBANK,UX     C$DML
          IBANK,M      I1,022000
              IN          MAIN
              IN          SUB2
          IBANK        I2,022000
              IN          SUB1
          IBANK        I3,022000
              IN          SUB3
          DBANK,MC     D1,(040000,I1,I2,I3)
              IN          MAIN
              IN          SUB1$$SYSDTA
              IN          SUB2$$SYSDTA
              IN          SUB3$$SYSDTA
              IN          SYS$LIB$*ACOB-DML.CBEP$$ACOB/FULL-LIB-CB
          END

        The previous collection examples illustrate techniques 1 and 2. If collection errors are
        received, attempt to resolve the errors by either using the C$DML common bank or
        dividing an I-bank into multiple I-banks. If collection errors are not resolved using either
        or both of these suggestions, ensure that all ASCII COBOL programs have the MEMORY
        3 MODULES clause specified. If collection errors still occur, the last technique must be
        used. This technique requires the examination of an S or L option collection listing.
        Every C$Dxxx and C$M7xx element that is included in the collection, as well as the
        element C$RET0 must be locally INed in each bank that references the element. All
        other ASCII COBOL library elements may be collected into a separate I-bank.




19ΓÇô8                                                                                7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                      Collection of Programs




         The following is a bank named collection not using the C$DML common bank. This
         collection shows the local inclusion of the library elements as required.
             LIB (ILIB/$ODD, D1/$EVEN)
             LIB SYS$LIB$*ACOB()
             IBANK,M I1,01000
                IN       MAIN
                IN       SUB2
                IN()     C$RET0
                IN()     C$D322
             IBANK    I2,01000
                IN       SUB1
                IN()     C$RET0
             IBANK    I3,01000
                IN       SUB3
                IN()     C$RET0
                IN()     C$D313,C$D326
             IBANK    ILIB,01000
             DBANK,MC D1
                IN       MAIN
                IN       SUB1$$SYSDTA
                IN       SUB2$$SYSDTA
                IN       SUB3$$SYSDTA
             END


19.3.5. Segmented Collections
19.3.5.1. Compiler Generated Maps
         Map elements produced by the ASCII COBOL compiler for programs using the
         segmentation module of the COBOL language should be used without modification. If
         the program is to be collected with the full common banked library or contain calls to
         subprograms, the map element must be modified accordingly.

19.3.5.2. Non-Compiler Segmented Collections
         Whenever possible, multibanked collections should be used instead of segmentation.
         Additional collection restrictions apply when using segmentation. These restrictions are:
         ΓÇó    Only the I-bank should be segmented. If the D-bank is segmented, the data-items in
              that segment contain their initial values when the subprogram is called for a second
              time and the segment was overlaid by another segment.
         ΓÇó    If the indirect load segment method is not used, the programmer is responsible for
              loading the segments.
         ΓÇó    The call to a subprogram must not cause a segment to be loaded which overlays any
              subprogram that has been called and has not returned control to the calling program.

         The following examples show the Collector directives for a segmented collection using
         the indirect load method with a main program and four subprograms. In these
         examples, SUB1 and SUB3 can not directly or indirectly call each other because they are
         included in segments that overlay one another.



7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                19ΓÇô9
Collection of Programs




        Not Using C$DML:
          IBANK,M I1,01000
          SEG     MAIN
              IN MAINPROG
              IN SUB2
          SEG     SEG1*,(MAIN)
              IN SUB1
          SEG     SEG2*,(MAIN)
              IN SUB3
          SEG     SEG3*,(SEG1,SEG2)
              IN SUB4
          DBANK,MC D1
              IN MAINPROG
              IN SUB1$$SYSDTA
              IN SUB2$$SYSDTA
              IN SUB3$$SYSDTA
              IN SUB4$$SYSDTA
          END

        Using C$DML:
          IBANK,UX C$DML
          IBANK,M  I1,022000
          SEG     MAIN
              IN  MAINPROG
              IN  SUB2
          SEG     SEG1*,(MAIN)
              IN  SUB1
          SEG     SEG2*,(MAIN)
              IN  SUB3
          SEG     SEG3*,(SEG1,SEG2)
              IN  SUB4
          DBANK,MC D1
              IN  MAINPROG
              IN  SUB1$$SYSDTA
              IN  SUB2$$SYSDTA
              IN  SUB3$$SYSDTA
              IN  SUB4$$SYSDTA
              IN  SYS$LIB$*ACOB-DML.CBEP$$ACOB/FULL-LIB-CB
          END

        Large programs may require that the D-bank be segmented or the program split into two
        or more programs. If the program cannot be split, the D-bank may be segmented as
        long as location counter 6 of all ASCII COBOL programs is collected in the main
        segment. The following examples show the Collector directives for a segmented
        I-bank and segmented D-bank collection.




19ΓÇô10                                                                         7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                              Collection of Programs




         Not Using C$DML:
           IBANK,M   I1,01000
             SEG     MAIN
                IN   MAINPROG
                IN   SUB2
             SEG     SEG1*,(MAIN)
                IN   SUB1
             SEG     SEG2*,(MAIN)
                IN   SUB3
             SEG     SEG3*,(SEG1,SEG2)

Section 20
Related Processors

         This section documents the ASCII COBOL interface with related processors. The
         following processor interfaces are described in this section:
         ΓÇó   Define File Processor (DFP)
         ΓÇó   Processor Common Input/Output System (PCIOS)
         ΓÇó   Shared File System (SFS)
         ΓÇó   Sort-Merge




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                            20ΓÇô1
Related Processors




20.1. Define File Processor (DFP) Interface
        The Define File Processor gives the ASCII COBOL user the facility to specify certain
        attributes of a file at execution time without the need to change the COBOL source
        statements, recompile, or recollect.

        For additional information on the Define File Processor call and keyword parameters,
        refer to the OS 2200 Define File Processor (DFP) Administration and Programming
        Reference Manual (7830 7816).

        Prior to file initialization time, the use name DFP$ must be attached to the file containing
        the Define File Blocks (DFB). At file initialization time, ASCII COBOL searches the DFP$
        file for an omnibus element of the same name as specified as the file name in the
        ASSIGN clause.

20.1.1. Parameters
20.1.1.1. Non-MSAM Files
        You may experience difficulties in running COBOL programs accessing files, especially
        where several files are accessed simultaneously or where the file records are very large.
        The reason is that the COBOL compiler tries to optimize the number of buffers and the
        size of the buffers so that the PCIOS processor may operate more efficiently. Thus, this
        parameter provides the ability to override the BLOCK CONTAINS clause and number of
        buffers allocated without recompiling or remapping, and thus, to adjust the current
        operating environment.

        The BLOCK keyword parameter list is as follows:
             BLOCK = bs/bo/bn/bl/bu

        where:
        bs
              is the BLOCK CONTAINS clause value of integer-2. It is an integer in the range
              0 < bs < 131072.

        bo
              is the buffer offset parameter. This parameter is valid only for input tape files
              assigned to INTERCHANGE. It is an integer in the range 0 Γëñ bo Γëñ 99.

        bn
              is the number of buffers parameter. It is an integer in the range 0 < bn < 64.
              However, values of bn greater than 2 are meaningful only for INDEXED files.

        bl
              is the replacement for BLOCK CONTAINS clause value of integerΓÇô1. It is an integer
              in the range 0 < bl < 131072. This parameter is meaningful only for INDEXED files.
              Also, this parameter is meaningful only when the bs parameter is specified and
              bl Γëñ bs.




20ΓÇô2                                                                                  7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                            Related Processors




         bu
               is the BLOCK CONTAINS clause RECORDS or CHARACTERS option. It is coded as
               one of the following:
                RECORDS

                CHARACTERS

               In the absence of a bu parameter, CHARACTERS is assumed. This parameter is
               meaningful only when the bs parameter is specified.

20.1.1.2. MSAM Files
         A method for altering the compiler defaults for buffer size and number of buffers for
         1974 Standard Indexed files (in other words, PCIOS MSAM files) is provided.

         The BLOCK keyword parameter list is as follows:
              BLOCK = bs//bn/bl//bu

         where:
         bs
               buffer size (see 20.1.1.2.1)

         bn
               number of buffer parameters (4 Γëñ bn Γëñ 63); for OUTPUT and IΓÇôO mode, bn must be
               ΓëÑ 5 (see 20.1.1.2.2)

         bl
               block loading factor (see 20.1.1.2.3)

         bu
               blocking unit, WORDS, CHARACTERS or RECORDS (ASCII characters are assumed)

20.1.1.2.1. Buffer Size

         Through the DFP, you can alter the compiler-generated buffer size by specifying bs or bs
         plus bu.

         If bu = CHARACTERS or bu parameter absent, the buffer size used is bs rounded up to
         words then rounded up again to a multiple of 448 words.

         If bu = WORDS, the buffer size used is bs rounded up to a multiple of 448 words.

         If bu = RECORDS, the buffer size used is the following (rounded up to a multiple of 448
         words):
              bs * (mrl + 2 + ndk) + 6

         This formula is the same formula used by ASCII COBOL (see 17.2.2.2); however, no
         minimum size check is made.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                    20ΓÇô3
Related Processors




20.1.1.2.2. Number of Buffers

        Through the DFP, you can alter the compiler generated number of buffers by specifying
        a DFP BLOCK bn parameter in the range 5 through 63 for OUTPUT and IΓÇôO and 4
        through 63 for INPUT. If bn is less than the compiler generated value, only the top level
        index block for the RECORD key is locked into main storage at run-time. If bn is 4, no
        index blocks are locked into main storage.

20.1.1.2.3. Block Loading Factor

        The DFP bl parameter is equivalent to the integerΓÇô1 field in a BLOCK CONTAINS
        integer-1 TO integer-2 ... clause.

        The block loading factor is the number of words reserved in a block at file creation time
        and is calculated as:
          ((bs - bl) / bs) * buffer size

        If bs is not present, or if bl is not less than bs, the bl parameter is ignored.

20.1.1.3. Record Formats
        The rf parameter of the RECORD keyword parameter list provided by the DFP is allowed
        for INTERCHANGE and System Data Format (SDF) files only. No validation checks on
        the parameter values specified are made at run time.
          RECORD = /rf

        where rf can be:

              U            Undefined
              F            Fixed
              D            Variable
              FB           Fixed-blocked
              DB           Variable-blocked
              FS           Fixed-segmented
              DS           Variable-segmented
              FBS          Fixed-blocked-segmented
              VBS          Variable-blocked-segmented




20ΓÇô4                                                                                   7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                            Related Processors




20.1.1.4. Prep Factors
         The PREP keyword parameter is valid only for mass-storage files
           PREP = pf

         where pf can be:

                0        MASSΓÇôSTORAGE
                28       MASSΓÇôSTORAGEΓÇô28
                56       MASSΓÇôSTORAGEΓÇô56
                112      MASSΓÇôSTORAGEΓÇô112

         For RELATIVE files (direct access), the PF parameter may be coded as 112, 224, 448,
         896, or 1792.

         Note: Any other values of pf are ignored for mass-storage files and rounded down to
         the next value allowed for RELATIVE files.

20.1.1.5. Label Records
         The LABEL keyword parameter list is:
           LABEL = lt/li/le/la

         where lt can be:
           OMITTED
           STANDARD
           USER

         Although this parameter is provided via the DFP, complete freedom of choice is not
         possible because of the label routine collection requirements. Also, in the case of user
         labels, declaratives must be coded in the source program in order to make this
         parameter meaningful. Therefore, this parameter may change the amount of label
         handling performed on a file only to a lower state than was declared in the source
         program. More precisely:


                      Source Program Stated           Allowable lt values

                USER (data-name)                USER, STANDARD, OMITTED
                STANDARD                        STANDARD, OMITTED
                OMITTED                         OMITTED




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                 20ΓÇô5
Related Processors




        If this parameter is used to change the label processing functions specified in the source

        li

20.1.1.6. Verify Parameter
        The VERIFY parameter specifies the file identifier for an existing file that requires
        verification before it can be overwritten using a new file identifier as follows:
             VERIFY = vi

        The vi parameter specifies the file identifier to be verified.

20.1.1.7. EBCDIC Translate
        The OPTIONS keyword parameter is:
             OPTIONS = A

        The A parameter indicates that for an EBCDIC file, a 256-character EBCDIC/ISO8859-1
        translate table is used. Absence of the A parameter indicates a 128-character translate
        table is used.

20.1.1.8. OPEN Parameter
        The OPEN parameter gives the status of the file at open time. It is coded as:
             OPEN = os

        where os is the open status and is interpreted as:

        NEW
              removes the effect of the OPEN statement EXTEND option if specified for a
              standard TAPE file.

20.1.1.9. CLOSE Parameter
         The CLOSE parameter specifies the disposition of the file at close time. It is coded as:
               CLOSE = cd

         where cd is the close disposition parameter and is interpreted as:

                close time.

         FREE
                if specified for 1974 Standard TAPE or INTERCHANGE file, or SDF file, the file is
                freed (@FREE) at close time.

         The SHARE keyword parameter specifies that a file is shared (processed by the Shared

         The format is:

         where:
         shr

                YES
                     the file is to be processed by the Shared File System (SFS 2200).

                NO

         itf
                is the ITF indicator, and has one of the following values:

20.1.2. Concatenation of Data Files
        Concatenation of data files allows separate ASCII COBOL physical files to be processed
        as one ASCII COBOL logical file. This is accomplished by linking each fileΓÇÖs Define File
        Block (DFB). The first and subsequent DFBs must be available via the general interface
        mechanism described at the beginning of this subsection. All DFB keyword parameters
        are interpreted from the first DFB; only LABELΓÇôID, OPEN, and CLOSE parameters are
        interpreted from each subsequent DFB.

        File concatenation is limited to the input (forward only) mode of 74 ANSI TAPE,
        INTERCHANGE, and SDF sequential DISC files. Concatenation of a set of ASCII COBOL
        files is allowed only on component files of the same file format, and uniform labeling
        conventions must exist for all component files. A component file is one of several files
        that compose a concatenated file, and a concatenated file is the entire collection of
        COBOL files that are processed as a single logical file.

        When a data file of the type just mentioned is opened for input, the concatenation field
        of the DFB is checked if a DFB exists for that file. If the field is zero, concatenation
        terminates. If nonzero, the field contains the element name for the DFB of the next file
        in the concatenation chain. All DFBs must be accessible in a file DFP$ either by
        assigning the file as DFP$ or by linking it to DFP$ via an @USE statement.

        When an end-of-file is detected on an input file that has a DFB, the concatenation field of
        the DFB is checked. If concatenation is specified, the present file is automatically closed
        observing the DFB CLOSE parameter, the next DFB is retrieved, and the data file
        specified in the DFB is opened. If the DFP OPEN parameter for this file is OPEN=OLD
        and the file was cataloged, it is also automatically assigned. Processing of the input file
        continues as if no end-of-file had occurred. A true end-of-file condition is not raised until
        the last record of the final component file is processed.

        The SELECT statement in the COBOL program for the concatenation file may specify the
        OPTIONAL clause but, if the first component file is present, all nonfirst component files
        must be present. If the first component file is not present, the entire concatenation file
        is treated as not present.




20ΓÇô8                                                                                 7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                             Related Processors




         The following example shows how the Define File Processor is used to produce the
         Define File Blocks required to concatenate three component files:
           @DFP,E F1.,DFP$.FA,DFP$.FB
             Keyword parameters describing F1*
           @EOF
           @DFP,E F2.,DFP$.FB,DFP$.FC
             Keyword parameters describing F2*
           @EOF
           @DFP,E F3.,DFP$.FC
             Keyword parameters describing F3*
           @EOF

         File DFP$ must be assigned. Files F1, F2, and F3 must be preassigned, or they must be
         cataloged with OPEN parameters of OPEN=OLD, in which case they are dynamically
         assigned by the run.

         The COBOL source lines to process these files as a single logical file would have the
         form:
           SELECT FA ASSIGN TO implementor-name.
               .
               .
               .
           OPEN INPUT FA.
           READ FA AT END imperative-statement.

         The imperative-statement is not executed until an end-of-file is reached on file F3.

20.2. Processor Common Input/Output System
      (PCIOS) Interface
        The Processor Common Input/Output System (PCIOS) is used as the ASCII COBOL
        Mass Storage Control System (MSCS) and the ASCII COBOL Tape Control System and
        serves as the interface between COBOL programs and Input/Output devices. All ASCII
        COBOL nonsymbiont files that conform to the American National Standard Institute
        (ANSI) COBOL X3.23ΓÇô1974 specifications are processed by PCIOS (except for shared
        files).

        If you are using a common banked ASCII COBOL library, then common banked PCIOS is
        required.

        If you are using a relocatable COBOL library, then either common banked (IN
        CBEP$$PCIOS) or relocatable PCIOS (LIB SYS$LIB$*PCIOS) can be used.

        For more information concerning PCIOS, refer to the OS 2200 Processor Common
        Input/Output System (PCIOS) Administration and Programming Reference Manual
        (7831 0588).




20ΓÇô10                                                                           7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                           Related Processors




20.3. Shared File System (SFS 2200) Interface
         The Shared File System (SFS) can be used as the ASCII COBOL Mass Storage Control
         System (MSCS) for Relative IΓÇôO (DSDF) and Indexed IΓÇôO (MSAM) files and serves as an
         interface between COBOL programs and input/output devices.

         To access files through the OS 2200 Shared File System (SFS 2200), you must install the
         SFS 2200 common IΓÇôO modules and banks. This interface allows multithread access to
         Indexed IΓÇôO (MSAM) and Relative (DSDF) files only. You can process these files singly
         or concurrently in a multithread environment and designate them as recoverable. PCIOS
         must co-exist with SFS 2200 to allow single-thread processing of the nonshared file
         access modes (SSDF, DSDF, MSAM, ANSI TAPE, ISAM). All programs that interface
         with SFS should use explicit thread control via the Relational Syntax Analyzer (see the
         Relational Database Server for ClearPath 2200 SQL End Use Guide).

         The SFS interface in ASCII COBOL common banks references the default application
         group (UDSSRC). To reference an alternate application group, use one of the following
         methods:
         ΓÇó   Modify your collection to reference a relocatable ASCII COBOL library (such as LIB
             ACOBLIB) and include the SFS CBEP$ element for the alternate application group
             (for example, IN UDS$$TWO*SFS.CBEP$$SFS). This method will always ensure
             that the alternate application group is referenced. You can also optionally modify
             your ASCII COBOL program as described in the second method.
         ΓÇó   If the SFS code banks in the default and alternate application groups are compatible,
             modify the ASCII COBOL program to specify the alternate application group name
             using an RSA BEGIN THREAD command, for example:
                BEGIN THREAD <thread-name> FOR APPLICATION APPTWO ...

         The ASCII COBOL Relative and Indexed IΓÇôO interface modules (C$SCIM and C$SIIO)
         reference the SFS 2200 common banked entry points if the SFS 2200 interface is
         present when you install the COBOL libraries. One of the following methods must be
         used to designate a file as shared:
         1. At compile time, specify AΓÇôSHAREDΓÇôFILE as the implementor-name-1 on the
            ASSIGN clause in the SELECT clause. This method will cause all DFP processing for
            the file to be bypassed.
         2. At runtime, use the SHARE parameter of the Define File Processor (see 20.1.1.10,
            DFP Interface).
         For more information about SFS 2200, see the Shared File System (SFS 2200) Interface
         Description (7831 0786).

20.3.1. Rollback and Deadlock Situations
        The Shared File System provides for concurrent file access as well as recovery. When a
        rollback or deadlock status is returned by the Shared File System, Table 20ΓÇô1
        summarizes the actions that ASCII COBOL will take during its error processing. These
        actions depend upon whether the user program specified a FILE STATUS clause in the
        file control entry of the shared file and/or defined a USE procedure for the shared file in
        the declaratives portion of the Procedure Division. It must be recognized that when an
        internal rollback or deadlock occurs and the file is declared as recoverable, all updates
        not yet committed are lost.


                Table 20ΓÇô1. ACOB Rollback/Deadlock Error Processing

                               FILE STATUS SPECIFIED              NO FILE STATUS SPECIFIED
        USE PROCEDURE          1.   Define File Status as:        1.   Close all open shared files
        SPECIFIED                   Status Key 1 = 9              2.   Issue warning diagnostic
                                    Status Key 2 =                         1502 (deadlock)
                                       binary 20 (deadlock)                1503 (rollback)
                                       binary 21 (rollback)       3.   Process the declarative
                               2.   Close all open shared files   4.   Normal return
                               3.   Process the declarative
                               4.   Normal return
        NO USE PROCEDURE       1.   Define File Status as:      Issue abort diagnostic
        SPECIFIED                   Status Key 1 = 9                1504 (rollback)
                                    Status Key 2 =                  1505 (deadlock)
                                       binary 20 (deadlock)
                                       binary 21 (rollback)
                               2.   Close all open shared files
                               3.   Normal return

20.4. Sort-Merge Interface
         The Sort-Merge interface provides the ASCII COBOL user the facility to order one or
         more files of records or combine two or more identically ordered files of records,
         according to a set of user-specified keys.

20.4.1. Main Storage Size
         At execution time, significant main storage is required to accomplish a sort or merge.
         The user can dynamically change the amount of main storage needed for a sort or merge
         by using the R$CORE feature. This feature requires mass storage assignment of a file
         name R$CORE whose maximum granularity on this assign will be used to determine the
         amount of main storage that is required for the sort or merge. The ASCII COBOL library
         multiplies the maximum granularity on the @ASG,T R$CORE statement by 1,000 to
         determine the actual amount of storage to dynamically assign. In the absence of an
         R$CORE statement, 22,500 words are used as the storage assignment. An example
         showing how to specify a 140,000 word Sort-Merge area is:
           @ASG,T R$CORE.,F///140


20.4.2. SortΓÇôMerge Files
         Special Sort-Merge files must be assigned prior to the execution of the program using
         the external names ΓÇ£XAΓÇ¥ through ΓÇ£XZΓÇ¥ for the required mass storage or tape. See the
         OS 2200 Sort/Merge Programming Guide (7831 0687) for a more detailed discussion of
         these assignments.

20.4.3. Suppression of SORT Console and Log Messages
         By default, the console and/or log messages are displayed when a program executes
         SORT/MERGE statements. ASCII COBOL provides the user with a run-time facility to
         suppress or enable these messages. To suppress or enable the console and/or log
         messages, the following statements can be specified in a COBOL program:

         To suppress console messages, use:
           CALL 'SUPCON$'.

         To suppress log messages, use:
           CALL 'SUPLOG$'.

         To suppress console and log messages, use:
           CALL 'SUPCONLOG$'.

         To enable console messages, use:
           CALL 'ENACON$'.

         To enable log messages, use:
           CALL 'ENALOG$'.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                             20ΓÇô13
Related Processors




        To enable console and log messages, use:
          CALL 'ENACONLG$'.

        When the CALL statement to suppress the console and/or log message is executed,
        these are suppressed until a CALL statement to enable these messages is executed or
        the end of the program is reached.

Section 21

21.1. General
         This section describes programming considerations, restrictions, and special collection
         requirements for executing ASCII COBOL programs in the TIP and HVTIP environments.
         The ASCII COBOL TIP library, normally SYS$LIB$*ACOBΓÇôTIPLIB, contains Message
         Control System (MCS) routines with TIP interfaces and main storage buffer elements.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                               21ΓÇô1
Transaction Processing




21.2. Message Control System (MCS)
        The ASCII COBOL MCS routines with TIP interfaces provide a direct interface between
        the ASCII COBOL SEND and RECEIVE statements and TIP. It is assumed that the ASCII
        COBOL programs are registered as TIP programs, and that each program will be initiated
        to receive and process one transaction. Each program may also send a message (or
        messages) to communications devices or other programs. All scheduling and routing is
        under the control of the TIP system, and the Communications Management System
        (CMS 2200) is used to enqueue and dequeue messages rather than MCS. The ASCII
        COBOL MCS routines use COMPOOL interfaces for all messages. No Message Control
        Bank (MCB) interfaces are provided.

21.2.1. The RECEIVE Statement
        To receive the text of an input transaction, the program executes a RECEIVE statement.
        You do not have to update the QUEUE field of the INPUT CD since there is, at most, one
        message available for a single execution of a transaction program at any time. After the
        execution of the RECEIVE statement, the fields of the INPUT CD are set as follows:
        QUEUE
            is initialized to TIP.

        SUBΓÇôQUEUEΓÇô1
            contains spaces.

        SUBΓÇôQUEUEΓÇô2
            contains spaces.

        SUBΓÇôQUEUEΓÇô3
            contains spaces.

        MESSAGE TIME
            contains spaces.

        MESSAGE DATE
            contains spaces.

        SYMBOLIC SOURCE
            if the transaction came from a terminal, this field contains the Position ID (PID) for
            that device. If the transaction was from another ASCII COBOL program, this field
            contains the PID of that programΓÇÖs transaction. The PID is right justified in the last
            four characters of this field and zero filled. If the SOURCE (in other words, the PID)
            is unknown, this field contains spaces.

        TEXT LENGTH
            is the number of characters transferred to the specific identifier. (On a transmission
            from some devices, the character covered by the cursor is transmitted. This may
            result in a blank character at the end of the message.)




21ΓÇô2                                                                               7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                      Transaction Processing




         END KEY
             is 0 until the entire message has been received into the ASCII COBOL program, at
             which time it is 2.

         STATUS KEY
             see Table 13-1 and Table 13-2.

         MESSAGE COUNT
             is 1 until the complete message has been received by the program, at which time it
             is 0.

         The concept of message segments is meaningless in this environment. End of Segment
         Indicators (ESI) are ignored, and End of Group Indicators (EGI) and End of Message
         Indicators (EMI) are equivalent. If no message text is available during the execution of a
         RECEIVE statement, the imperative statement in the NO DATA phrase is executed.

21.2.2. The SEND Statement
         To execute a SEND statement, you must update the fields of an OUTPUT CD. Since
         ASCII COBOL is interfacing through CMS to TIP programs and devices, the following
         conventions must be followed:

         For program to program, SYMBOLIC DESTINATIONS must be:
             PROG xxxxxx

                 One space after PROG is required. The xxxxxx parameter must contain the TIP
                 transcode for the called program, left justified and space filled.

         For program to output device, SYMBOLIC DESTINATIONS must be:
             DEVICE nnnn

                 The word DEVICE is not required, but the last four characters nnnn of this field
                 must be numeric digits reflecting a valid TIP PID. Normally, you should move the
                 SYMBOLIC SOURCE of transaction received to this field for output to the same
                 device. A SEND without EMI is permitted, as well as multiple destinations.
                 However, a message for any destination is not stored into COMPOOL until a
                 complete message with EMI is sent for that destination.

         The ENABLE and DISABLE statements are transparent, but are syntactically allowed in a
         TIP environment.

         Since a program is only scheduled when a message is available, the MESSAGE COUNT
         returned on execution of an ACCEPT MESSAGE COUNT is 1 until the complete
         message is received, at which time MESSAGE COUNT is 0.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                 21ΓÇô3
Transaction Processing




21.3. Main Storage Requirements
        Since efficiency is important in the transaction environment, all main storage should be
        obtained at collection time. For this purpose, 99 main storage elements reside in the
        ASCII COBOL TIP library. They are named C$SMCn, where n is the number of 512-word
        main storage blocks reserved in the C$SMCn element. One of these elements must be
        explicitly included in the collection of every ASCII COBOL transaction program. If this
        element is the last element explicitly included in the programΓÇÖs collection, an ER
        MCORE$ will be allowed to obtain additional space if necessary; otherwise, an ER
        MCORE$ will be prohibited and transaction programs will abort with diagnostic 1403A if
        insufficient space is allocated.

        The exact size of the buffer element required will depend upon the program content.
        Use the following guidelines for determining the appropriate size of the element to be
        included in a non-HVTIP program collection.
        ΓÇó    Begin with one to five core blocks for general COBOL use.
        ΓÇó    Increase the size by the space required for file record areas, file buffer areas, and the
             SORT/MERGE main storage requirements.
        ΓÇó    Add to that size the space requirements of other products (for example, DPS) that
             are used by the transaction.

        If an element larger than C$SMC99 is required, you may generate your own buffer
        element by creating a MASM element as follows:

            $(0)                         .
            C$FIRST*                     .
               $RES    size              .
            C$LAST*                      .
               $RES    1                 .
               $END                      .

        where size is the number of words of main storage required.




21ΓÇô4                                                                                  7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                        Transaction Processing




21.4. Transaction Interface Processing (TIP)
      Considerations
         The following subsections describe restrictions and collection requirements for nonΓÇô
         HVTIP ASCII COBOL TIP transactions.

21.4.1. Restrictions
         ASCII COBOL programs may be registered with TIP as a self-destructive, self-initializing,
         or reentrant transaction. The block-transfer loading and sticking options may be used
         with self-initializing and reentrant transactions. The following programming restrictions
         must be observed for self-initializing and reentrant transactions:
         ΓÇó    The contents of data items with initial values can not be altered.
         ΓÇó    Asynchronous processing is not allowed.
         ΓÇó    IΓÇôO to nonprint files which are not processed by PCIOS or SFS is not allowed.
         ΓÇó    Report writer is not allowed.
         ΓÇó    IΓÇôO to a file specified in an APPLY EXREF/EXDEF clause is not allowed.

21.4.2. Collection Considerations
         The collection of all ASCII COBOL transaction programs require that two elements (in
         other words, C$S400/TIP and C$SMCn) be included from the ASCII COBOL TIP library
         (SYS$LIB$*ACOBΓÇôTIPLIB). Reentrant transactions are restricted to one static I-bank,
         which must be the control bank, and one D-bank.

         The collection of ASCII COBOL communication programs may require special collection
         considerations depending upon whether or not the default ASCII COBOL library contains
         TIP interfaces. The collection examples in the following subsections assume that
         SYS$LIB$*ACOB contains the ASCII COBOL library, SYS$LIB$*ACOBΓÇôTIPLIB contains
         the ASCII COBOL TIP library, and TIP$*TIPLIB$ contains the TIP primitive library. In
         addition, the collection examples assume that the common bank C$DML is not being
         used. If you want to use C$DML, the collection examples must be modified accordingly
         (see 19.3.3).

21.4.2.1. Noncommunication Program Example
         If the relocatable element C$S205/TIP exists in the default library, ASCII COBOL
         communication and noncommunication programs should be collected using one of these
         sample collections.
             @MAP,IS ,PROG
             IN FILE.PROG
             IN SYS$LIB$*ACOB-TIPLIB.C$S400/TIP
             IN SYS$LIB$*ACOB-TIPLIB.C$SMCn




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                 21ΓÇô5
Transaction Processing




        If a reentrant online program is required, the program must be collected with the I-bank
        as the control bank, as follows:
          @MAP,IS ,PROG
          IBANK,CM IB
          IN FILE.PROG
          LIB (IB/$ODD,DB/$EVEN)
          LIB SYS$LIB$*ACOB(),TIP$*TIPLIB$()
          DBANK,M DB
          IN MEM$ERR
          IN FILE.PROG
          IN SYS$LIB$*ACOB-TIPLIB.C$S400/TIP
          IN SYS$LIB$*ACOB-TIPLIB.C$SMCn

        where C$SMCn is one of the main storage buffer elements described in 21.3.
