21.5. HVTIP Considerations
21.5.1. General
         ASCII COBOL allows programs to be executed in the high volume TIP (HVTIP)
         environment. The D-bank is made self-initializing by utilizing the relocatable segment
         (RSEG) capability. The following presumes a working knowledge of the HVTIP program
         environment.

         An HVTIP transaction system consists of a set of independently collected program banks
         that link to each other dynamically at run time, and can be independently updated; in
         other words, recompiled, recollected, and reloaded online without need for other
         changes. CALL$ and XFR$ (in other words, CALL and TRANSFER) are the two TIP
         executive requests that cause the I-bank of an HVTIP program to be switched. They are
         analogous to the effect of an LIJ instruction in a non-HVTIP program.

         To create high volume banks from COBOL subprograms involves writing a main
         transaction driver program and several special case transaction processing subprograms.
         Both the main and the subprograms can be written in COBOL. The main program must
         define all global work space in CommonΓÇôStorage (this includes global COBOL data and
         the DMCA record area). Subprograms then have global data in Common-Storage and
         local data in WorkingΓÇôStorage.

         Subprograms may be defined as either HVTIP bank entry-points subprograms or as
         ΓÇ£localΓÇ¥ subprograms. HVTIP bank entry-point subprograms are defined by an IBJLNK
         Collector directive and can be referenced by an HVTIP bank. ΓÇ£LocalΓÇ¥ subprograms are
         defined by IN or LIB directives and can be referenced only by programs within the HVTIP
         bank.

         If a COBOL subprogram is defined at collection time as existing under a TRANSFER
         IBJLNK directive, all previously allocated user work space (except for that of the main
         program) is released at run time before its own local work space is allocated and
         initialized.

         A subprogram defined at collection time under a CALL IBJLNK directive, at run time,
         causes its local work space to be initialized at first call and to remain in its last used state
         for subsequent calls within the transaction. Local work spaces accumulate as the
         transaction cascades through several HVTIP banks via CALL$, and are released only at
         transaction termination or on a transfer (in other words, XFR$), or by explicitly
         programmed cancellation (in other words, CANCEL statement).

         Basically, the ACOB/HVTIP interface is handled entirely within the main program or
         subprogram prologue routines. The collection process is the major consideration for
         creating HVTIP applications.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                       21ΓÇô7
Transaction Processing




21.5.2. Creating Module Name Equate Elements
        To define the HVTIP bank-to-bank calling relationships, either one or two Module Name
        Equate (MNQ) elements are required. These elements relate the entry-point name of
        each HVTIP subprogram bank, as used on a COBOL CALL statement, to the library and
        bank numbers the Exec uses to identify the bank.

         Normally, there are two such elements defined for the complete set of HVTIP
        transaction programs that make up the application system. They should be created as
        part of the overall system design then placed in an appropriate user file from where they
        can be accessed during the collection of each HVTIP bank. You should place both the
        source and relocatable form of these elements in the user file, and use the names
        CALL$MNQ and XFR$MNQ for these elements.

        One element, CALL$MNQ, defines all those subprogram banks that are to be entered
        using a CALL$. The other, XFR$MNQ, is for all those to be entered using a XFR$.

        Note: A subprogram bank should not be entered by both CALL$ and XFR$.

        Each entry point in an MNQ element must be defined as a 36ΓÇôbit value as follows:
          S1    library number
          S2,S3 bank number
          H2    (not used)

        The following is an example of creating the MNQ elements:
          @MASM,I      APPL.CALL$MNQ
          SUB1*      $EQU      010001000000      .
          C$BSUB1*   $EQU      0                 .
          SUB3*      $EQU      010003000000      .
          C$BSUB3*   $EQU      0                 .
                     $END

          @MASM,I      APPL.XFR$MNQ              .
          SUB2*      $EQU      010002000000      .
          C$BSUB2*   $EQU      0                 .
                     $END

        These elements define an HVTIP system consisting of two CALL$ subprogram banks
        and one XFR$ subprogram bank contained in HVTIP library number 01 as banks 01, 02,
        and 03, respectively, in addition to any ICPs defined by VALTAB. Entry points of the
        form C$Bxxxx are included for completeness to satisfy references to the data areas of
        the called subprograms that are otherwise undefined.

        COBOL names may contain a minus character, but such a name is not acceptable as a
        MASM label. In such a case, you should use a $INFO 6 directive to define the COBOL
        entry point.




21ΓÇô8                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                       Transaction Processing




21.5.3. TIP Interface
         A program in the ICP bank (possibly the main program) should do a COMPOOL primitive
         call to read the incoming message or do a RECEIVE. The ICP then contains logic to
         process the message or branch to a subprogram module to process it. Alternatively, a
         COMPOOL primitive call can be made in one of the subprogram banks.

21.5.4. CALL Statement
         The CALL statement is used to effect a CALL$ or a XFR$ from one HVTIP bank to
         another and to transfer control to a local subprogram. The execution of a CALL$ or XFR$
         is determined at collection time by reference to the MNQ elements.

          A subprogram called by using an XFR$ cannot thereafter execute a return from that
         subprogram, and the calling program never resumes execution unless called again, at
         which time it is reinitialized. No parameters can be passed on an XFR$ call.

         The CALL data-name form of the CALL statement can be used to result in either form of
         HVTIP bank to bank switch, in which case the value of dataΓÇôname should correspond to
         an entry point in one of the MNQ elements.

21.5.5. EXIT Statement
         The EXIT PROGRAM statement is used to return from one HVTIP bank to another,
         except as noted earlier (XFR$).

21.5.6. CANCEL Statement
         The CANCEL statement can be used to cause the local data space of a previously called
         HVTIP bank subprogram to be freed and, when next called, to be reallocated and
         reinitialized. A ΓÇ£localΓÇ¥ subprogram must not be explicitly cancelled, but is automatically
         cancelled upon the cancellation of its HVTIP bank entryΓÇôpoint subprogram. Common
         banked subprograms are handled as though they were locally contained in the HVTIP
         bank making the call.

21.5.7. Writing MASM Subprograms for COBOL/HVTIP
         Using HVTIP, the data area of a subprogram is located at an address that is assigned only
         at run-time. The COBOL compiler and library ensure that the data of a COBOL
         subprogram is addressed correctly. Since neither the COBOL compiler nor the COBOL
         library has control over a program written in MASM, it is the programmerΓÇÖs responsibility
         to know where the address of the MASM subprogramΓÇÖs data area can be found at run-
         time.

         The data area address is available in H1 of the word pointed to by register A0 when the
         subprogram is entered at run time. The value contained in this half word is the address
         of the tag C$BXXXX if the MASM subprogram entry point has the name XXXX. The
         programmer should dedicate a register in the program to contain this value. All
         references to data contained in the MASM subprogram must use this register. The data
         area itself should be allocated following the tag C$BXXXX.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                  21ΓÇô9
Transaction Processing




        In the following example, register A3 is loaded with the address of the subprogramΓÇÖs
        data area immediately upon entry. The data area itself is contained in the same element
        as the code that references it.
                      AXR$
            $(0)
            C$BASMEP*                         .
            DUMMY     +015                    .
            DATA      $EQUF    0,A3           .
               .
               .
               .
            $(1)                              .
            ASMEP*                            .
                      L,H1      A3,0,A0       .
                      L         A2,DATA
               .
               .
               .
                      $END                    .

        When collected, the $ODD and $EVEN location counters are split between the HVTIP
        bank and the relocatable segment (RSEG) of the DΓÇôbank. This data area is local to each
        HVTIP bank, so that different copies of this routine in different banks each access their
        own private data. To access a MASM-defined global data area from different HVTIP
        banks requires interaction with the COBOL run-time control tables and should be done
        only with extreme care.

21.5.8. Restrictions
        The following is a list of source program and compiler option restrictions that must be
        adhered to in order for successful execution of ASCII COBOL programs in the HVTIP
        environment.
        ΓÇó    The OBJECTΓÇôCOMPUTER paragraph of all ASCII COBOL programs must contain the
             MEMORY 3 MODULES clause.
        ΓÇó    APPLY EXREF and APPLY EXDEF are not allowed.
        ΓÇó    Asynchronous processing is not allowed.
        ΓÇó    Program segmentation is not allowed.
        ΓÇó    Entry-point subprograms cannot be compiled with the 4 extra options.
        ΓÇó    The ON OVERFLOW phrase of the CALL statement has no effect.
        ΓÇó    The only ENTER statements allowed are ENTER ASM and ENTER MASM.
        ΓÇó    Subprograms cannot be compiled with the 7 extra option.




21ΓÇô10                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                      Transaction Processing




21.5.9. Main Storage Requirements
         As in the TIP environment, efficiency is important in the HVTIP environment, therefore,
         adequate storage should be allocated at collection time. The Initial Control Program (ICP)
         should reserve sufficient main storage for the entire transaction. HVTIP transactions
         require more main storage than TIP transactions. Thus, you must determine the main
         storage requirements based on the guidelines in 21.3 plus the requirements for all HVTIP
         bank RSEGs.

         Upon transaction initialization, the ICPΓÇÖs RSEG is loaded into dynamic memory and
         remains in storage throughout the entire transaction. Each time a subprogram bank is
         called, the RSEG for that bank must be loaded into dynamic memory, unless it already
         resides in memory from a previous call. The RSEG will remain in memory until either the
         entry-point subprogram is CANCELled or a subprogram bank is called via XFR$.

21.5.10. Automatic Collection of ASCII COBOL HVTIP
         Transactions
         Collecting ASCII COBOL/HVTIP programs are nontrivial. For this reason, a runstream
         called MAPHVTIP is available in the ASCII COBOL TIP library. The runstream uses an
         SSG skeleton.

         Before using the skeleton, the source of the two MNQ elements, CALL$MNQ and
         XFR$MNQ, must exist in some user file as described in 21.5.2. If no CALL$ or XFR$
         entry points exist, the corresponding element should exist but be empty. An empty
         element should never contain an END image. The last image in a nonempty element
         must be an END image. In addition, the relocatables for all ASCII COBOL programs must
         be located in a user file.

         If you use a common-banked ASCII COBOL library, the element, CBEP$$ACOB, contains
         entry points C$S30S, C$S327, C$S35X, C$S335, C$S310, C$S31A, and C$S31C. Since
         elements C$S310 and C$S30S must be collected in HVTIP banks, these entry points
         cause the Collector to give a message saying that these entry points are already defined.
         This is not a problem. Leaving these entry points in CBEP$$ACOB allows the C$S310
         and C$S30S routines in the C$INITIAL common bank to be used by your non-HVTIP
         applications.

         To use the skeleton, enter as input:
           @ADD SYS$LIB$*ACOB-TIPLIB.MAPHVTIP
           user SGSs
           @EOF
           @EOF

         The skeleton is designed so that each run can collect one or more HVTIP banks; i.e., ICP
         or subprogram banks. The HVTIP and LOCAL SGSs describe the individual banks and
         may occur any number of times. All other SGSs describe information common to all the
         banks and must occur only once. The only required SGSs are the HVTIP SGSs, one per
         bank to be collected, and the DMS SGS if DMS 2200 is being used.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                21ΓÇô11
Transaction Processing




        Fields should be given in the sequence indicated. Optional fields are shown enclosed in
        [brackets]. Where needed, file names may include a qualifier, but periods are not allowed
        in file names or element names. All version-names are optional and default to blanks.
        Where the name of a COBOL relocatable element is indicated, it means the element
        containing the code. The SYSDTA elements are handled automatically.

21.5.10.1. User SGSs
        The following subsections describe the user SGSs that can be supplied to the
        MAPHVTIP skeleton.

21.5.10.1.1. HVTIP

        Format:
          HVTIP prog-type,prog-id [ bank-type ] ;

          [ IN,[element],[version] ] ;

          [ OUT,[element],[version] ]

        where:

        prog-type
            ICP or SUBPROGRAM

        prog-id
            the COBOL prog-id or ENTRY name of the entry program

        bank-type
            STATIC or DYNAMIC

        Each HVTIP SGS calls for the collection of either an ICP or subprogram bank. The entry
        program (in other words, main program if an ICP, CALL$ subprogram if a subprogram
        bank) is the relocatable with element and version names given as IN, and the collected
        absolute has element and version names given as OUT. The default for both element
        names is the prog-id of the entry program. The default bank-type is the globally defined
        bank-type (see 21.5.10.1.7).




21ΓÇô12                                                                            7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                     Transaction Processing




21.5.10.1.2. LOCAL

         Format:
            LOCAL local-to-id [ FILE,file ] ;

                lang,element[,version] ;

                [ lang,element[,version] ] . . . .

         where:

         lang
             is COBOL, ASM, or MASM.

         local-to-id
             is TO, progΓÇôid   or   ALL.

         These SGSs name the relocatable elements of subprograms local to the HVTIP bank
         whose entry program has the given progΓÇôid. If ALL is specified, the listed elements are
         to be included in all the HVTIP banks. There may be any number of LOCAL SGSs for
         each bank. FILE names the file containing the relocatables on each LOCAL SGS and
         defaults to the REL file. There may be one or more lang fields on each SGS.

21.5.10.1.3. REL

         Format:
            REL file

         The REL SGS names the file containing the relocatables of all entry programs and all
         local subprograms named on LOCAL SGSs without a FILE. The default for REL is the file
         TPF$. If the REL file defaults to TPF$, the CONTROL SGS must be specified, and it
         must specify a file other than TPF$.

21.5.10.1.4. ABS

         Format:
            ABS file

         The ABS SGS names the file to which the generated absolutes are directed. The default
         is the file specified on the REL SGS.

21.5.10.1.5. CONTROL

         Format:
            CONTROL file

         The CONTROL SGS names the file containing the source of the equate elements
         CALL$MNQ and XFR$MNQ, if this type of bank switching is used. The default is the file
         specified on the REL SGS.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                              21ΓÇô13
Transaction Processing




21.5.10.1.6. MAP

         Format:
           MAP file

         The MAP SGS names the file that contains the MAP processor to be used for
         collections. The default is the system installed Collector (@MAP).

21.5.10.1.7. IBANKS

         Format:
           IBANKS ARE bank-type

         where bank-type is STATIC or DYNAMIC.

         The IBANKS SGS defines the type of I-bank generated for those banks that do not
         have a bank-type given on their HVTIP SGS. The default is STATIC.

21.5.10.1.8. DBANK

         Format:
           DBANK IS decimal-or-octal integer

         The DBANK SGS defines the D-bank requirement for the transaction. The default is 4096
         words.

21.5.10.1.9. USING

         Format:
           USING [ MCS ] [ SORT ] [ DEBUG ]

         The USING SGS must specify MCS if the COBOL SEND/RECEIVE syntax is used for
         communicating messages with TIP, and/or must specify SORT if the COBOL SORT
         facility is used in the transaction, and/or must specify DEBUG only if frequency task
         generation is invoked in the initial control program (ICP).

21.5.10.1.10. LIST

         Format:
           LIST list-type

         where list-type is SHORT, NORMAL, or LONG.

         The LIST SGS gives the type of listing required from the MAP processor. The default is
         NORMAL.




21ΓÇô14                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                          Transaction Processing




21.5.10.1.11. COBOL

         Format:
            COBOL [ LIB,libfile ] [ TIPVERSION,tipfile ] ;

                     [ COMMON BANKED [ CBEP$,cbfile ] [ UTILITY,util-size ] ]

         where:

         util-size
              is ASCII, FIELDATA, and NONE.

         libfile
              is the COBOL library file. This file defaults to SYS$LIB$*ACOB.

         tipfile
              is the ASCII COBOL TIP relocatable library. This file defaults to the file
              SYS$LIB$*ACOBΓÇôTIPLIB.

         cbfile
              is the file containing the CBEP$$ACOB relocatable element banks. This file defaults
              to the libfile..

         The UTILITY option says whether the utility-based common bank, C$DML, contains only
         ASCII (the default) or also FIELDATA routines. This prevents the HVTIP I-banks from
         overlapping with the C$DML library common bank. If you do not want to use the
         C$DML common bank, UTILITY, NONE should be specified.

21.5.10.1.12. TIP

         Format:
            TIP LIB,file

         The LIB file contains the TIP primitives including the RSEGLOAD routine. The default for
         this file is TIP$*TIPLIB$.

21.5.10.1.13. DMS

         Format:
            DMS [ LIB,file ] [ S$WORK,[file],[subschema] ] ;

                   [ SORTBUF ] [ D$WORK,[file],[impart-prog] ]

         The DMS SGS is required if the transactions use DMS 2200. However, all fields can be
         omitted.

         Note: This skeleton is not usable with single-thread DMR.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                              21ΓÇô15
Transaction Processing




        The LIB file contains the DMS 2200 elements to be included in the HVTIP banks
        (COBLNK, LINKER, CLSEG$, SORTBUF). The default is SYS$*RLIB$.

        The S$WORK and D$WORK files are where those elements can be found, and both
        default to the REL file. The parameter subschema is used as a version name to
        S$WORK and, if not specified, any subschema in that file is acceptable. The impartΓÇôprog
        is the COBOL prog-id of the program in the transaction that executes the IMPART
        statement, and defaults to the main program prog-id.

        SORTBUF need only be specified if a set whose mode is pointer array is going to be
        loaded.

21.5.10.1.14. DPS

        Format:
          DPS local-to-id [FILE,file]

        where local-to-id is TO,prog-id or ALL.

        The DPS SGS names the HVTIP banks that are to include the DPS elements
        CBEP$$DPS and ACOB/INTERFACE. FILE names the file that contains these
        relocatables. The default is SYS$LIB$*DPS. If TO,prog-id is specified, only that HVTIP
        Ibank whose entry program is prog-id will include both elements. If ALL is specified, all
        HVTIP Ibanks will include both elements. This SGS assumes that DPS is installed as a
        common bank. LOCAL SGS must be used if DPS is not installed as a common bank.
        Multiple DPS SGSs may be specified, but only one DPS SGS can apply to each HVTIP
        Ibank.

21.5.10.1.15. RDMS

        Format:
          RDMS local-to-id [FILE,file]

        where local-to-id is TO,prog-id or ALL.

        The RDMS SGS names the HVTIP banks that are to include the RDMS elements
        CBEP$$RSA and RDMR-ACOBDAT. FILE names the file that contains these
        relocatables. The default is SYS$LIB$*RSA. If TO,prog-id is specified, only that HVTIP
        Ibank whose entry program is prog-id will include CBEP$$RSA. If ALL is specified, all
        HVTIP Ibanks will include CBEP$$RSA.

        RDMR-ACOBDAT will be included in each HVTIP Dbank. Multiple RDMS SGSs may be
        specified, but only one RDMS SGS can apply to each HVTIP Ibank.




21ΓÇô16                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                         Transaction Processing




21.5.10.1.16. OWN

         Format:
           OWN LIB,file[,file. . . .]

         These LIB files are user files to be searched first, in the order given, during the
         collections.

21.5.10.1.17. DBANKADDRESS

         Format:
           DBANKADDRESS start-address

         The DBANKADDRESS SGS defines the D-bank start address of the HVTIP transaction
         that must be at least 040000 and greater than the maximum address calculated for any I-
         bank called by the transaction using the following formula:
           LASTI$ + (19/18 * size of the RSEG) + 4

         where LASTI$ is the Collector defined variable for the highest I-bank address.

         The default D-bank start address is:
                040000    if the DMS SGS is not specified.
                0150000   if the DMS SGS is specified.

21.5.10.1.18. NOCOMMON

         Format:
           NOCOMMON

         The NOCOMMON SGS indicates that the ICP does not contain a COMMON-STORAGE
         section. If this SGS is not specified, BLANK$COMMON will be included in the ICPΓÇÖs
         collection.

21.5.10.2. Examples of Map SGSs
         Example 1:
           HVTIP    ICP,MAIN
           LOCAL    TO,MAIN COBOL,XYZ COBOL,ABC
           HVTIP    SUBPROGRAM,SUB
           LOCAL    TO,SUB FILE,A*B ASM,SHARED
           LOCAL    TO,SUB COBOL,P3
           REL      MYFILE
           DBANK    IS 512
           COBOL    LIB,SYS$*ACOBLIB$




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                  21ΓÇô17
Transaction Processing




        This example calls for the collection of one ICP and one subprogram bank. The ICP
        contains the main program in element MAIN and subprograms in elements XYZ and
        ABC. The subprogram bank contains the CALL$ entry program in element SUB and local
        subprograms SHARED and P3. All relocatables are in file MYFILE, except for the MASM
        routine SHARED in file A*B. The two absolutes are also generated in file MYFILE.

        The initial transaction D-bank size is 512 words. A relocatable COBOL library is used in
        file SYS$*ACOBLIB$. The TIP library is file TIP$*TIPLIB$. The ASCII COBOL TIP
        relocatable library is SYS$LIB$*ACOBΓÇôTIPLIB. DMS 2200 is not used.

        Example 2:
          HVTIP ICP,B1 STATIC IN,Q1
          HVTIP SUBPROGRAM,B2 IN,Q2
          HVTIP SUBPROGRAM,B3 IN,Q3
          HVTIP SUBPROGRAM,B4 IN,Q4
          MAP    UTILITY
          ABS    MASTER
          IBANKS ARE DYNAMIC
          COBOL TIPVERSION,COBTIP COMMON BANKED
          TIP    LIB,SYS$*RLIB$
          DMS    S$WORK,,SS4

        This example calls for the collection of one ICP and three subprogram banks. Each bank
        contains just one COBOL program. All the relocatables are in the TPF$ file, with
        element Q1 for prog-id B1 (the main program) and elements Q2, Q3, and Q4 for
        subprograms with prog-id B2, B3, and B4, respectively.

        The subprogram banks are dynamic, while the ICP is static with an initial D-bank of 4096
        words. The absolutes are placed in file MASTER, after collecting with the MAP
        processor in file UTILITY.

        A common-banked COBOL library with C$DML is used with the ASCII COBOL TIP library
        in file COBTIP. The DMS 2200 subschema definition is in TPF$.S$WORK/SS4.

21.5.11. Program Example
21.5.11.1. General
        The following is an example of a COBOL HVTIP transaction program and the steps that
        were taken to execute it.

21.5.11.2. COBOL Source Programs
        The transaction program in this example consists of a COBOL main program and two
        COBOL subprograms. The main program uses the CALL identifier and the Message
        Control System (MCS). The data entered in the main program is the name of the
        subroutine to be called. The name is retrieved by executing a RECEIVE statement. Each
        of the subprograms are placed in a bank separate from the one containing the main
        program.




21ΓÇô18                                                                              7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                     Transaction Processing




21.5.11.2.1. Main Program Source

         The source code for the COBOL main program follows:
           IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
           PROGRAM-ID. COBHV1.
           ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
           CONFIGURATION SECTION.
           SOURCE-COMPUTER. UNISYS-1100.
           OBJECT-COMPUTER. UNISYS-1100 MEMORY SIZE IS 3 MODULES.
           DATA DIVISION.
           COMMUNICATION SECTION.
           CD     COMM-INPUT FOR INPUT
                  TEXT LENGTH IS LENGTHI
                  SYMBOLIC SOURCE IS MSG-SOURCE.
           CD     COMM-OUTPUT FOR OUTPUT
                  DESTINATION COUNT IS OP-DEST-CNT
                  TEXT LENGTH IS OP-TXT-L
                  SYMBOLIC DESTINATION IS OP-DEST.
           COMMON-STORAGE SECTION.
           01     COMCOM         PIC         X(80).
           WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
           01     MY-DATA.
                  02 MY-ACT      PIC         X(6).
                  02 FILLER      PIC         X.
                  02 MY-SUB      PIC         X(6).
                  02 FILLER      PIC         X(67).
           01     CALL-DATA.
                  02 CALLID      PIC         X(6).
                  02 FILLER      PIC         X(74).
           01     MPARM1      PIC         H9(10) VALUE 1.
           PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           BEGIN. DISPLAY ΓÇÿBEFORE RECEIVEΓÇÖ LENGTHI MSG-SOURCE UPON PRINTER.
                  RECEIVE COMM-INPUT MESSAGE INTO MY-DATA.
                  DISPLAY ΓÇÿAFTER RECEIVEΓÇÖ LENGTHI MSG-SOURCE UPON PRINTER.
                  DISPLAY MY-DATA UPON PRINTER.
                  MOVE MY-SUB TO CALLID.
                  DISPLAY CALLID UPON PRINTER.
                  DISPLAY ΓÇÿBEFORE CALLΓÇÖ, MPARM1 UPON PRINTER.
                  CALL CALLID USING MPARM1.
                  DISPLAY ΓÇÿAFTER CALLΓÇÖ, MPARM1 UPON PRINTER.
                  MOVE MSG-SOURCE TO OP-DEST.
                  MOVE 80 TO OP-TXT-L.
                  MOVE 1 TO OP-DEST-CNT.
                  DISPLAY OP-DEST-CNT OP-DEST OP-TXT-L UPON PRINTER.
                  SEND COMM-OUTPUT FROM MY-DATA WITH EMI.
                  DISPLAY ΓÇÿMSG SENTΓÇÖ UPON PRINTER.
                  DISPLAY ΓÇÿEND COBHV1ΓÇÖ UPON PRINTER.
                  CANCEL CALLID.
                  STOP RUN.

         The start byte, length, and USAGE of the data item MYΓÇôSUB are key to the retrieval of
         the name of the subprogram to be called (see 21.5.11.6).

              EXIT.

                                                                        Transaction Processing




21.5.11.3. C$S333
         Because the CALL identifier is used (see 18.7.1), element C$S333 is updated as follows:
           @MASM,E             SYS$LIB$*ACOB.C$S333,COBOL*CLIB.
           -40
                               CREATE ΓÇÿCOBHV2ΓÇÖ
                               CREATE ΓÇÿCOBHV3ΓÇÖ
           @EOF

         The file into which the relocatable element is placed must be prepped (@PREP) prior to
         running MAPHVTIP.

21.5.11.4. MNQ Elements
         Since the COBOL main program used in this example passes parameters to each
         subroutine it may call, the element XFR$MNQ is empty. The entry-point-names of the
         subprograms called are COBHV2 and COBHV3. The MNQ elements are created as
         follows:
           @ED,I    MYFILE.XFR$MNQ
           @EOF
           @ED,I    MYFILE.CALL$MNQ
           COBHV2*            $EQU 010002000000
           C$BCOBHV2*         $EQU 0
           COBHV3*            $EQU 010003000000
           C$BCOBHV3*         $EQU O
                              $END
            @EOF

         Both subprograms are placed in library file number 1.

21.5.11.5. SGS Input to MAPHVTIP
         The following SGS was used as input to MAPHVTIP:
           HVTIP               ICP,COBHV1
           HVTIP               SUBPROGRAM,COBHV2
           HVTIP               SUBPROGRAM,COBHV3
           REL                 COBOL*TPF$
           ABS                 COBOL*TPF$
           CONTROL             COBOL*MYFILE
           MAP                 SYS$LIB$*MAP
           IBANKS    ARE       STATIC
           DBANK     IS        4096
           USING               MCS
           LIST                LONG
           COBOL               LIB,COBOL*CLIB TIPVERSION,COBOL*TIPTIP
                               UTILITY,NONE
           TIP                 LIB,TIP$*TIPLIB$

         Given the preceding input, the skeleton MAPHVTIP was instructed to find the relocatable
         elements produced by the COBOL compiler for the main program and subprograms in
         file TPF$. It was also instructed to find the source for the MNQ elements in file MYFILE.



7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                              21ΓÇô21
Transaction Processing




        The updated element C$S333 is in file COBOL*CLIB, and the ASCII COBOL TIP library is
        in file COBOL*TIPTIP. Both CLIB and TIPTIP must be prepped (@PREP) prior to running
        MAPHVTIP.

        For the given SGSs, the skeleton produces three absolute elements: COBHV1,
        COBHV2, and COBHV3, and leaves them in file TPF$.

21.5.11.6. Program Input
        Before you execute the transaction, a VALTAB entry must be created, a TIP library must
        be created, TIP storage must be allocated, and the three absolutes must be copied to
        the library file. See the ASCII COBOL Runtime Technical Reference Manual for more
        information.

        The following data image was entered on a TIP terminal, beginning in column 1:
          COBHV1 COBHV2

        Note: Only one blank space appears between COBHV1 and COBHV2. The cursor was
        positioned on the first blank space following the ΓÇ£2ΓÇ¥ in ΓÇ£COBHV2ΓÇ¥ when this line was
        transmitted.

21.5.11.7. Program Output
        The following output appeared on the printer. Each line of output starts in column 1.

          BEFORE RECEIVE
          AFTER RECEIVE 0014000000000008
          COBHV1 COBHV2
          COBHV2
          BEFORE CALL 0000000001
          IN COBHV2
          LEAVING COBHV2
          AFTER CALL 0000000002
          00010080000000000008
          MSG SENT
          END COBHV1

        The length of the text received (via RECEIVE) (14 characters) includes the blank character
        positioned under the cursor when the input line COBHV1 COBHV2 was transmitted.

Appendix C
Diagnostic Messages


C.1. Compiler Diagnostics
         This section describes the diagnostics produced during compilation. These diagnostics
         appear in the compilation listings in the format illustrated and explained as follows.

         Column:
         Column:

             2      6       10    16        21       28      33         47              100
                                            R
                                            W        LINE   /////
             **     nnnn    **   SEV.       M        COL. cc             ddd     ...    dd
                                            S
                                            F        blanks
                                            L

         where:

         nnnn
             The 4-digit diagnostic number.

         R, W, M, S, F, L
             Severity codes which have the following meanings:

             R (Remark)
                 Explains action taken by compiler but does not indicate an error in the source
                 program.

             W (Warning)
                 Denotes source code that deviates from the specification and may therefore
                 produce unacceptable results. The diagnostic is merely precautionary. Compilation
                 continues and code is generated.
             M (Minor)
                 Indicates an instance of incorrect usage or omission. The compiler makes a
                 reasonable assumption of the userΓÇÖs intent and continues, but further errors may
                 result if compiler assumptions were inappropriate.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                     CΓÇô1
Diagnostic Messages




                S (Serious)
                 Indicates a serious source error for which the compiler is unable to compensate or
                 make a reasonable assumption of the userΓÇÖs intent. Either no code at all or
                 incomplete code is generated for the statement in error.

                F (Fatal)

                 Either a serious source program error or deficiency has been encountered. No
                 code will be generated unless the A option is used on the @ACOB processor call
                 statement.

                L (Leveling)

                 Indicates a source code level violation error. The H, I, L, and R options in the Extra
                 Options field of the @ACOB processor call statement determine the level of
                 Standard COBOL at which leveling checks are performed. (See 18.4.)

        /////
                The number of the source line where the error was detected.

        cc
                The column number of the COBOL syntactical unit in error.

        ddd...dd
                The text of the diagnostic message.

        In general, diagnostic messages are printed immediately after the source line image
        containing the error. Some fatal diagnostics cannot be associated with specific lines or
        columns in the source. In this case, columns 28 through 37 will be blank.

        The following table (based upon diagnostic number ranges) indicates when the
        diagnostic is detected and during which listing the diagnostic will be issued.


        Diagnostic                   Condition Detected                        Diagnostic Issued
         Number

        1-100               While the source program is read.       Throughout the Source listing.
        101-400             While processing the IDENTIFICATION,    During the Source Listing of the
                            ENVIRONMENT, or DATA DIVISIONS          IDENTIFICATION, ENVIRONMENT or
                            (except the REPORT SECTION).            DATA DIVISIONS.
        401-600             While processing the REPORT             During the Source Listing of the
                            SECTION.                                REPORT SECTION.
        601-900             While processing the PROCEDURE          During the Source Listing of the
                            DIVISION                                PROCEDURE DIVISION.
        901-1000            During the code generation phase. Not   After the Source Listing or during the
                            detected or issued if 5 extra option    Object Listing.
                            specified.
        1001-1100           Throughout the compilation.             At any point during the compilation.

Diagnostic Messages




        The following is a list, in numeric order, of the diagnostic message text, its severity, and
        an explanation of the error. Diagnostics that refer to specific COBOL syntactical units fill
        in the units in parentheses for clarification.

        001       F   IDENTIFICATION DIVISION HEADER IS MISSING

              The first word of the source program is not IDENTIFICATION; possibly a misspelled
              control statement was treated as an initial image. Compilation continues as if an
              Identification Division header had been processed.

        002       W PROGRAMΓÇôID HEADER IS MISSING

              The second line of source text does not have the paragraph header PROGRAMΓÇôID.
              Compilation continues as if a paragraph header had been present.

        003       W PERIOD AFTER PREVIOUS LINE IS MISSING

              The line should have a period after the header or at the end of the line. The period is
              assumed present.

        004       W ILLEGAL/UNSEQUENCED PARAGRAPH HEADER IN IDΓÇôDIVISION

              The paragraph header is not allowed or it is out of sequence in the Identification
              Division. Permissible headers are PROGRAMΓÇôID, AUTHOR, INSTALLATION, DATEΓÇô
              WRITTEN, DATEΓÇôCOMPILED, SECURITY, and REMARKS. Processing continues,
              ignoring the inadmissible Identification Division paragraph header.

        005       M       TEXTΓÇôNAME IS NOT FOLLOWED BY (OF, IN, OR REPLACING)

              In a COPY statement, the only allowable words after the text-name are OF, IN or
              REPLACING. If the text-name is qualified by library-name, the only allowable word
              after library-name is REPLACING. When the E option in the Extra Options field is
              used, the only allowable word after text-name is REPLACING. If the word is the first
              word on a source line, it is treated as if it were the beginning of the statement which
              follows the COPY statement. Otherwise, the word and any remaining words on the
              source line are ignored.

        006       S       SUBJECTΓÇôWORD NOT FOLLOWED BY (BY)

              The REPLACING phrase of a COPY statement should contain a sequence of phrases
              in the form subject-word BY object-word. If the word BY is not found after the
              subject-word, the compiler diagnoses the absence and ignores the REPLACING
              phrase of the COPY.




CΓÇô4                                                                                  7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                            Diagnostic Messages




         007       S       LIBRARY HEADER NOT EQUAL TO COPY STATEMENT HEADER

               The first line of the library element in American National Standard 1968 COBOL
               libraries (signified by the E option appearing in the Extra Options field of the
               processor call statement) has a header (procedure-name or level indicator) which
               does not match the header preceding the COPY statement. The library element
               header may be omitted in American National Standard 1968 COBOL libraries (except
               for Procedure Division sections). If headers exist and do not match, the compilation
               will terminate the COPY.

         008       M       ILLEGAL DUPLICATE PARAGRAPH/SECTION NAME

               Either the same section-name has been defined twice in the Procedure Division or
               the same paragraph name has been defined twice within one section. The duplicate
               definition is accepted, but may cause erroneous execution if referenced.

         009       W       DECIMAL POINT SHOULD BE COMMA

               The DECIMALΓÇôPOINT IS COMMA clause appeared in the Environment Division but a
               numeric literal has a period-decimal marker instead of a comma-decimal. The period
               was treated as if a comma had been used.

         010       W       ILLEGAL HYPHEN IN COLUMN 7

               The next line is a comment-entry in the Identification Division or the current line ends
               with a punctuation mark or a literalΓÇôdelimiting quote, followed by a blank. In either
               case the continuation hyphen is unnecessary and therefore ignored. If within a
               COPY proc, the previous line contains a hyphen although the line prior to it ended
               with a separator period. The hyphen is illegal in this case, and is ignored.

         011       M       (ΓÇÖ) MISSING; IT IS ASSUMED TO BE AFTER COL. 72

               The last word on the line is an alphanumeric literal with no ending delimiter, and the
               next line has no continuation hyphen. An ending delimiter quotation mark is
               assumed after column 72.

         012       M       OVERSIZE NAME/LITERAL, THE ITEM WILL BE TRUNCATED

               A user-name over 30 characters or numeric literal over 18 digits or alphanumeric
               literal over 132 characters was found. The word is truncated at the maximum size,
               the balance is treated as a new word.

         013       W       CONTINUATION (ΓÇÖ) MISSING BEFORE FIRST NONΓÇôBLANK ITEM

               A continued alphanumeric literal does not have a quotation mark before the first
               nonblank character. The quotation mark is assumed.

         014       W       LITERAL CONTINUATION (ΓÇÖ) APPEARS BEFORE COL. 12

               The continuation quotation mark for an alphanumeric literal should be in the Area B
               (column 12 or higher). The quotation mark was accepted as is.



7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                      CΓÇô5
Diagnostic Messages




        015       W       WORD SHOULD CONTINUE IN AREA B

              The continuation part of a word should start in the Area B (column 12 or higher). The
              continued word was accepted as is.

        016       S       UNABLE TO FIND TEXTΓÇôNAME, COPY IGNORED

              The text-name cannot be found in the userΓÇÖs Library Index of files, therefore COPY
              cannot be completed.

        017       S       ILLEGAL DATA ITEM IN SOURCE CLAUSE OR USE STATEMENT

              In CONTROL FOOTING, PAGE HEADING, PAGE FOOTING, and REPORT FOOTING
              report groups, SOURCE clauses and USE statements may not reference: (a)group
              data items containing control data items, (b) data items subordinate to a control data
              item, or (c) a redefinition or renaming of any part of a control data item. In PAGE
              HEADING and PAGE FOOTING report groups, SOURCE clauses and USE
              statements must not reference control data-names.

        018       S       SUBSTITUTION TABLE OVERFLOW, REPLACING TERMINATED HERE

              Too many REPLACING items in a COPY statement caused the compiler table to
              overflow. All replacements up to but not including the current one are honored.
              Others are ignored.

        019       M       DUPLICATE (ΓÇÖ) AT BEGINNING OF LITERAL; IGNORED

              It is illegal for an alphanumeric literal to begin with two quotation marks. If an
              imbedded quotation mark is desired as the first character of the literal, the stated
              literal should start with three quotation marks. Extraneous quotation mark is
              ignored.

        020       M       ILLEGAL VERB/USER NAME FOLLOWS PAR/SEC NAME, IGNORED

              The paragraph name or section name is followed by something other than a period
              or the word SECTION. The extraneous word is ignored.

        021       W       BLANK MISSING BEFORE OPERATOR

              Any arithmetic or comparison symbol must be preceded by a blank. The blanks are
              assumed to be present and the symbol is treated as a correct operator or
              punctuation character.

        022       W       BLANK MISSING AFTER ARITHMETIC OR RELATIONAL OPERATOR

              An arithmetic or relational operator must be followed by a blank. A blank is assumed
              present and the symbol is treated as an arithmetic or relational operator.




CΓÇô6                                                                                   7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                            Diagnostic Messages




         023       R       NOTE VERB ALLOWED ONLY IN PROCEDURE DIVISION

               The NOTE statement appears illegally in the Identification, Environment, or Data
               Division. It is processed in the same manner as a legal Procedure Division NOTE
               statement.

         024       S       WORD (COPY) AT THIS POINT IS SYNTACTICALLY INVALID

               It is illegal for library text to contain a COPY statement. The library COPY statement
               is ignored and the original COPY is terminated.

         025       F       PROCEDURE DIVISION HEADER MISSING, COMPILE TERMINATED

               The source program does not contain a valid Procedure Division header. Code
               generation is suppressed unless the @ACOB processor call statement had the A
               option, in which case an unexecutable program will result.

         026       M       HYPHEN AT END OF WORD; IS TREATED AS PART OF NAME

               A user-name must not end with a hyphen. If the hyphen is intended as a minus sign,
               it must be preceded by a blank. The hyphen is accepted as part of the name.

         027       M       ILLEGAL CHARACTER IN WORD; TRUNCATED

               Each character in a user-name must be a letter, a digit, or a hyphen. The remaining
               characters in the name, starting with the illegal one, are truncated.

         028       M       ILLEGAL CHARACTER IN NUMERIC LITERAL; TRUNCATED

               A sequence of digits followed by a letter is treated as a legal user-name. A
               sequence of digits with a decimal point is assumed to be a numeric literal and, if a
               letter or other nondigit appears, it is an illegal character. The numeric literal is
               truncated starting with that character.

         029       W       ILLEGAL (.) (,) (;); TREATED AS PUNCTUATION

               When a period, comma, or semicolon is used as punctuation (not in a PICTURE or a
               literal), it must be followed by a blank. The character is accepted as punctuation and
               compilation continues as if a blank had been present.

         030       W       BLANK MISSING BETWEEN PLUS/MINUS AND A USERΓÇôNAME

               A blank must appear between a plus or minus sign and a user-name. Processing
               continues as if a blank had been present.

         031       R       MORE THAN 99 DIAGNOSTICS FOR THIS LINE

               A maximum of 99 diagnostic messages can be printed for one source image.
               Excessive diagnostics are suppressed.




7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                     CΓÇô7
Diagnostic Messages




        032       W       ILLEGAL WORD IN AREA A; WORD ACCEPTED

              This word is not an allowable section, paragraph, or entry header and therefore
              should not start in Area A (between columns 8 and 11). The word is accepted and
              processed as if it were properly positioned.

        033       R       ATTEMPT RECOVERY HERE AFTER ERRONEOUS SOURCE SKIPPED

              After the syntax error in an earlier image or column, the compiler is attempting to
              resume normal syntax analysis at this point.

        034       M       THIS USER NAME IS INADEQUATELY QUALIFIED

              This user-name is duplicated and therefore requires qualification when referenced.
              The first declaration of the name is used if: (1) the user-name had no qualifiers at all;
              or (2) the user-name is improperly qualified but has no duplicates. If the user-name
              is inadequately qualified and has duplicates then the second declaration is used.

        035       M       LAST IDENTIFIER IN THIS LINE INADEQUATELY QUALIFIED

              The same as 034 except that user name and its qualifiers are on separate source
              images and therefore require that the message be worded differently to identify the
              source of error.

        036       M       THIS QUALIFIER INAPPROPRIATE FOR USER NAME

              There is no declaration of this user-name which fits the existing set of qualifiers. The
              first declaration of this user-name is used if it had no duplicates; otherwise the last
              declaration is used.

        037       M       QUALIFIERS INAPPROPRIATE FOR LAST NAME IN THIS LINE

              For the last identifier on the indicated line, there is no declaration of the first user-
              name which fits the existing set of qualifiers. The first declaration of this user-name
              is used if it had no duplicates; otherwise the last declaration is used.

        038       M       EXTRANEOUS OR UNRECOGNIZABLE TOKEN(S) IN LINE: IGNORED

              Tokens not belonging to the text are deleted.

        039       W       BLANK MUST PRECEDE STARTING QUOTE

              A blank must precede a starting quotation mark.

        040       M       ITEM SIZE GREATER THAN 262K; MAXIMUM USED

              A data item, elementary or group, must not contain more than 262,140 characters or
              65,535 words; 262,140 characters are allocated.




CΓÇô8                                                                                    7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                                               Diagnostic Messages




         041       M        ILLEGAL CHARACTER IN PICTURE; ILLEGAL ONES IGNORED

               The PICTURE contains an illegal character; only the following are allowed:
                   0, 1, 9, A, B, C, D, P, R, S, V, X, Z, +, -, /, currency sign, comma, decimal point,
                   and parenthesized integers.
               The illegal character or characters are ignored and the rest of the PICTURE is
               processed as if illegal characters had not been present.

         042       M        ILLEGAL ORDER OF CHARACTERS; CONFLICTING ONES IGNORED

               The PICTURE contains a pair of characters which either must not appear in the same
               PICTURE or must not appear in the stated order. Cases of the first type are: S with
               an editing character; 1 with anything but S or 1; S, V, or P with A or X; two decimal
               markers (V or . ); two different floating characters (Z, *, pair of +ΓÇÖs, $ΓÇÖs). Cases of the
               second type are: + or ΓÇô after $; floating symbol after 9; S in any but the highΓÇôorder
               position; C not followed by R; D not followed by B; PΓÇÖs not high or low order. Any
               PICTURE character which conflicts with an earlier character is ignored. Any
               PICTURE string is processed as if conflicting characters had not been present.

         043       M        ILLEGAL REPEAT COUNT; ILLEGAL CHARACTER IGNORED

               The repeat count following a left parenthesis either has a nondigit in it, or has more
               than five digits, or the PICTURE ends before the right parenthesis occurs. PICTURE
               is processed as if illegal characters were not present.

         044       M        ILLEGAL CHARACTER WITH FLOAT/SUPPRESSION SYMBOL; IGNORE

               It is illegal to have both a floating insertion or zero suppression symbol (+, ΓÇô, $, *, or
               Z) and a 9 to the right of the decimal point in an edited PICTURE string. The string is
               processed as if floating insertion or zero suppression were specified for the entire
               item.

         045       W        (X) IN NUMERIC EDIT PICTURE; X TREATED AS 9

               An item is numeric edited if BLANK WHEN ZERO is present or if its PICTURE
               contains any of the following characters:
                   0, /, B, C, R, D, B, Z, *, +, -, $, comma, decimal point
               Any X in the PICTURE is treated as a 9.

         046       M        NUMERIC EDITING MAXIMUM SIZE 31; EXCESS TRUNCATED

               A numeric-edited item must not be larger than 31 characters. The excess characters
               in the PICTURE are truncated on the right.

         047       M        ALPHANUMERIC EDITING MAXIMUM SIZE 255; TRUNCATED

               An item is alphanumeric edited if its PICTURE contains at least one A or X, and at
               least one editing character B or O, and no other numeric editing characters. An
               alphanumeric edited item must not be larger than 255 characters. The excess
               characters in the PICTURE are truncated on the right.


7830 7709ΓÇô002                                                                                         CΓÇô9
Diagnostic Messages




        048       M        EXACT BINARY MAXIMUM 72 BITS; EXCESS TRUNCATED

              An item is exact-binary if its PICTURE contains all 1ΓÇÖs with an optional S. An
              unsigned exactΓÇôbinary item must not be larger than 71 bits or, if signed, it must not
              be larger than 72 bits. The excess bits are truncated on the right if the size is greater
              than 72 bits.

        049       M        MAXIMUM DECIMAL SIZE 18 DIGITS; EXCESS TRUNCATED

              An item is numeric if its PICTURE contains only the following characters:
                  1, 9, S, V, P
              If a numeric PICTURE contains 9ΓÇÖs, it must not contain more than 18 of them. The
              excess is truncated on the right.

        050       M        ILLEGAL POINT LOCATION CLAUSE; CLAUSE IGNORED

              The POINT LOCATION clause can be stated only for an item with an exactΓÇôbinary
              PICTURE (all 1ΓÇÖs with a possible S). In all other cases, the POINT LOCATION clause
              is ignored.

        051       M        ILLEGAL JUSTIFIED (RIGHT) CLAUSE; CLAUSE IGNORED

              The JUSTIFIED (RIGHT) clause can be stated only for an alphanumeric or
              alphanumeric edited item. In all other cases it is ignored.

        052       M        ILLEGAL BLANK WHEN ZERO CLAUSE; CLAUSE IGNORED

              The BLANK WHEN ZERO clause can be stated only with a numeric (other than
              exactΓÇôbinary) or numeric edited PICTURE. In all other cases, it is ignored.

        053       M        ILLEGAL CHARACTER IN CURRENCY LITERAL

              The literal in the CURRENCY SIGN clause must not match any of the allowable
              PICTURE characters or punctuation characters: A, B, C, D, L, P, R, S, V, X, Z, +, ΓÇô, *,
              /, comma, decimal point, left parenthesis, right parenthesis, semicolon, space, and
              the digits 0 through 9. The illegal currency sign will not be recognized as a currency
              sign but as a regular character in the picture. The currency sign ($) will be accepted
              (in other words, CURRENCY SIGN clause is ignored).

        054       W        MORE THAN 18 NUMERIC CHARACTERS; TREAT AS ALPHANUMERIC

              A PICTURE containing only 9ΓÇÖs, and more than 18 of them, is treated as if it

              two criteria:
              1. All its elementary items, other than exact-binary, are 9-bit usage (DISPLAY or
                 COMPUTATIONAL) and any exact binary items occupy integral 9-bit bytes, either
                 individually or in groups of consecutive items.

                 COMPUTATIONALΓÇô4) and any exact-binary items occupy integral 6-bit bytes,
                 either individually or in groups of consecutive items.

              padding in the compressed record on external media depends dynamically on the

        787       S       SENTENCE OR STATEMENT TOO LARGE; STATEMENT OMITTED

              An internal compiler table overflowed at this point, and the entire sentence or
              statement is omitted. For a conditional sentence, the solution is to break the
              compared conditions (ANDs and ORs) or the nested conditions (IF ... IF ... ELSE)
              into two or more smaller conditional sentences. For an imperative statement, the
              overflow is caused by multiple operands (MOVE A TO B, C, D ...); the solution is to
              break the statement into two or more statements with fewer operands.
              This error can sometimes occur after DEBUGGING, MONITOR, or subscript range
              checks have been added to a program. This is because additional entries are created
              for an internal table to handle these features. As a result of these additional entries,
              the table can overflow on statements that normally compile without these features.

         947       F       PARAMETER WORD TABLE OVERFLOW IN INSPECT/UNSTRING

               The complexity of the INSPECT or UNSTRING statement caused an internal compiler
               table to overflow. Code generation for this statement is incomplete or incorrect and
               may cause an illegal operation halt. Reduce the complexity of the INSPECT or
               UNSTRING statement to correct the error.

         948       F       PARAMETER WORD TABLE OVERFLOW IN STRING/DISPLAY

               An internal compiler parameter word table overflows while generating code for an
               extremely complex STRING statement (for example, a STRING statement that
               contains a large number of DELIMITED identifiers) or for a DISPLAY statement that
               specifies a large number of operands where at least one of the operands contains an
               OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause. Code generated for this statement is incomplete
               or incorrect and may cause an illegal operation interrupt (IOPR) if executed. To
               correct this error, reduce the complexity of the STRING or DISPLAY statement.

         949       S       MOVE OF NONΓÇôNUMERIC TO NUMERIC GIVES UNDEFINED RESULTS

               A move of a figurative constant (other than ZERO, ZEROS, or ZEROES) to a numeric
               field may have unpredictable results. The move will be generated.

         950       F       REGISTER OVERFLOW; ALL PROTECTED, NONE AVAILABLE

C.2. Compiler Errors
        This section describes the Compiler Errors that cause termination of compilation. These
        diagnostics appear in the source program listing in the format illustrated and explained as
        follows.

        Format:
          Column

          2            6                                         21       25

          ***       COMPILER ERROR    nnn    ***

        where nnn is the 3-digit diagnostic number.

        The following is a list, ordered by phase, of the diagnostic number along with its
        meaning.

        Phase 0

              400      OPENO called with invalid file-id
              403      WRFILE called for a file not open for output
              404      WRFILE called with an invalid record length
              405      CLOSEO called with invalid file-id
              406      OPENI called with invalid file-id
              407      RDFILE called for a file not open for input
              408      CLOSEI called with an invalid file-id
              409      DIAGER called with an unassigned diagnostic number
              500      Diagnostic message contains an invalid severity designator
              501      The length of a diagnostic message is not 56 characters
              502      Illegal attempt to expand NAMTAB
              503      Illegal attempt to expand PROTAB
              504      Illegal attempt to expand CONTAB
              505      Illegal attempt to expand DESTAB

        GNT, Picture Processor, Phase 2

              421      Zero action (in other words, undefined code routine)
              422      Stack over/underflow

        Phase 3

              431      Word count in CONTAB = 0




CΓÇô104                                                                               7830 7709ΓÇô002
                                                              Diagnostic Messages




         Phase 4

             441     All Phase 4 error conditions

         If any of these errors occur, please submit a UCF.

C.3. Execution Diagnostics
        This section describes the diagnostics produced during program execution. These
        diagnostics are output on the program print file (printer or terminal for batch or demand
        mode execution, respectively) and therefore may be interspersed with program
        generated writes and displays.

        The format of this message is:
        Column:

        1            6       8
                     W
        nnnn         A       ddd . . . dd   fff . . . ff
                     blank

        where:

        nnnn
             is the 4-character diagnostic number.

        W and A
             are severity codes.

        W (Warning)
             Indicates that an error has occurred that probably affects execution correctness, but
             the execution is continued.

        A (Abort)
             Indicates an error which is severe enough that further execution is not possible. The
             main program, subprograms, and any active ACS cycles are terminated.

        blank
             Severity is used for several ACS diagnostics for which neither of the above suffice.

        ddd ... dd
             is the text of the message which may be followed by fff ... ff

        fff ... ff
             is the name or contents of the item or file to which the diagnostic text refers.

         The following is a list, in numeric order, of the message number, text, and explanation of
         execution diagnostics.

         0000ΓÇô1100       Not issued.

         1101        A    ATTEMPTED TO OPEN FILE WHICH IS ALREADY OPEN

             A program logic error results in attempting to open a file twice without an
             intervening close.

         1102        A    INVALID EQUIPMENT ASSIGNED TO FILE

             The program-assigned device does not correspond to the run stream @ASG
             statement assignment.

         1103        A    NO EQUIPMENT ASSIGNED TO FILE

             A file which was not selected as OPTIONAL has no associated @ASG statement in
             the run stream.

         1104        A    NO DATA AVAILABLE ON ACCEPT

             The OS 2200 Executive symbiont which supports the device from which an ACCEPT
             is expected has no data available.

         1105        A    ATTEMPTED TO WRITE ON UNOPENED FILE

             A program logic error results in a WRITE statement referencing a file which is
             currently closed.

         1106        A    ATTEMPTED TO OPEN FILE PREVIOUSLY CLOSED WITH LOCK

             A program logic error results in an attempt to open a file which, because of a CLOSE
             WITH LOCK statement, can no longer be accessed by this run unit.

         1107        A    ATTEMPTED TO REWRITE RECORD LONGER THAN ORIGINAL

             A record which is rewritten must be equal to or shorter than the record it replaces.

         1108        A    ATTEMPTED TO READ PAST MAXIMUM FASTRAND ASSIGNMENT

             The @ASG statement for this file did not specify sufficient space for the data.
             Revise allocation upward.

         1109        W    CLOSE REEL SPECIFIED, NO REELS LEFT

             Either no data was processed since the last CLOSE REEL, the entire file has already
             been closed, or no OPEN statement has been executed.

        1110       A     ATTEMPTED TO WRITE ON FILE OPENED FOR INPUT

                        ON READ

           The system was unable to read from the specified file. This resulted in octal I/O
           error status code xx being returned. See the Exec System Software Executive
           Requests Programming Reference Manual for a description of the error.

        1113       A     A WRITEΓÇôONLY FILE OPENED FOR INPUT

           A file with an @ASG statement defining it as write-only has been opened for input.
           This indicates that either a program logic error or an incorrect job stream was set up.

        1114       A     A READΓÇôONLY FILE OPENED FOR OUTPUT

           A file with an @ASG statement defining it as read-only has been opened for output.
           This indicates that either a program logic error or an incorrect job stream was set up.

        1115       A     PREMATURE END OF FILE REACHED ON MULTIFILE TAPE

           A file on a multifile tape is not present at the position expected. For example, file
           four is requested but file three is followed by two tape marks. Either the specified
           tape is incorrect or malformed, or the position of the file in question was incorrectly
           stated in the COBOL program.

        1116       A     ATTEMPTED TO READ AN UNOPENED FILE

           A program logic error resulted in a READ statement referencing a file which is
           currently closed.

        1117       W     ENDING LABEL NOT FOUND

           A malformed tape does not contain an expected EOF label.

        1118       W     FILEΓÇôLIMITS ARE NOT IN SEQUENCE, IGNORED

           The FILEΓÇôLIMITS clause does not specify values in ascending order. All file-limit
           values starting with the first value out of order are ignored.

         1119       A    CLOSE UNIT INVALID

            The CLOSE UNIT statement applies only to files assigned to mass storage. The
            CLOSE statement is ignored.

         1120       A    READΓÇôONLY/WRITEΓÇôONLY FILE IS OPENED FOR IΓÇôO

            A file whose @ASG statement specified read-only or write-only is opened for IΓÇôO
            which could violate the assignment.

         1121       A    ABNORMAL RETURN FROM AREAD$/AREADA$

            An abnormal return from the system routine, AREAD$ or AREADA$, was caused by
            an attempt to read a control card as data. That is, expected data in the run stream
            was not present. See the OS 2200 Exec System Software Executive Requests
            Programming Reference Manual (7830 7899) for an explanation of the error code
            printed with this message.

         1122       A    READ REVERSE ILLEGAL ON ASSIGNED TAPE UNIT

            A file which is opened reversed must be assigned to a tape device which is capable
            of reading backwards. Reassign the file and rerun to correct the error.

         1123       A    INVALID KEY CONDITION WITH NO CLAUSE STATED

            A program logic error resulted in an INVALID KEY condition being detected with no
            invalid key action being specified. For example, a WRITE statement does not
            contain a KEY clause yet causes a record to be placed outside of file limits.

         1124       A    ATTEMPTED TO OPEN MORE THAN 1 FILE ON MULTIFILE TAPE

            When several files exist on the same tape, only one may be open at any point in
            time.

         1125       W    FILE IS ALREADY CLOSED

            A program logic error results in a file being closed before it is opened. The CLOSE
            statement is ignored.

         1126       A    TOO MANY INDEX LEVELS FOR FILE

            This error occurs when a program creates small logical records with very large keys,
            thus causing the index blocks to fill up very rapidly and new index blocks to be
            created. The error is corrected by using smaller keys and larger logical records. The
            maximum number of index blocks per file is 100.

         1127       A    START INVALID WHEN ACCESS IS RANDOM

            The START statement can be executed only for ACCESS IS SEQUENTIAL input or
            IΓÇôO files. A source program correction is required.

        1128       W    REEL NO. IN VOL1 LABEL DOES NOT MATCH REEL ON ASG

           The tape reel number in the VOL1 label does not match the reel number on the fileΓÇÖs
           @ASG statement. This may mean an out-of-order reel in a multireel file, a
           malformed label, a mismounted tape, or an @ASG statement error. The tape is
           processed as if the error had not occurred.

        1129       A    FILE DESCRIPTION OR FILE NOT STATED IN USING CLAUSE

           A program logic or source error causes this file to be currently unassigned. Probable
           causes in the COBOL program are a missing FD entry, serious errors in the FD or
           SELECT statements for the file, or accessing the file in a USE FOR RANDOM
           PROCESSING section which does not name the file in its USING clause. Correct the
           source error and recompile to correct the error.

        1130       W    STANDARD LABEL VALUE & LABEL DISAGREE/NOT COMPARED

           The user specified VALUE OF value does not agree with the actual value in a
           standard label or the user specified VALUE OF value is not compared to the label
           because the file originator is not COBOL.

        1131       A    ATTEMPTED TO READ BEYOND END OF FILE

           A READ statement has been executed after an AT END condition has been
           detected. This is probably a program logic error.

        1132       A    ATTEMPTED TO READ A FILE OPENED FOR OUTPUT

           A program logic error resulted in executing READ statement referencing a file which
           is currently open for output.

        1133       A    UNRECOGNIZABLE LABEL

           A label contains something other than HDR1, HDR2, VOL1, UHL, UVL, UTL, EOF in
           the initial character positions of the label. The malformed label was possibly caused
           by a program error during creation, or during hardware or system failure.

        1134       W    LABEL VALUE DOES NOT AGREE WITH USER LABEL

           The user specified VALUE OF value does not agree with the actual value in a user
           label.

        1135       A    FILE NOT ASSIGNED TO MAGNETIC TAPE

           A file selected and assigned to UNISERVO has been assigned via the @ASG
           statement to a nontape device.

        1136       W    BEGINNING LABEL NOT FOUND

           A file being processed is missing a HDR1 label. File processing is continued as if the
           label had been found. The error indicates incorrect processing when the file was
           created.

         1137       A     ATTEMPTED TO OPEN A PRINT/PUNCH FILE AS INPUT OR IΓÇôO

            A program error results in attempting to open an output-only device file for input.
            This message is usually caused by a misspelled file-name or improper assignment of

         1138       A     ATTEMPTED TO OPEN A CARDΓÇôREADER FILE AS OUTPUT OR IΓÇôO

            A program error results in attempting to open an input-only device file for output.
            This is frequently caused by a misspelled file-name or improper assignment of a file.

         1139       A     ITEM SIZE IN LABEL DOES NOT MATCH RECORD DESCRIPTION

            A VALUE OF item in a label (standard or user) does not agree with the size of the
            item in the label record description.

         1140       W     BLOCK COUNT DOES NOT MATCH END LABEL

            The actual number of data blocks on a file does not agree with the block count value
            contained in the EOF label created when the file was written. Program error or
            hardware or system failure could cause this apparent malformed file or label.

                          TAPEΓÇôCHECKPOINT NOT TAKEN

            The checkpoint dump file, specified in the RERUN clause, must be appropriately
            assigned. If a file-name was specified, that fileΓÇÖs external-name must appear on an
            @ASG statement. If UNISERVO or MASSΓÇôSTORAGE was specified, the file-name
            RERUN$ must be the subject of an @ASG statement for the appropriate class of
            devices.

         1142       W     CHECKPOINT ERROR CODE (xxxxx) RETURNED FOR FILE

            Checkpoint/Restart encountered an error while attempting a checkpoint. The
            checkpoint is ignored and processing will continue. The checkpoint error code xxxxx

         1144       W     CHECKPOINT DUMP NOT ALLOWED ON FILES OPENED FOR INPUT

            The file-name specified in the RERUN clause must be opened for output prior to the

        1145       W     INVALID CREATION/PURGE DATE ΓÇô DATE IGNORED

           The value specified as VALUE OF CREATIONΓÇôDATE or PURGEΓÇôDATE must be valid
           dates of the form MMDDYY. If the date value is not equal to six characters or if the
           digits do not correspond to valid dates, todayΓÇÖs date is used for both values.

                        EXTERNAL BLOCK LENGTH ON THIS TAPE

           The BLOCK CONTAINS clause value for an input tape file does not represent the

           CONTAINS specification, a LABEL RECORDS OMITTED clause was specified for a
           labeled tape, or an illegal block was generated causing the number of words
           received and the number of words specified in the block control word to differ.

        1183       W    C$INFO FOUND FILE NOT OPEN OR NOT MSAM FILE

           The routine C$INFO found that the file was not open, or the file is not a MSAM file.
           The user area has been zero filled before return of control.

        1184       W    C$INFO FOUND PARAMETER LIST IN ERROR

           The routine C$INFO found that the parameter list was in error. The user area has
           not been altered before return of control.

        1185       A    ACCEPT IMAGE > SIZE OF A SINGLE DATA TRANSFER

           Buffer space is allocated to accommodate the maximum size of a single data
           transfer. If this area overflows it will overlay whatever follows. See 2.6.4.4 for
           general rules for the ACCEPT statement to determine maximum data transfer sizes.

        1186       A    INAPPROPRIATE IBM HARDWARE TRANSLATE SPECIFIED

           For IBM tape hardware translate, the RECORDING MODE must be F AN or U AN
           and the @ASG statement must specify ASCII for PROCESSOR code, EBCDIC for
           TAPE code, and Q for data transfer FORMAT.

        1187       W    MAXIMUM NO. OF BUFFERS EXCEEDED, MAXIMUM USED

           The user has created a Define File Block for an Indexed IΓÇôO file and has specified a
           value for bn (the number of buffers) which is too large. The maximum number of
           buffers (63) is used.

        1188       W    TOO FEW BUFFERS SPECIFIED, MINIMUM USED

           The user has created a Define File Block for an Indexed IΓÇôO file and has specified a
           value for bn (the number of buffers) which is too small. The minimum number of
           buffers (4) is used.

        1189       W    OVER 65K MODE IS REQUIRED FOR HVTIP SUBPROGRAM

           COBOL requires that HVTIP subprograms be compiled with the OBJECTΓÇô
           COMPUTER paragraph containing the clause ΓÇ£MEMORY SIZE 3 MODULESΓÇ¥ in
           order to allow D-bank addresses to become X-register based.

        1190       A    THIS SUBPROGRAMΓÇÖS DΓÇôAREA IS MISSING:

           COBOLΓÇÖs D-bank parameter address is too small. This can occur if the subprogramΓÇÖs
           D-bank element is not included (for example, IN RO$$$$SYSDTA) in the programΓÇÖs

        1191       W    WRONG NUMBER OF USING OPERANDS FOR SUBPROGRAM

            (one that resides in the same HVTIP bank as the calling program). The subprogram
            xxx will not be marked as canceled, in other words, the CANCEL will be ignored.

           values:

                    @       C$S240 unknown message terminator

                    O       Cannot free queue file

         1205        W    ZERO PARAMETERS REQUIRED FOR XFR$ CALLED SUBPROGRAM: xxx

            PROGRAM or CALL statement. The error occurs either while attempting to return

            which results in the program exceeding the maximum number of nested CALL$ΓÇÖs.

         1207        W    CANCELED SUBPROGRAM NOT RESIDENT ΓÇô IGNORE CANCEL: xxx

            Any subprogram being canceled must reside in memory before the execution of the
            CANCEL statement. Since the subprogram xxx was not resident in memory, the

         1208   A    BLOCK TRUNCATED WHILE WRITING TO TAPE FOR FILE

            The Exec indicated that a block being written to tape did not transfer all of the data
            requested. This situation probably occurred as a result of the file being assigned
            with quarter-word mode (Q-mode) enabled and a record containing data with a stop
            bit set (e.g., binary or Fieldata characters). The program is aborted as the file being
            written will contain corrupted information and probably will be unreadable. To avoid
            this problem assign the file without Q-mode.
